changelog.body:
# @gridkitjs/core

## 0.14.0

### Minor Changes

- 2ac1c45: Count messages such as `filterResults`, `filterSearchFirst`, `copied` and `selectedCount` now format numbers with the grid's `locale` — "1,204 of 10,000 rows" under `en`, "1.204 of 10.000 rows" under `de-DE` — and in the runtime's locale when none is given, where they printed bare digits ("1204 of 10000 rows"). Overrides keep their signatures and still receive plain numbers.

  `resolveMessages` takes the locale as an optional second argument, `resolveMessages(messages, locale)`, and the new `createDefaultMessages(locale)` returns the English defaults for a locale; `defaultMessages` is the one for the runtime's locale.

- 6a4c6c2: `GridMessages` has two new keys, `firstPage` ("First") and `lastPage` ("Last"), naming the pager's buttons to the first and last page. A partial `messages` override keeps working unchanged; a complete `GridMessages` object written out in full needs the two keys added.
- 6a4c6c2: `paginationWindow` now returns the same number of entries for every page once `pageCount` exceeds `2 * boundaryCount + 2 * siblingCount + 3` (7 with the defaults), so a numbered pager no longer grows and shrinks as the user pages through. Near either end the run of sibling pages slides inwards instead of being cut short: page 1 of 10 gives `[1, 2, 3, 4, 5, "ellipsis", 10]` where it gave `[1, 2, "ellipsis", 10]`, and page 10 of 10 gives `[1, "ellipsis", 6, 7, 8, 9, 10]` where it gave `[1, "ellipsis", 9, 10]`. Middle pages and page counts small enough to show every page are unchanged.

## 0.13.0

### Minor Changes

- 7fc1b14: Columns take two new props for exporting. `exportable: false` keeps a column
  — one of action buttons, say — out of every export, clipboard copy and print.
  `exportValue(value, row)` returns the typed value an export stores for a cell
  (a new `ExportScalar`: `string | number | boolean | Date | null`) where the raw
  value is not the one to keep; the text every format writes still comes from
  `formatCellValue`.
- 7fc1b14: `buildExportTable(source, options?)` turns the grid's view into an
  `ExportTable` — columns, every row as cells carrying both the formatted text
  and a typed value, group header and summary rows, and the grand total — the
  one model every export format, the clipboard and print are written from. It
  reads the view and state, never the page, so rows on another page or inside a
  collapsed group still export. By default it holds every filtered and sorted
  row, every group expanded, and the visible columns less any with
  `exportable: false`; `ExportOptions` narrows it with `scope`, `columns`,
  `includeGroups`, `includeAggregates` and `includeHeader`. A command passes its
  `GridCommandContext` as the source as it is.
- ebac1dd: `copyContent(source, request)` builds what the clipboard carries from the
  export model: tab-separated text (no byte order mark, no formula guard) and an
  HTML table. `request` is a cell (`{ kind: "cell", rowId, columnId }`), a row
  (`{ kind: "row", rowId }`) or the selection (`{ kind: "selection" }` — the
  selected rows, else the selected columns, else the selected cell). Hidden and
  `exportable: false` columns never copy, and a row the filter hides gives
  `null`. Three new built-in commands use it: `copy.cell`, `copy.row` and
  `copy.selection`, labelled by the new `messages` keys `copyCell`, `copyRow`
  and `copySelection`, with the `copy` icon key. The default cell context menu
  now starts with the three, then a separator. Two more keys, `copied(count,
unit)` and `copyFailed`, are for a renderer's announcement.
- 7fc1b14: `toCsv(table, options?)` and `toTsv(table, options?)` write an `ExportTable`
  as text. CSV is quoted per RFC 4180 and by default starts with a UTF-8 byte
  order mark, ends records with CRLF, writes each cell as the grid shows it, and
  prefixes a field a spreadsheet would run as a formula (`=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, a
  leading tab or carriage return) with `'` — a numeric cell keeps its sign.
  `delimiter: "auto"` with a `locale` writes `;` where a decimal is written with
  a comma, and `values: "raw"` writes typed values plainly instead. TSV, the
  clipboard's plain-text form, is tab-separated with LF line ends, no byte order
  mark and no formula guard. Both return a string; making a `Blob` is the
  renderer's job.
- 812d0b6: Exporting is a set of built-in commands. `export.csv` and `export.json` save
  the grid's view through `host.saveFile`, under the grid's `export` defaults;
  `export.xlsx` and `export.pdf` do the same and show only once a writer for
  their format is registered through `exportWriters`. `exportSelection.csv`,
  `exportSelection.json` and `exportSelection.xlsx` save the selected rows, and
  show only while rows are selected. Each shows on the grid, toolbar, body and
  cell targets, and is disabled while there is nothing to export. Their labels
  are new `messages` keys: `exportCsv`, `exportJson`, `exportXlsx`, `exportPdf`,
  `exportSelectionCsv`, `exportSelectionJson` and `exportSelectionXlsx`.

  A toolbar takes a new entry, `"export"`: a dropdown, labelled
  `messages.exportMenu` ("Export"), of the export commands that show — left out
  when none do. It is not among the default toolbar's entries; list it to add
  it:

  ```ts
  toolbar={{ items: ["search", "spacer", "export"] }}
  ```

- 812d0b6: A new `messages` key, `exportFailed` ("Export failed"), is what a renderer
  announces when an export's writer fails and no file is saved.
- 812d0b6: Export formats are pluggable. An `ExportWriter` — `{ format, fileExtension,
mimeType, write(table, context) }`, `write` returning text, bytes or a promise
  of either — turns an `ExportTable` into a file's contents; `csvWriter` and
  `jsonWriter` ship built in. `exportFile(source, format, options, writers)`
  builds the table, runs the format's writer and names the file, returning an
  `ExportFile` (`{ fileName, mimeType, content }`), a promise of one for an
  asynchronous writer, or `null` for a format with no writer.

  Two new grid options go with it: `export`, a `GridExportOptions` holding the
  grid's export defaults (every `ExportOptions` field, `fileName` — `"export"`
  by default, the extension added — and `csv` / `json` settings), and
  `exportWriters`, which registers further formats by `format` and replaces a
  built-in writer of the same one. `resolveExportWriters(exportWriters)` gives
  every writer a grid has, by format.

- 7fc1b14: `formatGroupValue(value, column, locale, messages)` is exported from
  `@gridkitjs/core`: the text a group's own value reads as, as the grouped
  column's cells read it, with a missing value reading
  `messages.blankGroupValue`. The React grid's group headers now use it, so a
  header and an export name a group the same way; nothing changes on screen.
- 0119cd3: **Breaking for a hand-built command host.** `GridCommandHost` has a new
  required member, `print(document, options)`, which puts a `PrintDocument` on
  paper — the `print` command hands it the document it built and the
  `PrintOptions` it built it under. A host you build yourself, for a renderer of
  your own or a test, has to add it; one that cannot print passes a member that
  does nothing:

  ```ts
  // before
  const host = {
    autoFitColumns() {},
    openPanel() {},
    announce() {},
    saveFile() {},
    writeClipboard() {},
  };

  // after
  const host = {
    autoFitColumns() {},
    openPanel() {},
    announce() {},
    saveFile() {},
    writeClipboard() {},
    print() {},
  };
  ```

- 812d0b6: **Breaking for a hand-built command host.** `GridCommandHost` has a new
  required member, `saveFile(file)`, which saves an `ExportFile` (or a promise of
  one) — the export commands hand it the file they write. A host you build
  yourself, for a renderer of your own or a test, has to add it; one with no
  file to save to passes a member that does nothing:

  ```ts
  // before
  const host = { autoFitColumns() {}, openPanel() {}, announce() {} };

  // after
  const host = {
    autoFitColumns() {},
    openPanel() {},
    announce() {},
    saveFile() {},
  };
  ```

- ebac1dd: **Breaking for a hand-built command host.** `GridCommandHost` has a new
  required member, `writeClipboard(content)`, which puts a `CopyContent` on the
  clipboard and announces it — the copy commands hand it what they copy. A host
  you build yourself, for a renderer of your own or a test, has to add it; one
  with no clipboard passes a member that does nothing:

  ```ts
  // before
  const host = {
    autoFitColumns() {},
    openPanel() {},
    announce() {},
    saveFile() {},
  };

  // after
  const host = {
    autoFitColumns() {},
    openPanel() {},
    announce() {},
    saveFile() {},
    writeClipboard() {},
  };
  ```

- 7fc1b14: `toHtmlTable(table, options?)` writes an `ExportTable` as an HTML `<table>`
  string — column names in `<thead>`, rows in `<tbody>`, the grand total in
  `<tfoot>`, every text escaped. It carries the class names
  `gridkit-export-table`, `export-group` (with `data-level`) and
  `export-group-summary`, and each column's alignment inline so it survives a
  paste into a spreadsheet or document. `caption` adds a `<caption>`.
- 7fc1b14: `toJson(table, options?)` writes an `ExportTable`'s data rows as a JSON array
  of objects, one property per column holding the cell's typed value — dates as
  ISO 8601 strings. Group, summary and total rows are left out. Properties are
  named by column id, or by header text under `keys: "header"`, where a
  repeated header is suffixed ` (2)`; `space` indents the output.
- 0119cd3: A built-in `print` command prints the grid's view — every row an export would
  hold, across pages and collapsed groups — under a new `print` grid option, a
  `PrintOptions`. It shows on the grid, the toolbar, the body and a cell, is
  labelled by the new `print` message ("Print") with the new `print` icon key,
  and hands the host the document `exportPrintDocument(source, options)` builds:
  `buildPrintDocument` over the grid's own view, its timestamp in the grid's
  locale and, given no `title`, titled with the grid's `label`. `print` is no
  longer a reserved command id.
- 0119cd3: `buildPrintDocument(table, options?)` lays an `ExportTable` out as a printable
  document: a heading of the `title`, `subtitle` and `timestamp` set in a new
  `PrintOptions`, the table as `toHtmlTable` writes it, and a `footer` line,
  every piece of text escaped. It returns a `PrintDocument` — the document's
  `title`, its `bodyHtml`, and the `page` it is laid out on with every default
  settled: `paperSize` (`"A4"`), `orientation` (landscape for a table of more
  than six columns, else portrait), `pageNumbers` (on) and `fitToWidth` (off).
  It holds no styles; a renderer prints it.
- 610d28a: `GridMessages` gains the filter checklist's strings: `filterSearchLabel`
  ("Search values"), the accessible name of its search box; `filterSelectAll`
  ("Select all"), the checkbox over every value the search shows;
  `filterValuesLabel` ("Values"), the accessible name of its list; and
  `filterByCondition` ("Filtered by condition"), shown above it while the
  column is filtered by conditions.
- a5ace0c: `filterChecklist(draft, { valueLimit, blanksLabel })` returns the list a
  checklist filter editor draws: `items` — the values its search shows, in sort
  order, cut to `valueLimit`, then a blanks item while nothing is searched —
  each with its `key`, `label`, `count` and `checked`. A column with more values
  than `valueLimit` lists nothing until something is searched (`needsSearch`),
  and a search matching more lists the first of them, with the rest counted in
  `hiddenCount`.

  `GridMessages` gains `filterBlanks` ("(Blanks)"), `filterSearchFirst(total)`
  ("Type to search 12000 values") and `filterMoreValues(count)` ("250 more,
  refine the search").

- a5ace0c: `isColumnFiltered(filter, columnId)` says whether any entry is about the
  column — whether `describeColumnFilter` reads it as anything but `"none"` —
  for a header to show its column as filtered. A global search marks no column.
- a5ace0c: A condition model for a simple filter editor's rows, which hold text until
  the editor is applied. `filterOperandArity(operator)` says how many inputs a
  row shows. `parseFilterOperand(text, type)` reads a typed operand as the
  column filters it — a number with a point for decimals, rejecting `"12abc"`
  and `"1,5"`; a date as a date input (`yyyy-mm-dd`, local midnight) or a
  date-time input (`yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm`) gives it — and `formatFilterOperand(value,
type)` writes one back for its input.

  `conditionRowsFrom(shape, operators, type)` opens a column's two rows over its
  `describeColumnFilter` shape, as `ConditionRowDraft`s — `{ operator, text,
textTo }`. `conditionsFromRows(rows, columnId, type)` reads them back as
  `{ conditions, invalid }`: the conditions for `filterEditorReducer`'s
  `setConditions`, and the indexes of rows whose operand is missing or doesn't
  read. An empty second row is dropped rather than invalid.

- 1026158: `GridMessages` gains the simple filter editor's strings:
  `filterConditionLabel(position)` ("Condition 2"), `filterOperatorFieldLabel`
  ("Operator"), `filterValueLabel` ("Value"), `filterFromLabel` ("From") and
  `filterToLabel` ("To") for a `between` condition's two ends,
  `filterCombinatorLabel` ("Combine conditions"), `filterAnd` ("And"),
  `filterOr` ("Or"), and `filterValueInvalid(family)` — "Enter a number" on a
  number column, "Enter a date", "Enter a value" or "Choose a value" on the
  others.
- 1026158: Two built-in commands for a column's filter menu, both shown on the header of
  a column `resolveColumnFilterMenu` gives a menu: `filter.open` asks the host
  to open it — `host.openPanel("filter", target)` — and `filter.clear`, enabled
  while `isColumnFiltered`, takes every entry about the column out of the
  filter. `defaultContextMenu.header` lists both after the sort commands.

  `GridPanelKind` gains `"filter"`, and `GridCommandSource` gains
  `"filterMenu"`, for the sort and clear commands a filter menu runs. A switch
  over either that covers every member needs the new case.

  `buildKeyShortcuts` takes `filterable`, naming `Alt+Shift+ArrowDown` — the key
  that opens a header's filter menu.

  `GridMessages` gains `openFilter` ("Filter…"), `clearColumnFilter` ("Clear
  filter"), `filterMenuLabel(columnName)` ("Name filter"), `columnFiltered`
  ("Filtered"), `applyFilter` ("OK"), `cancelFilter` ("Cancel"), `customFilter`
  ("Custom filter") and `filterResults(shown, total)` ("3 of 10 rows").

- a5ace0c: Filter menu options, for a renderer to draw a filter menu in each column's
  header. `GridOptions` gains `filterableColumns` (off by default, like
  `sortableColumns`) and `filterMenu` — `{ ui?: "simple" | "excel";
showCounts?: boolean; valueLimit?: number }`. `ColumnDefinition` gains
  `filterable` and `filterMenu` — `{ ui?, operators? }` — which override the
  grid's, as `sortable` does.

  `resolveColumnFilterMenu(options, column)` settles them for one column: `null`
  when it has no filter menu, else a `ResolvedColumnFilterMenu` — its `ui`
  (`"simple"` by default), the `operators` its conditions offer (the column's
  own without `in`, else its type's `defaultFilterOperators`), its operator
  `family`, `showCounts` (off by default) and `valueLimit`
  (`DEFAULT_FILTER_VALUE_LIMIT`, 10,000, by default).

- 098fd6e: New `excelFilter` preset: `{ filterableColumns: true, filterMenu: { ui: "excel",
showCounts: true } }`, a plain `GridOptions` value that turns on the
  Excel-style filter popup in one spread. Options given after it override it;
  `filterMenu` is replaced whole, not merged.
- 610d28a: `GridMessages` gains the excel filter editor's operator submenu strings:
  `filterOperatorMenu(family)` ("Text filters", "Number filters", "Date
  filters" or "Boolean filters", by the column's `filterOperatorFamily`), the
  button opening the conditions a column offers and that menu's accessible
  name; and `filterBackToValues` ("Back to values"), the button going from a
  condition back to the checklist.
- a5ace0c: Operators by column type, for a filter menu's conditions.
  `filterOperatorFamily(type)` reads a column's `type` as the
  `FilterOperatorFamily` it filters as — `"text"`, `"number"`, `"date"` or
  `"boolean"` — and `defaultFilterOperators(type)` lists the operators a menu
  offers on it: contains, equality, the ends and blanks on text; the orderings
  and `between` on numbers; before, after and `between` on dates, with equality
  left out on date-time and time columns, whose instants a typed value seldom
  equals. `in` is never among them: the checklist is its editor.

  `GridMessages` gains `filterOperatorLabel(operator, family)` — "Before" for
  `lt` on a date, "Less than" on a number, "Is blank" for `isEmpty`.

- a5ace0c: `createColumnValueOptionsCache()` remembers each column's checklist values, so
  reopening a column's filter doesn't count its rows again. Its
  `get(rows, dataColumns, filter, columnId, { locale?, messages? })` returns the
  column's whole `columnValueOptions` list, and the same object again while the
  rows, the columns, the locale, the messages and the filter's entries about
  other columns keep their identity. A column's own entries don't count, so
  applying its filter leaves its list cached.

### Patch Changes

- bd78d43: The package manifests and READMEs now point at the repository's current home, `github.com/gridkitjs/gridkitjs`.

## 0.12.1

### Patch Changes

- 0cf56d4: The `onColumnResize` doc comment no longer claims auto-fit skips it: fitting a column to its content calls it once, with `phase: "end"`.
- 0cf56d4: The `onFilterChange` doc comment names every way the filter changes — the toolbar's search box, `filter.clearAll`, `setFilter` and a restored state — in place of a note that the grid had no filter UI.

## 0.12.0

### Minor Changes

- 183babc: The sorting, grouping, hiding and autofit built-in commands carry an `icon`
  key — `sortAscending`, `sortDescending`, `group`, `hide` and `autoFit`, typed
  as the new `BuiltInCommandIcon` — for a renderer to draw beside their labels.
  An app command may use the same keys.
- 183babc: The controller has `clearColumnSort(columnId)`, which takes one column out of
  the sort and keeps the rest. Its `onColumnSortChange` names that column, where
  a `setColumnSort` leaving it out names the first key that changed — the next
  column, when it was the first key. The built-in `sort.clear` command uses it,
  so clearing the first key of a multi-column sort reports the column cleared.
- 22cf630: A column chooser model and the built-in `column.choose` command, which asks
  the renderer to open the column chooser panel —
  `host.openPanel("columnChooser", target)` — on the grid, a toolbar or a
  header target. `resolveColumnChooser({ columns, visibility, search })` lists
  every data column for a search, hidden ones included, with whether each is
  shown and whether its checkbox is disabled (not `hideable`, or the last
  column shown), the tri-state of a "Show all" checkbox over the hideable
  columns the search lists, and which columns toggling it shows or hides —
  never one that is not `hideable`, and never the last column shown.

  `GridMessages` has new keys: `chooseColumns`, the command's label;
  `columnChooserLabel`, `columnChooserSearchLabel`, `showAllColumns` and
  `noMatchingColumns` for the chooser; and `columnsShown(count)` and
  `columnsHidden(count)`, announced when one change shows or hides more than one
  column.

- 66c2815: `GridMessages` gains `columnsAutoFitted(count)` — "3 columns autofitted",
  "1 column autofitted" — announced when one action autofits more than one
  column.
- 183babc: Three new grid options. `commands` registers the app's own commands for its
  menus to list by id; one with a built-in's id replaces that built-in wherever
  it is listed. `onCommand` is called after a command or an inline menu item
  runs, with a `GridCommandEvent` — `{ commandId, target, source }`, `source`
  being a `GridCommandSource`: `"contextMenu"`, `"toolbar"` or `"api"`.
  `onContextMenuOpenChange` is called as the grid's context menu opens or
  closes, with a `ContextMenuOpenChangeEvent` — `{ open, target }`.
- 183babc: `contextMenu` has three more areas beside `header`: `cell`, a data cell's
  menu, acting on its row and cell; `group`, a group header row's; and `body`,
  the body's empty space. `defaultContextMenu` gives `cell` select all rows,
  clear the selection, and expand or collapse every group; `group` expand or
  collapse every group and stop grouping by its column; and `body` nothing, so
  empty space keeps the browser's menu until it is given entries.
  `GridContextMenuTarget` is a command target in one of the four areas.

  `GridMessages` has three new keys naming these menus: `cellMenuLabel` ("Row
  menu"), `groupMenuLabel` ("Group menu") and `bodyMenuLabel` ("Grid menu").

- 183babc: A `contextMenu` grid option for the grid's own context menu on column
  headers, off by default. `true` shows the defaults — `defaultContextMenu`:
  sort ascending and descending, clear the sort, group by and stop grouping,
  autofit the column or all of them, hide it, and choose the columns shown,
  each where the column allows;
  `{ header: entries }` lists a header's menu in the menu vocabulary, and
  `{ header: [] }` leaves the browser's menu.

  `buildKeyShortcuts` takes an optional `contextMenu` capability, which adds
  `Shift+F10`. `GridMessages` has three new keys: `headerMenuLabel(columnName)`,
  a header menu's accessible name, and `columnHidden(columnName)` and
  `columnShown(columnName)`, announced when one column is hidden or shown.

- 183babc: A `contextMenu` area takes a function as well as entries, asked each time its
  menu opens with a `GridContextMenuRequest` — `{ target, defaults, context }`,
  the target typed for the area — and returning the entries to show, or `null`
  for the browser's menu there. It is how to add to an area's defaults, take
  some out, reorder them, or vary the menu by column or row:

  ```ts
  contextMenu: {
    cell: ({ target, defaults }) =>
      target.columnId === "Id" ? null : ["orders.open", "separator", ...defaults],
  }
  ```

  For a renderer of its own, `contextMenuEntries(contextMenu, context)` gives
  the entries for the place `context.target` names, asking an area's function
  if it has one, and `hasContextMenu(contextMenu, area)` says whether an area
  opens a grid menu at all. `GridContextMenuEntries` is the type of an area's
  option.

- 1fdf433: `columnValueOptions` takes an optional `messages` in its query, the grid's own
  partial `GridMessages`. A boolean option is then labelled `booleanTrue` /
  `booleanFalse`, the same words its cells use, and `search` matches those
  labels. Without it, booleans still read `"true"` / `"false"`.

  ```ts
  columnValueOptions(rows, dataColumns, filter, "Active", {
    locale,
    messages: { booleanTrue: "ja", booleanFalse: "nein" },
  });
  ```

- 3758583: Grid commands: the one implementation behind a menu item, a toolbar button and
  a renderer's API. `builtInCommands()` returns the grid's own — sort a column
  ascending or descending, clear its sort or all sorting, group and ungroup,
  expand or collapse every group, hide or autofit a column, select all rows,
  clear the selection, clear filters — each deciding from a `GridCommandContext`
  whether it shows and whether it can run, and changing the grid only through
  the controller's actions. `resolveCommands(commands)` lays an app's own
  commands over them, replacing a built-in of the same id; `createCommandContext`
  builds the context for a header, cell, group, toolbar or grid target; and
  `runCommand` runs a command only when it is visible and enabled.

  `ColumnDefinition` takes `hideable` (default `true`), which the built-in
  `column.hide` command honours; `hideColumns` still hides any column.
  `GridMessages` has a new key for each built-in label — `sortAscending`,
  `groupByColumn(columnName)`, `clearFilters` and the rest.

- 3758583: A menu model every renderer draws its menus from. A menu is a list of
  `MenuEntry`s — command ids, `"separator"`, inline items and submenus — and
  `resolveMenu(entries, { commands, context })` turns it into what to draw:
  hidden entries and unknown ids left out, labels resolved to strings, `checked`
  set only on checkable items, separators never leading, trailing or doubled,
  empty submenus dropped, and each item's `run()` bound to its context.

  `nextMenuIndex` and `typeaheadIndex` are the pure halves of a menu's keyboard
  handling: where an arrow, Home or End key moves focus, skipping separators and
  wrapping, and which item a typed prefix picks.

- 5f9a5da: `searchTextOf(filter)` and `setSearchText(filter, text)` read and write the
  filter's global text entry as a search box shows it: `setSearchText` stores
  `%text%` — contains `text`, in any column — or removes the entry for empty
  text, leaving every column's entries alone; `searchTextOf` gives the text
  back without its `%` anchors, so a box reading from the filter shows what was
  typed.
- 5f9a5da: `GridMessages` gains the toolbar's strings: `toolbarLabel` ("Grid toolbar"),
  `searchLabel` ("Search"), `searchPlaceholder` ("Search…"), `moreToolbarItems`
  ("More") and `searchResults(count)` ("3 rows found", "1 row found", "No rows
  found"), announced when a search settles. A `messages` object that lists
  every key needs these five added.
- 5f9a5da: A toolbar model, written in the menu vocabulary. A `ToolbarEntry` is any
  `MenuEntry` — a command id is a button, a checkable one a toggle, a submenu a
  dropdown — plus `"search"`, `"spacer"` and `{ type: "custom", id }` for a
  renderer's own content. `resolveToolbar(entries, { commands, contextFor })`
  resolves them by `resolveMenu`'s rules, each item in a context targeting
  `{ area: "toolbar", itemId }`, and separators also collapse beside a spacer.
  `GridToolbarOptions`, `defaultToolbar` (search, spacer, `filter.clearAll`,
  `column.choose`) and
  `toolbarEntries(toolbar)` describe the `toolbar` grid option.

  For a toolbar too narrow for its items, `fitToolbarItems` works out how many
  fit — pinned entries (search and custom, see `isPinnedToolbarItem`) always
  stay, and room for a "More" button is kept only when something overflows —
  and `splitToolbarItems` splits the resolved items into what stays and the
  "More" menu's entries.

  A menu or toolbar entry naming no command is now reported as "the menu or
  toolbar entry `id` names no command, so it is left out."

- 5f9a5da: `GridOptions` gains `toolbar?: boolean | GridToolbarOptions<Row>`: a toolbar
  above the grid, off by default. `true` lists `defaultToolbar` — the search
  box, a spacer, "Clear filters" and "Choose columns" — and `{ items, label }` lists your own
  entries and names the toolbar for a screen reader.

### Patch Changes

- 1fdf433: A checklist filter on a date column whose cells hold ISO strings now opens with
  its values checked after a restore. `restoreState` revives a saved `in` list to
  `Date`s, which still filtered correctly, but `initialFilterEditorDraft` showed
  those values unchecked. Checklist values are now keyed the way the `in`
  operator matches them, so on a date column a date string and the `Date` it

### Minor Changes

- bedd76c: `virtualized`: renders only the rows near the current scroll position rather than every row at once, for a dataset too large to mount in full.   ```tsx

### Minor Changes

### Minor Changes

### Minor Changes

- 375c736: `fitColumnsToWidth` now shrinks unsized columns toward their `minWidth` when
  they exceed the available width, instead of leaving them at their full size

## 0.3.0

### Minor Changes

- 1e112a6: Columns take a `wrap` option — `{ header?: boolean; cells?: boolean }` — and
  two escape-hatch class fields, `headerClassName` and `cellClassName`.

  `wrap` lets a column's header and/or cell text wrap onto multiple lines
  instead of the grid's default single line with an ellipsis; it's off by

## 0.2.0

### Minor Changes

- 7f0645b: Column ordering, as the framework-agnostic half of drag-and-drop reordering.
  `applyColumnOrder(columns, order)` permutes a column list by a
  `ColumnOrderState` — an array of column ids that need not name every column,
  so one it omits keeps its position among the definitions and follows those it
  lists. `moveColumnBefore(order, movedId, beforeId)` produces the new order,
  returning the array it was given when the move changes nothing, and
  `resolveDropBefore(order, targetId, side)` turns a `"before"`/`"after"` hit
  into the id to move in front of, and `movesColumn(order, movedId, beforeId)`
  answers whether such a move would rearrange anything — the two gaps either
  side of a column are drops that change nothing, so an adapter asks this before
  offering one as a target.

  the new `reorderable` option in the same way as `resizable` and surfaced on

## 0.1.0

### Minor Changes

- e0f5b59: Columns take `headerTemplate` in place of `header`, and a new `cellTemplate`
  renders a column's cells.

  `{ field: "Id", header: "#" }` becomes `{ field: "Id", headerTemplate: "#" }`.

  `cellTemplate` receives `{ value, row, rowIndex }` and returns whatever the
  adapter renders — in React, `cellTemplate: ({ value }) => <b>{value}</b>`.
  `value` is the cell's own value read off the field path, so a template that
  only formats it never repeats the path. A column without one renders the raw
  value as before.

- 401a2cc: Address nested fields with `"Parent.Child"` paths, and derive columns from data

  `ColumnDefinition["field"]` now autocompletes one level of nesting via the new
  `FieldPath<Row>` type, while still accepting any string so a path the type
  cannot see is never a hard error. `defineColumnsFromRows` derives a column per
  field across a set of rows, in first-seen order and without duplicates.

  `ColumnDefinition` takes a second type parameter for what a header renders to.
  It defaults to `string` in `@gridkitjs/core`, which stays framework-agnostic;
  `@gridkitjs/react` exports a `ColumnDefinition<Row>` alias bound to `ReactNode`,
  so a header callback can return JSX. This replaces the untyped `Function`.

- a3db97e: Resolve a column's label, resizability and alignment in core

  `ResolvedColumn` gains `label`, `resizable` and `alignment`, so it now describes
  a column completely rather than only its width. `resolveColumnWidths` decides
  all three: a header is resolved eagerly or by calling it, falling back to a
  label read off the field path; `resizable` takes the column's own setting over
  the grid's; alignment falls back to the column's type. A second framework
  adapter renders identically without repeating any of it.

  `resolveColumnWidths` takes a `ColumnResolveOptions` object as its third
  argument in place of the size defaults — `{ sizes: { width: 60 } }` where it was
  `{ width: 60 }` — since the grid-level defaults are no longer only sizes.
  `resolveColumnLabel`, `alignmentForType` and `KEYBOARD_STEP` are exported for
  adapters that resolve columns themselves.

  Columns that set a numeric `type` without an explicit `alignment` now align
  right, matching columns inferred from data — previously only the inferred ones
  did. Numeric alignment covers `decimal`, `currency` and `percent` alongside
  `number`. A column with `header: ""` now renders an empty header instead of
  falling back to its field name.

- 45e492c: Size, resize and auto-fit columns

  `ColumnDefinition` gains `width`, `minWidth`, `maxWidth` and `resizable`, plus an
  optional `id` that state is keyed by and that defaults to `field`. Every width
  calculation lives in `@gridkitjs/core` — `resolveColumnWidths` applies the
  precedence (sizing state, then the column, then the default) and clamps;
  `beginColumnResize`/`applyColumnResize` turn a pointer position into a width;
  `fitColumnsToWidth` distributes a container's width across columns. A future
  adapter for another framework inherits all of it.

  `DataGridComponent` takes `resizableColumns`, `resizeMode`, `onColumnResize` and
  two sizing props that read alike but differ: `defaultColumnSizing` sets the
  starting width of specific columns, keyed by id, while `columnSizeDefaults` sets
  the width and bounds used for any column that does not size itself. Columns can
  be dragged by their right edge, resized with the arrow keys, and sized to their
  content by double-clicking the handle.

  `resizeMode` chooses what a resize does to the other columns. Under the default
  `"fit"`, columns fill the grid: auto-fit leaves those the user has sized alone
  and shares the remaining width between the rest, so a column giving up space
  hands it to its neighbours. Under `"fixed"`, every column keeps its own width —
  a resize moves one column and nothing else, and the grid scrolls or leaves a gap
  to suit.

  The grid now renders inside a scrolling wrapper and sizes its columns through a
  `<colgroup>` with `table-layout: fixed`, which is what makes a width exact.
  Cell content that does not fit its column is truncated with an ellipsis instead
  of wrapping.

## 0.2.0

### Minor Changes

- 183babc: `attachContextMenuTrigger` also asks for a menu on a touch long-press: a
  primary touch resting for half a second without moving, reported as a
  `"pointer"` request at the touch's point. A browser's own `contextmenu` for
  the same press asks only once, and once the long-press opened a menu, the
  click its lifting brings is taken so it does not land in the menu or the cell
  under it.
- 183babc: `attachContextMenuTrigger(root, { onRequest })` reports each context menu the
  user asks for inside `root` — a right-click, Shift+F10 or the ContextMenu
  key — with the element it was asked on, the pointer's position (`null` from
  the keyboard) and how it was asked. `onRequest` answers whether it opened a
  menu, which prevents the browser's own. A key press asks once, even where the
  browser follows it with a `contextmenu` event of its own, and an event a cell
  template already prevented is left to the template.
- 3758583: `attachMenu(panel, options)` makes a `role="menu"` panel a renderer drew
  behave as a menu, following the WAI-ARIA menu pattern. Items are found by
  their menu item role and `data-gridkit-menu-item` id, with one of them the tab
  stop. The arrow keys, Home, End and typeahead move focus among them; Enter,
  Space and a click choose one (`onActivate`), never a disabled one; ArrowRight,
  or the pointer resting on a submenu item, asks for its submenu
  (`onOpenSubmenu`), and ArrowLeft in a submenu asks to close it
  (`onCloseSubmenu`); resting on another item asks to close the open submenu
  (`onCollapseSubmenu`); Tab asks to close every menu (`onClose`). It returns
  `focusItem` and `detach`. Escape stays with `attachOverlay`'s stack, so a
  submenu shown in an overlay of its own above its menu closes alone.
- 4193f42: `attachOverlay` takes two new options and keeps a panel attached as it
  changes size:

  - `initialFocus` — `"first"` (the default, as before), `"panel"`, `"none"` or
    an element — says where focus goes when the overlay attaches.
  - `offset`, also taken by `placeOverlay`, shifts the panel along the anchor's
    edge, so a submenu opened `right-start` can line its first item up with the
    item that opened it.
  - The panel is placed again whenever its own size changes, so a panel flipped
    above its anchor keeps its bottom edge against it as its content shrinks.

- 66c2815: `attachOverlay` takes `ignoreScrollAfterInput`: when `true`, a scroll outside
  the panel in the two animation frames after an `input` or `change` event inside
  it does not dismiss it, so a panel whose controls change the page under it is
  not closed by what they cause. Every other scroll outside the panel still
  dismisses it, and without the option nothing changes.
- 4193f42: Overlays attached with `attachOverlay` now stack in the order they attach, so
  a submenu or a picker can open above the overlay it came from.

  - Escape asks only the topmost overlay to close, and is now consumed: it is
    taken in the capture phase on `window` with `preventDefault()` and
    `stopPropagation()`, so no other listener on the page hears an Escape that
    closed an overlay. With no overlay open, Escape is left alone.
  - A pointer down or a focus move inside an overlay above counts as inside
    every overlay below it.
  - Detaching an overlay dismisses the overlays above it with a new
    `OverlayDismissReason`, `"parent"`, and detaches them. A `switch` over the
    reason that must be exhaustive needs a case for it.

- 5f9a5da: `attachToolbar(toolbar)` makes a `role="toolbar"` element a renderer drew one
  tab stop, following the WAI-ARIA toolbar pattern. Its entries are found by
  `data-gridkit-toolbar-item`, each entry's control being the entry itself or
  the first focusable element in it; ArrowRight and ArrowLeft move between them,
  wrapping, and Home and End go to the ends, passing over separators and
  spacers and keeping `aria-disabled` controls focusable. The tab stop follows
  focus and survives entries coming and going. A text field keeps Home, End and
  the arrows while its caret has text to move through, and the arrows lead out
  of it at either end.
- 66c2815: `ToolbarOverflowItem` takes an optional `label`. When `update` finds an entry's
  label changed while it was in "More", `observeToolbarOverflow` forgets the
  width it remembered for it and measures it afresh, so an entry whose label grew
  shorter comes back out of "More" once it fits. `resolveToolbar`'s items carry
  their labels already.
- 5f9a5da: `observeToolbarOverflow(toolbar, { items, onChange })` measures a toolbar's
  entries and the room it has, and reports how many entries fit — core's
  `fitToolbarItems` count — straight away and whenever that changes: as the
  toolbar or an entry resizes, or as entries are drawn or taken away. Entries
  are found by `data-gridkit-toolbar-item` and the "More" button by
  `data-gridkit-toolbar-more`; an entry moved into "More" keeps the width it
  was last measured at, a spacer counts as nothing, and the toolbar's padding
  and gap are allowed for. It returns `update(options)`, for new items, and
  `detach()`.

## 0.1.0

### Minor Changes

- da4fbda: `bodyCellFrom`, `groupRowFrom` and `bodyRowFrom` turn a delegated body event's
  target into the data cell, group-header row or body row it addresses, by the
  grid's `data-gridkit-*` attributes.
- da4fbda: `startColumnResizeGesture(handle, press, session, { onMove, onEnd, onCancel })`
  drags a column's edge with the pointer captured, reporting each width,
  `onEnd(null)` for a click that resized nothing, and `onCancel` on Escape. Only
  the main button of the primary pointer starts it. `measureColumnContent(table,
columnId)` measures the width a column's widest rendered cell needs.
- da4fbda: `startDragReorder(id, grabElement, press, { resolveTarget, onState, onDrop })`
  runs a reorder drag: a 4-pixel threshold before it opens, the ghost's
  `transform`, and the drop target on every move, reported through `onState` and
  reset to `NO_DRAG` when it ends. Only the main button of the primary pointer
  starts one. `resolveColumnDropTarget` and `resolveGroupByDropTarget` hit-test
  the grid's headers and group-by bar.
- da4fbda: `observeElementWidth(element, onWidth)` reports an element's `clientWidth` at
  once and on every change, and returns the function that disconnects it.
- da4fbda: `createGridFocus({ rowCount, columnCount, isSkippableRow, virtualRange })`
  keeps a grid's single tab stop: `getFocus`, `subscribe`, `focusCell`,
  `handleKey(key, modifiers, pageSize)` for the navigation keys, `attach` to the
  rendered rows, and `focusDrawnCell` to move the browser's focus once a move is
  drawn — scrolling a virtualized row into range first. `findBodyRow` and
  `measurePageSize` read the grid's markup.
- da4fbda: `attachInfiniteScroll(root, { sentinel, hasMore, onLoadMore, isLoadingMore,
rootMargin })` calls `onLoadMore` as the sentinel nears the bottom of `root`,
  once per approach until a load in flight finishes, and returns `update` and
  `detach`.
- da4fbda: `createLiveAnnouncer(container?)` adds a visually hidden, polite live region
  (`role="status"`, class `gridkit-sr-only`) and returns `announce(text)` and
  `destroy()`. Announcing the same text twice in a row reads it out twice.
- da4fbda: `attachOverlay(anchor, panel, { placement, gap, onDismiss, returnFocusTo })`
  positions a panel beside an element or a point — flipping to the other side or
  edge when it would run off screen — moves focus into it, and reports
  `onDismiss` on Escape, a pointer down outside it, a scroll, a resize or focus
  leaving it. Detaching returns focus. `placeOverlay` is the placement
  arithmetic on its own.
- da4fbda: New package: `@gridkitjs/dom`, the browser behaviours a GridKit renderer
  attaches to its own markup — pointer gestures, focus movement, observers, row
  virtualization, overlays and a live-region announcer — as framework-free
  TypeScript. You only need it to write a renderer; `@gridkitjs/react` depends
  on it already.
- da4fbda: `createRowVirtualizer(scrollElement, { estimatedRowHeight, overscan, onRange })`
  windows rows of any height down to those near the scroll position, measuring
  each mounted row, and reports the window through `onRange` only when it moves.
  It has `setRowCount`, `resetHeights`, `measureRow(index)` ref callbacks,
  `scrollToIndex` (which corrects itself once an unmounted target mounts) and
  `destroy`.

## 0.13.0

### Minor Changes

- 6a4c6c2: The built-in pager is redrawn as one connected bar, `« ‹ pages › »`, that no longer shifts as the user pages through it, followed by the page-size `<select>` with its label to its right.

  - New First and Last buttons, named by the new `firstPage` and `lastPage` messages.
  - Previous and Next show chevron icons instead of their text; `previousPage` and `nextPage` are now their accessible names and tooltips. A test that found them by text, such as `locator(".grid-pager-button", { hasText: "Next" })`, should find them by role: `getByRole("button", { name: "Next" })`.
  - The arrows and pages sit inside a new `.grid-pager-bar`. Arrow buttons carry `grid-pager-nav` plus `grid-pager-first`, `grid-pager-previous`, `grid-pager-next` or `grid-pager-last`; page-number buttons carry `grid-pager-page`. All of them keep `grid-pager-button`.
  - The compact status is wrapped in `.grid-pager-status-slot` beside a hidden `.grid-pager-status-sizer` holding its widest text, so it keeps one width; `.grid-pager-status` still holds the visible text.
  - The page-size label text follows the `<select>` inside `.grid-pager-page-size`, in a `.grid-pager-page-size-label` span, where it came before it.

- 6a4c6c2: `DataGrid`'s header, body and footer `<table>` elements are now `role="presentation"`, and their `<thead>`, `<tbody>` and `<tfoot>` carry `role="rowgroup"`, so every row and cell belongs to the `grid` or `treegrid` element instead of to a native table. A grouped grid's group rows keep `aria-level`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-posinset` and `aria-setsize`, which are now valid there; screen readers stop announcing a table inside the grid, and the axe `aria-required-children` and `aria-conditional-attr` violations are gone. Class names and keyboard behaviour are unchanged.

  A test that found the grid's markup by the `table` role no longer matches. Query the grid instead, or a class name:

  ```ts
  // Before
  page.getByRole("table");
  // After
  page.getByRole("grid"); // or "treegrid" while grouped
  page.locator(".gridkit-data-grid-header"); // one table, by class
  ```

The `use*State` hooks such as `usePaginationState` render their pre-mount values on the server too.

## 0.12.0

### Minor Changes

- 1026158: Applying a column's filter menu is announced: once the grid has drawn the rows
  the filter keeps, the live region reads how many of all the rows they are —
  "2 of 3 rows", the `filterResults` message. A controlled `filter` that doesn't
  take the change announces nothing.
- 610d28a: `filterMenu.ui: "excel"` — the grid's or a column's — now opens the excel
  editor in place of the simple one: a search box, a tri-state "Select all"
  checkbox and a checklist of the column's values, in its sort order and
  labelled as its cells print, with "(Blanks)" last and, under
  `filterMenu.showCounts`, how many rows hold each. The values cascade from the
  other columns' filters. The search narrows the list and "Select all" acts on
  what it shows; past `filterMenu.valueLimit` values (10,000 by default) the
  list waits for a search, then lists the first matches and how many more there
  are. The list is windowed, one `listbox` stop for Tab, moved through with the
  arrow keys, Home, End, PageUp and PageDown, Space checking a value.

  OK, or Enter anywhere but on a button, applies the checked values: every value
  checked removes the column's filter, anything less sets one `in` entry, OR-ed
  with `isEmpty` while "(Blanks)" stays checked. Conditions or a custom filter
  open with every value checked under a note, and stay until a value is changed
  and applied. Reopening a column's menu reuses the values it counted until the
  rows, the columns or another column's filter change.

- 1026158: A filterable header shows a filter button beside its sort toggle, which opens
  the column's filter menu and closes it pressed again, and
  `Alt+Shift+ArrowDown` on a focused header opens it too, listed in the
  header's `aria-keyshortcuts`. While the column is filtered the button carries
  `is-filtered` and the header `aria-description="Filtered"` (the
  `columnFiltered` message), whatever set the filter. A column without a filter
  menu shows neither, however it is filtered.

  `Alt+Shift+ArrowDown` on a groupable header no longer groups it: grouping
  takes `Alt+ArrowDown` alone, as its `aria-keyshortcuts` always said.

- 098fd6e: `excelFilter` is exported from `@gridkitjs/react`, so the Excel-style filter
  popup turns on with `<DataGrid {...excelFilter} />`. A prop written after the
  spread overrides it, e.g. `filterMenu={{ ui: "simple" }}`.
- 1026158: `DataGridApi` gains `openFilterMenu(columnId)`, which opens a shown column's
  filter menu below its header and returns whether it did — `false` for a
  column with no filter menu — and `closeFilterMenu()`, which closes it and
  leaves the column chooser open.
- 1026158: A column with a filter menu — every column under `filterableColumns`, or one
  whose own `filterable` is `true` — opens it from "Filter…" in its header's
  context menu: a dialog below the header, named after its column ("Name
  filter"), with the column's sort entries while it sorts, then "Clear filter",
  Cancel and OK. Tab stays inside it; Escape or a click outside closes it,
  giving focus back to the header. Its sort entries and "Clear filter" run the
  `sort.*` and `filter.clear` commands, so `onCommand` hears them with the
  source `"filterMenu"`.
- 1026158: The column filter menu has an editor: one condition — an operator and a value
  — and an optional second, joined by And or Or. The operators are the column
  type's, or its own `filterMenu.operators`, and the value box suits the type: a
  number box, a date picker on a `"date"` column, a date-and-time picker on a
  `"dateTime"` or `"time"` one, a true/false choice on a `"boolean"` one, text
  otherwise. OK, or Enter, applies the conditions in place of the column's
  filter; reopened, the menu shows them, however they were set. A value missing
  or not reading keeps the menu open, its box marked `aria-invalid` and
  focused; a filter the editor can't show reads "Custom filter" until
  conditions replace it.

  Focus now starts on the first condition's value box rather than the menu's
  first button.

- 610d28a: The excel filter editor has an operator submenu: a "Text filters" button —
  "Number filters", "Date filters" or "Boolean filters", by the column's type —
  above its search box opens a menu of the conditions the column offers,
  beside the filter menu. Choosing one shows the simple editor's conditions in
  place of the checklist, the first at the operator chosen, under a "Back to
  values" button that brings the checklist back as it was left; OK there
  applies the conditions in place of the column's checked values. While the
  column is filtered by conditions, the button is ticked and the operators in
  use are checked in its menu; choosing one opens the conditions as applied.
  The button follows the menu button pattern (Enter, Space or ArrowDown opens
  the menu on its first item, ArrowUp on its last), and Escape or Tab in the
  menu closes it alone. A column whose `filterMenu.operators` is empty offers
  no menu.

  Switching `filterMenu.ui` at runtime keeps every filter: conditions show in
  the simple editor or through this menu, checked values in the excel editor.

- ebac1dd: The grid copies to the clipboard, as tab-separated text and an HTML table, so
  a paste into a spreadsheet keeps the columns. With `contextMenu` on, the cell
  menu now starts with Copy cell, Copy row and Copy selection. Ctrl+C (Cmd+C on
  a Mac) in the grid copies the selection, else the focused cell — but not in a
  text field inside a cell or while text is highlighted on the page, which stay
  the browser's. `runCommand("copy.selection")` copies from code. A screen reader
  hears what was copied ("3 rows copied") or "Copy failed".
- 812d0b6: The grid exports. The toolbar's `"export"` entry draws an Export dropdown, and
  the export commands — `export.csv`, `export.json`, `exportSelection.csv` and
  the rest — download their file from the toolbar, a context menu or
  `runCommand`; none is shown by default, so list them where you want them:

  ```tsx
  <DataGrid toolbar={{ items: ["search", "spacer", "export"] }} />
  ```

  One export downloads at a time — one asked for while an asynchronous writer
  is still writing is dropped and logged — and a writer that fails is logged
  and announced as `messages.exportFailed`.

  The ref gains `exportData(format, options?)`, which resolves to a `Blob` of

  `options` over it. It rejects for a format no writer is registered for.
  `ExportFile`, `ExportOptions`, `ExportWriter` and `GridExportOptions` are
  re-exported from `@gridkitjs/react`.

- 0119cd3: The grid prints. `"print"` in the toolbar's items is a Print button, `print`
  in a context menu area a Print item, and `ref.current.print(options?)` prints

## 0.10.0

### Minor Changes

- 6af35c6: Columns can be shown and hidden. A column with `hidden: true` starts out
  hidden; `defaultColumnVisibility` (column id → `true`/`false`) overrides that
  per column, and the ref's `showColumns(ids)` / `hideColumns(ids)` change it
  afterwards. A hidden column still sorts, filters and groups, and keeps its
  place in the column order for when it is shown again.

  - `onColumnVisibilityChange` fires once per change with `{ columnIds,
visibility }`.
  - `DataGridApi` gains `getColumnVisibility()` and `getDataColumns()` (every
    column, hidden ones included); `getColumns()` lists only what is shown.
  - `useColumnVisibilityState(gridRef)` follows the visibility state from
    outside the grid.
  - `aria-colcount`, the column widths and keyboard column moves count only the
    columns shown; a group header or group-by chip for a hidden column keeps
    its label.

- bad8ea3: `DataGrid` takes controlled `columnSizing`, `columnOrder` and
  `columnVisibility` props beside `defaultColumnSizing`, `defaultColumnOrder`
  and `defaultColumnVisibility`. Given one, the grid applies it as given, and a
  resize, a drop or `showColumns`/`hideColumns` asks for a change through
  `onColumnResize` (whose `sizing` is the next state), `onColumnOrderChange` or
  `onColumnVisibilityChange` instead of making it.
- bad8ea3: `DataGrid` takes controlled `columnSort`, `groupBy`, `groupExpansion` and
  `pagination` props beside the existing `default*` ones. Given one, the grid
  shows exactly that value, and a header click, group toggle or pager button
  only asks for a change through the matching `on*Change` callback, taking
  effect once the prop follows:

  ```tsx
  const [sort, setSort] = useState<ColumnSortState>([]);

  <DataGrid
    sortableColumns
    columnSort={sort}
    onColumnSortChange={(event) => setSort(event.sort)}
  />;
  ```

  Each slice is controlled or not on its own; passing both a controlled prop and
  its default logs a `console.error` once and the controlled value wins. A
  controlled `pagination` is not sent back to the first page when the filter,
  sort or grouping changes — reset it alongside the change if you want that.

- 6af35c6: Cells and aggregates without a template now render through `formatCellValue`
  from `@gridkitjs/core`, and `DataGrid` takes a `locale` prop (`"de-DE"`, or a
  list to fall back through).

  - A `Date` cell renders as text instead of throwing, and a boolean cell reads
    `true`/`false` instead of rendering nothing.
  - Formatting is opt-in: setting `locale`, or a column's `format`, formats
    that column's dates and numbers through `Intl` by its `type` — `currency`
    with `format.currency`, `percent` reading `0.25` as 25%, `date` and
    `time` showing only that part. Without either, numbers, totals and group
    values read exactly as before.
  - Footer, group-summary and inline group aggregates then format like their
    column's values (a `count` reads as a plain number); a group header's value
    formats like its column's cells.
  - Announcements name a column by its new `header` text when it has one, so a
    column with a markup `headerTemplate` is announced by name.

- 78e10e5: Add `getPageRows()` to `DataGridApi`: the current page of `getDisplayRows()`,
  exactly the rows the body renders — all of them when `paginated` is off.
- bad8ea3: `DataGridApi` can now drive every slice of state, not only read it:
  `setColumnSort`, `setGroupBy`, `setGroupExpansion`, `setPagination`,
  `setColumnSizing`, `setColumnOrder`, `setColumnVisibility`,
  `setRowSelection`, `setColumnSelection` and `setCellSelection` each replace
  their slice and fire its `on*Change` callback as a user's change would
  (nothing for an equal value; only a request for a controlled slice).
  `getState()` reads every slice at once and `restoreState(saved)` puts a whole
  or partial state back with one re-render; `serializeGridState`, now
  re-exported from `@gridkitjs/react`, makes it safe to save as JSON.
  `autoFitColumn(columnId)` sizes a column to its content as double-clicking
  its resize handle does.

  `setFilter` now treats a filter equal in content to the current one as no
  change, rather than only the same entries.

- 8d411eb: `DataGrid` takes `messages`, a partial `GridMessages` that replaces its own
  English strings key by key: the pager's buttons and status, the group-by bar,

  every live-region announcement. Left out, every string reads exactly as
  before. `GridMessages` is re-exported.
- bad8ea3: `@gridkitjs/core` exports `GridOptions<Row>`: every grid setting that names no
  renderer type — data, row identity, what the user may do, starting state and
  change callbacks — in one interface, with the `Borders`, `HoverableConfig` and

- da4fbda: `@gridkitjs/react` now depends on `@gridkitjs/dom`, which holds the browser

- 487d8fa: **Breaking:** the grid component is renamed from `DataGridComponent` to

  ```tsx
  // before
  import { DataGridComponent } from "@gridkitjs/react";
  <DataGridComponent columns={columns} dataSource={rows} />;
  ```

## 0.9.0

### Minor Changes

- bedd76c: `infiniteScroll`: loads more rows as the user scrolls near the bottom of the grid's body, in place of `paginated`'s page-by-page navigation.

  ```tsx
  <DataGridComponent
    columns={columns}
    dataSource={rows}
    height={400}
    infiniteScroll={{ hasMore, isLoadingMore, onLoadMore }}
  />
  ```

  `hasMore` and `onLoadMore` are required; `isLoadingMore` suppresses further calls while a load is in flight; `rootMargin` (default `"200px"`) tunes how early it fires relative to the grid's own scrollable body; `loadingTemplate` replaces the built-in "Loading more…" row.

  Mutually exclusive with `paginated` — setting both logs a dev-time `console.error` and only `paginated` takes effect. Independent of `virtualized`, though pairing the two is the recommended combination for a dataset that grows without bound.

- bedd76c: `height`: bounds the row area to a fixed size, independently scrollable — the group-by bar, header, footer, and pager stay outside it and always visible.

  ```tsx
  <DataGridComponent columns={columns} dataSource={rows} height={400} />
  ```

  A number is pixels; a string is passed through as a CSS length (e.g. `"60vh"`). Omitted, the body's height stays content-driven, exactly as before this prop existed.

  Breaking: the header, body, and footer now render as three separate `<table>`s — `.gridkit-data-grid-header`, the body's own (wrapped in a new `.gridkit-data-grid-body` scroll container), and `.gridkit-data-grid-footer` — inside a new `.gridkit-data-grid-tables` wrapper `<div>` that now carries `role="grid"`/`"treegrid"` and the grid's other grid-level ARIA attributes. Previously all three sat inside one `<table>`, which itself carried that role. This only matters to a consumer whose own CSS or tests reach into the grid's raw table structure (unsupported usage, but possible) — every cell-level role, and everything reachable through `DataGridApi`, is unchanged. One exception: `DataGridApi.table` now points at the body's `<table>` specifically (the one holding `<tbody>`) rather than a single table that also held the header and footer.

- bedd76c: `virtualized`: renders only the rows near the current scroll position rather than every row at once, for a dataset too large to mount in full. Requires `height` to be set — a body with no bounded height has no viewport to window rows against, and a dev-time `console.error` fires if `virtualized` is on without it.

  ```tsx
  <DataGridComponent
    columns={columns}
    dataSource={rows}
    height={400}
    virtualized
  />
  ```

  Row height is measured per row rather than assumed uniform, so `.is-wrapped` cells and group header/summary rows (which differ in height from data rows) lay out correctly. Two new props tune it: `overscan` (rows rendered outside the visible range on each side, default `4`) and `estimatedRowHeight` (the assumed height for a row never yet measured, default `40`) — both meaningful only with `virtualized` on.

  `scrollToRow` and keyboard navigation (arrow keys, `Home`/`End`, `Ctrl+Home`/`Ctrl+End`) both work correctly when their target row isn't currently mounted: they scroll it into range first, using measured heights where known, then correct the exact position once it mounts and is measured.

  Fully orthogonal to `paginated` and `groupBy` — combinable with either, though virtualizing an already-small paginated page is low-value.

  `@gridkitjs/core` gains `visibleRange` (plus its `RowHeights`/`VisibleRange` types) — the pure range math `virtualized` is built on. Not something most consumers need directly; it's exported for the same reason `paginateRows` is.

## 0.8.0

### Minor Changes

- 6e8189b: Aggregates: compute a subtotal per group and a grand total over the whole filtered/grouped dataset.

  ```ts
  <DataGridComponent
    columns={columns}
    dataSource={rows}
    groupableColumns
    defaultGroupBy={[{ columnId: "Region" }]}
    aggregates={[{ columnId: "Amount", fn: "sum" }]}
  />;
  ```

  - `aggregates` is a plain controlled prop — `AggregateState<Row>`, an array of `{ columnId, fn, id?, alignment? }` specs. Unlike `sort`/`filter`/`groupBy`/`pagination`, there is no built-in UI to add or remove an aggregate interactively, so there's no `defaultAggregates`/`onAggregatesChange` pair.
  - `groupAggregateDisplay` chooses how a group's own subtotal renders: `"inline"` (the default) keeps it as text in the group header, next to its leaf-row count; `"row"` instead renders a dedicated row after that group's last visible entry, with each aggregate's value in the `<td>` for its own column, aligned the same way the grand-total footer's cells are.
  - A footer or `"row"`-mode summary cell aligns the same way its column's own data cells do, unless `AggregateSpec.alignment` overrides it for that specific aggregate — e.g. centering a `count` under an otherwise right-aligned currency column. When two specs share a column and disagree, the first one in `aggregates` wins for that shared cell.
  - A grand-total footer (a `<tfoot>`, outside `aria-rowcount`) renders below the body whenever `aggregates` is non-empty, regardless of `groupAggregateDisplay`.
  - `ColumnDefinition.footerTemplate` renders a column's own aggregate result in place of its plain formatted value, in the grand-total footer and — under `groupAggregateDisplay: "row"` — a group's own summary row.
  - A group's summary row is presentational: it occupies a real row slot (`aria-rowindex` counts it, same as a header or data row) but the arrow keys step over it rather than landing a tab stop there, and it never splits from its own group across a page boundary.
  - Aggregates are always computed over the full dataset, never scoped to the current page — composed ahead of pagination in the render pipeline, so a group's subtotal reads identically regardless of which page currently shows it.
  - `DataGridApi` gains `getAggregates()` for the grand total; a specific group's own results are read off `getDisplayRows()`, which now returns rows carrying a populated `aggregates` field.

  Depends on `@gridkitjs/core`'s new aggregate primitives (`computeAggregates`/`withGroupAggregates`) — see that package's own changelog entry, including the additive `aggregates` field it adds to `ResolvedGroupRow`.

- 6e8189b: `pager.template` — a render prop that replaces the built-in pager's markup entirely, called on every render where pagination-relevant state changed. Also exports the new `PagerTemplateContext` type. As a side effect, `pager={{ template: () => null }}` is now the documented way to suppress the built-in pager while keeping `paginated` row-windowing and the imperative API active — previously there was no way to do that short of turning `paginated` off entirely.
- 6e8189b: Opt-in numbered pager: `pager={{ variant: "numbered" }}` swaps the built-in pager's "Page X of Y" display for `[Prev][1][2][3]…[n][Next]` page buttons. `pager.boundaryCount` (default `1`) and `pager.siblingCount` (default `1`) control how many pages are always shown at each end and around the current page. Default stays `"compact"` — today's Prev/status/Next — so no existing consumer's rendered output changes.
- 6e8189b: `DataGridProps.pageSizeOptions` is now grouped under a `pager` config object,
  so future pager presentation options (a variant, a custom template) can land
  without another breaking rename:

  ```diff
   <DataGridComponent
     paginated
  -  pageSizeOptions={[10, 25, 50]}
  +  pager={{ sizeOptions: [10, 25, 50] }}
   />;
  ```

- 6e8189b: Pagination: split the grid's rows into pages, respecting group boundaries.

  ```ts
  <DataGridComponent
    columns={columns}
    dataSource={rows}
    paginated
    defaultPagination={{ pageIndex: 0, pageSize: 25 }}
    pager={{ sizeOptions: [10, 25, 50] }}
    onPaginationChange={({ pagination }) => persist(pagination)}
  />;
  ```

  - `paginated` turns pagination on; `defaultPagination`/`onPaginationChange` are the uncontrolled page/page-size pair and its change callback, mirroring `defaultColumnSort`/`onColumnSortChange`. Pagination always composes after filtering, sorting, and grouping — a page is a window onto the finished result. When grouping is also active, a page's unit is a top-level group, never a leaf row, so a group is never split across a page boundary.
  - Turning `paginated` on renders a minimal, semantically-classed pager below the grid (Previous/Next, a page display, and — with `pager.sizeOptions` — a page-size select). Style it via `@gridkitjs/theme-tailwind` or your own CSS.
  - `DataGridApi` gains `getPagination()`, `getPageCount()`, `goToPage()`, `nextPage()`, `previousPage()`, and `setPageSize()`.
  - Filtering, sorting, or changing the group-by stack resets to the first page, so a user is never silently stranded on a page a smaller result set no longer has.

  Depends on `@gridkitjs/core`'s new pagination primitives (`paginateRows` and friends) — see that package's own changelog entry, including the `datasetIndex` field this adds to `ResolvedRow`/`ResolvedGroupRow`/`CellTemplateContext`.

  Breaking: `aria-rowindex` on a rendered row is now built from that row's absolute dataset position rather than its rendered position — the two only diverge once `paginated` is on, but the change applies unconditionally. `GridGroupRow`'s exported prop shape (if consumed directly, which is not the supported path) drops `rowIndex` in favor of `datasetIndex`.

- 6e8189b: `DataGridApi` gains `subscribe(listener)`, a read/notify channel for reacting to grid state without polling the imperative getters — not a second, imperative-only way to drive that state. It's the primitive the new `use*State` hooks (added in following changes) are built on with `useSyncExternalStore`; most consumers should reach for one of those instead of calling `subscribe` directly.
- 6e8189b: New `useAggregateState(gridRef)` hook: the grand-total aggregate results, read reactively off a mounted `DataGridComponent`'s `ref`, for a summary footer or bar living outside the grid's own DOM. Read-only, and updates even on changes with no dedicated `on*Change` prop of their own — a filter/sort/regroup altering the grand total.
- 6e8189b: New `useColumnSizingState(gridRef)` and `useColumnOrderState(gridRef)` hooks: column widths and column order, read reactively off a mounted `DataGridComponent`'s `ref`. Read-only — sizing and order stay uncontrolled via `defaultColumnSizing`/`defaultColumnOrder` and the grid's own resize/reorder handles.
- 6e8189b: New `useColumnSortState(gridRef)` hook: the grid's active sort, read reactively off a mounted `DataGridComponent`'s `ref`, for a sort indicator living outside the grid's own DOM. Read-only — `DataGridApi` has no sort-mutating action.
- 6e8189b: New `useGroupByState(gridRef)` hook: reactive group-by and group-expansion state read off a mounted `DataGridComponent`'s `ref`, with `expandAllGroups`/`collapseAllGroups` actions, for a custom group-by UI living outside the grid's own DOM.
- 6e8189b: New `usePaginationState(gridRef)` hook: reactive pagination state and actions (`goToPage`, `nextPage`, `previousPage`, `setPageSize`) read off a mounted `DataGridComponent`'s `ref`, for building a pager entirely outside the grid's own DOM. Updates on every pagination change, including the silent page-0 reset a filter/sort/regroup triggers.
- 6e8189b: New `useSelectionState(gridRef)` hook: row, column, and cell selection read together as one reactive concern off a mounted `DataGridComponent`'s `ref`, with `clearSelection`/`selectAllRows` actions, for a "N rows selected" toolbar living outside the grid's own DOM.

### Minor Changes

- 388def3: Drag a column header into the group-by bar to add it to the grouping, and
  drag chips within the bar to reorder the stack.

  ```ts
  <DataGridComponent
    columns={columns}
    dataSource={rows}
    groupableColumns
    groupByDraggableColumns
    groupByBarVisibility="always"
  />;
  ```

  - `groupByDraggableColumns` (grid-level) / `ColumnDefinition.groupByDraggable`
    (per-column) let a header be dragged straight into the group-by bar,
    independent of `groupableColumns` — a column can be groupable via its
    header's click/keyboard toggle, via this drag, both, or neither. Dropped at
    a specific point among the bar's existing chips, it's inserted there, not
    appended. A column already in the group-by stack rejects its own header
    dragged back toward the bar — a `not-allowed` cursor and a muted outline in
    place of the usual accent one — since repositioning an existing level is
    the chip's job, not the header's.
  - Chips in the group-by bar are now draggable to reorder the stack, and each
    chip is its own focusable stop — focus one and press `Ctrl+ArrowLeft`/
    `Ctrl+ArrowRight` to move it, mirroring a column header's own reorder
    shortcut.
  - `groupToggleIconColumns` (grid-level) / `ColumnDefinition.groupToggleIcon`
    (per-column) hide a groupable header's group-toggle icon without touching
    its capability — `Alt+ArrowDown` keeps working with the icon hidden.
  - `groupByBarVisibility` (`"always" | "auto" | "never"`, default `"auto"`)
    controls when the group-by bar renders, decoupled from `groupableColumns`.
    `"auto"` shows it once `groupBy` is non-empty, or while a header drag
    eligible to drop into it is in progress, so there's a drop target even
    from a fully empty grouping.

  **Breaking**: the group-by bar's visibility no longer follows
  `groupableColumns` — it's governed by the new `groupByBarVisibility` alone.
  A grid grouping purely programmatically (`defaultGroupBy` with
  `groupableColumns` off) previously showed no bar; under the new `"auto"`
  default it now does once `groupBy` is non-empty. Pass
  `groupByBarVisibility="never"` to keep the previous behavior.

  Internally, `useColumnDrag`'s pointer-drag mechanics are extracted into a
  new, reusable `useDragReorder` hook shared with the group-by bar's own chip
  dragging — no change to any existing public API.

- 388def3: Row grouping: stack one or more columns into nested, collapsible groups.

  ```ts

    columns={columns}
    dataSource={rows}
    groupableColumns
    defaultGroupBy={[{ columnId: "Region" }, { columnId: "Status" }]}
    onGroupByChange={({ groupBy }) => persist(groupBy)}
  />;
  ```

  - `groupableColumns` (grid-level) / `ColumnDefinition.groupable` (per-column)
    turn on each header's group toggle — click its icon, or focus the header
    and press `Alt+ArrowDown`, to add or remove that column from the group-by
    stack. A group-by bar above the grid lists the active stack as removable
    chips.
  - `defaultGroupBy`/`onGroupByChange` and `defaultGroupExpansion`/
    `onGroupExpansionChange` for the uncontrolled group-by stack and its
    collapsed/expanded state. Click a group header, or focus it and press
    `Space`/`Enter`, to toggle it.
  - `DataGridApi` gains `getGroupBy()`, `getGroupExpansion()`, `getDisplayRows()`
    (`getRows()`'s data regrouped, with group headers interleaved), and
    `expandAllGroups()`/`collapseAllGroups()`. `getRows()` itself is unchanged —
    it still returns the flat, ungrouped rows, exactly as before.
  - The grid's `role` switches from `"grid"` to the WAI-ARIA `"treegrid"`
    pattern whenever `groupBy` is non-empty, with `aria-expanded`/`aria-level`/

- ac7695f: Internal refactor of `DataGrid`'s implementation: pointer-drag lifecycles

## 0.4.0

### Minor Changes

- f30a2a9: The grid is now an ARIA grid a keyboard can navigate. It carries `role="grid"`
  with row and column counts and indices, headers carry `scope="col"`, and one
  roving tab stop moves cell to cell under the arrow keys, Home, End, Ctrl+Home,
  Ctrl+End and the page keys.

  Two changes to what a keyboard already did:

  - **Tab now passes the whole grid**, entering it once instead of stopping on
    every resize handle. The handles have left the tab order — a widget under
    `role="grid"` has one tab stop, and a grid of twenty columns previously had
    twenty.
  - **Keyboard resize moved to `Alt+ArrowLeft` / `Alt+ArrowRight`** on the focused
    header, from the bare arrows on its handle, which the grid now needs for
    navigation. `Ctrl+ArrowLeft` / `Ctrl+ArrowRight` still reorder.

  `label` and `labelledBy` give the grid its accessible name, without which a
  screen reader announces only "grid":

  ```tsx
  <DataGridComponent label="Application costs" ... />
  ```

  Reorders and resizes are announced through a live region, so a change with only
  a visual cue is no longer silent.

- f92198e: `DataGridComponent` takes `getRowId`, giving each row a stable identity for
  state keyed by it. Rows are keyed by it rather than by their array position, and
  `cellTemplate` receives it as `rowId` alongside a `selected` flag.

  ```tsx
  <DataGridComponent dataSource={rows} getRowId={(row) => row.Id} />
  ```

  Without it a row is identified by its position, which is enough for a static
  grid — so nothing has to change — but ties row state to where a row sits rather
  than to the row itself.

- 4a92413: Rows, columns and cells can be selected. `selectable` says which and how many
  of each — off by default, since selection claims the click:

  ```tsx
  <DataGridComponent
    dataSource={rows}
    getRowId={(row) => row.Id}
    selectable={{ rows: "multiple", columns: "multiple", cells: "single" }}
    onRowSelect={({ row }) => console.log(row.row.Name)}
    onRowSelectionChange={({ added, removed, selected }) => persist(selected)}
  />
  ```

  A cell takes `false | "single"` rather than a mode of its own — it addresses one
  value, so there is no range to take.

  Click replaces, Ctrl-click toggles and Shift-click takes a range; from the
  keyboard, Space toggles the focused row or column, Enter replaces, `Ctrl+A`
  takes every row and Escape lets them all go. Rows and cells report
  `aria-selected`, and the grid `aria-multiselectable`.

  Thirteen callbacks report it — `onRowSelect`, `onRowsSelect`, `onRowDeselect`,
  `onRowsDeselect` and `onRowSelectionChange`, the same five for columns, and
  `onCellSelect` / `onCellDeselect` / `onCellSelectionChange`. Each carries the
  resolved row, column or cell value rather than a bare id, and all of them are
  fanned out from one diff, so no two can disagree about what an interaction did.
  `defaultRowSelection`, `defaultColumnSelection` and `defaultCellSelection` set
  the starting state.

  Give `getRowId` alongside `selectable` for data that sorts, filters or pages:
  without it a row is identified by its position, so a re-sort leaves the same
  positions selected under different rows.

## 0.1.0

### Minor Changes

- e0f5b59: Columns take `headerTemplate` in place of `header`, and a new `cellTemplate`
  renders a column's cells.

  `{ field: "Id", header: "#" }` becomes `{ field: "Id", headerTemplate: "#" }`.

  `cellTemplate` receives `{ value, row, rowIndex }` and returns whatever the
  adapter renders — in React, `cellTemplate: ({ value }) => <b>{value}</b>`.
  `value` is the cell's own value read off the field path, so a template that
  only formats it never repeats the path. A column without one renders the raw
  value as before.

- 401a2cc: Address nested fields with `"Parent.Child"` paths, and derive columns from data

  `ColumnDefinition["field"]` now autocompletes one level of nesting via the new
  `FieldPath<Row>` type, while still accepting any string so a path the type
  cannot see is never a hard error. `defineColumnsFromRows` derives a column per
  field across a set of rows, in first-seen order and without duplicates.

  `ColumnDefinition` takes a second type parameter for what a header renders to.
  It defaults to `string` in `@gridkitjs/core`, which stays framework-agnostic;
  `@gridkitjs/react` exports a `ColumnDefinition<Row>` alias bound to `ReactNode`,
  so a header callback can return JSX. This replaces the untyped `Function`.

- a3db97e: Resolve a column's label, resizability and alignment in core

  `ResolvedColumn` gains `label`, `resizable` and `alignment`, so it now describes
  a column completely rather than only its width. `resolveColumnWidths` decides
  all three: a header is resolved eagerly or by calling it, falling back to a
  label read off the field path; `resizable` takes the column's own setting over
  the grid's; alignment falls back to the column's type. A second framework
  adapter renders identically without repeating any of it.

  `resolveColumnWidths` takes a `ColumnResolveOptions` object as its third
  argument in place of the size defaults — `{ sizes: { width: 60 } }` where it was
  `{ width: 60 }` — since the grid-level defaults are no longer only sizes.
  `resolveColumnLabel`, `alignmentForType` and `KEYBOARD_STEP` are exported for
  adapters that resolve columns themselves.

  Columns that set a numeric `type` without an explicit `alignment` now align
  right, matching columns inferred from data — previously only the inferred ones
  did. Numeric alignment covers `decimal`, `currency` and `percent` alongside
  `number`. A column with `header: ""` now renders an empty header instead of
  falling back to its field name.

- 45e492c: Size, resize and auto-fit columns

  `ColumnDefinition` gains `width`, `minWidth`, `maxWidth` and `resizable`, plus an
  optional `id` that state is keyed by and that defaults to `field`. Every width
  calculation lives in `@gridkitjs/core` — `resolveColumnWidths` applies the
  precedence (sizing state, then the column, then the default) and clamps;
  `beginColumnResize`/`applyColumnResize` turn a pointer position into a width;
  `fitColumnsToWidth` distributes a container's width across columns. A future
  adapter for another framework inherits all of it.

  `DataGridComponent` takes `resizableColumns`, `resizeMode`, `onColumnResize` and
  two sizing props that read alike but differ: `defaultColumnSizing` sets the
  starting width of specific columns, keyed by id, while `columnSizeDefaults` sets
  the width and bounds used for any column that does not size itself. Columns can
  be dragged by their right edge, resized with the arrow keys, and sized to their
  content by double-clicking the handle.

  `resizeMode` chooses what a resize does to the other columns. Under the default
  `"fit"`, columns fill the grid: auto-fit leaves those the user has sized alone
  and shares the remaining width between the rest, so a column giving up space
  hands it to its neighbours. Under `"fixed"`, every column keeps its own width —
  a resize moves one column and nothing else, and the grid scrolls or leaves a gap
  to suit.

  The grid now renders inside a scrolling wrapper and sizes its columns through a
  `<colgroup>` with `table-layout: fixed`, which is what makes a width exact.
  Cell content that does not fit its column is truncated with an ellipsis instead
  of wrapping.

  is open — with a `.filter-menu-submenu-icon` before its label, ticked in
  `--gridkit-accent` while the column is filtered by conditions, and a
  `.filter-menu-submenu-indicator` chevron at the end. `.filter-menu-back`,
  "Back to values" above a condition the submenu chose, is drawn the same, its
  `.filter-menu-back-icon` chevron before its label.
- 0119cd3: Printing the page with the browser's own print (Ctrl+P) now shows the grid as
  a plain table: an `@media print` block hides the toolbar, the group-by bar, the
  pager and the resize handles, lets a `height`-bound grid's drawn rows flow
  onto as many pages as they take, keeps header shading, and never splits a row
  across two pages. It prints only the rows the grid has drawn; the grid's own
  Print prints every row.

### Patch Changes

- bd78d43: The package manifests and READMEs now point at the repository's current home, `github.com/gridkitjs/gridkitjs`.

## 0.8.1

### Patch Changes
