- 84c51ec: Dropped the `.header-resize-grip` rules; no component has rendered that element, so the stylesheet is smaller with nothing visible changed.

## 0.8.0

### Minor Changes

- 22cf630: Styles for the grid's column chooser, in both palettes: `.gridkit-column-chooser`,
  the panel; `.column-chooser-search`; `.column-chooser-option`, a checkbox and
  its label, muted while disabled; `.column-chooser-all`, the "Show all"
  checkbox set apart from the list; `.column-chooser-list`, which scrolls inside
  itself past about ten columns; and `.column-chooser-empty`. Like the menus, the
  chooser renders into `document.body`, so these selectors are top-level.
- 183babc: Styles for the grid's menus, in both palettes: `.gridkit-overlay`, the box a
  menu opens in, above the grid; `.gridkit-menu` and its items (`.menu-item`,
  with `.menu-item-icon`, `.menu-item-label`, `.menu-item-shortcut` and
  `.menu-submenu-indicator`), focused, disabled, checked and expanded through
  their ARIA attributes; and `.menu-separator`. Overlays render into
  `document.body`, so these selectors are top-level.
- 5f9a5da: Styles for the grid's toolbar, in both palettes: `.gridkit-toolbar`, sticky
  to the grid's start edge so it stays in view while the tables scroll
  sideways; `.toolbar-button` (with `.toolbar-button-icon` and
  `.toolbar-button-indicator`), disabled, pressed and expanded through their
  ARIA attributes; `.toolbar-more`, `.toolbar-search`, `.toolbar-separator`,
  `.toolbar-spacer` and `.toolbar-custom`.

### Patch Changes

- 66c2815: A long-press on a header, cell or group row that opens the grid's context menu
  no longer also brings up iOS's own callout, or starts selecting the text under
  the finger on a touch screen.
- 66c2815: The toolbar's "More" button can no longer be cut off: the search box narrows to
  at most half a narrow toolbar's width, and when the search box and custom
  entries alone are still wider than the toolbar, "More" sticks to its end edge.

## 0.7.0

### Minor Changes

- bedd76c: `.grid-loading-cell`: styles `@gridkitjs/react`'s new `infiniteScroll` loading row — centered, muted text, matching the grand-total footer's own cell padding. The row is `aria-hidden` and outside `aria-rowcount`, so this is a purely visual cue.
- bedd76c: `.gridkit-data-grid-body`: the row area's scroll container, styled to honor `@gridkitjs/react`'s new `height` prop (`overflow-y: auto`, height driven by the prop or `auto` when it's unset). No `position: sticky` is added for the header or footer — splitting them into their own tables already keeps them out of the region that scrolls, so there's nothing to stick. Add your own CSS targeting `.gridkit-data-grid-header`/`.gridkit-data-grid-footer` for a divider or shadow at the seam.

## 0.6.0

### Minor Changes

- 6e8189b: Styles for aggregates (`@gridkitjs/react`'s new `aggregates` prop): `.group-aggregates`/`.group-aggregate` for a group header's inline subtotal (`groupAggregateDisplay: "inline"`), `.grid-group-summary-row`/`.grid-group-summary-cell` for a group's own summary row (`groupAggregateDisplay: "row"`), and `.grid-footer`/`.grid-footer-cell` for the grand-total footer — including each one's `borders-*` variants.
- 6e8189b: Styles for the built-in pager's numbered variant (`@gridkitjs/react`'s `pager.variant: "numbered"`): `.grid-pager-button[aria-current="page"]` for the active page, and `.grid-pager-ellipsis`.
- 6e8189b: Styles for the new built-in pager (`@gridkitjs/react`'s `paginated` prop): `.gridkit-grid-pager`, `.grid-pager-button`, `.grid-pager-status`, and `.grid-pager-page-size`.

## 0.5.0

### Minor Changes

- 388def3: Styles for dragging a header into the group-by bar and reordering its chips:
  drop indicators on chips, a dashed drag-target outline on the bar itself, a
  `not-allowed` cursor and muted outline for a header already in the group-by
  stack dragged back toward it, a grab cursor and drag ghost for chips, and an
  empty-bar placeholder shown only when at least one column is draggable into
  it.
- 388def3: Styles for `@gridkitjs/react`'s new row grouping: the group header row, its
  expand/collapse toggle, each groupable column header's group icon, and the
  group-by bar and its removable chips.

## 0.4.0

### Minor Changes

- a01c851: The stylesheet no longer registers its own `@custom-variant dark` — it now
  follows whatever `dark:` variant your app's own Tailwind build already
  resolves to, so it never conflicts with an app that configures its own
  (a class, a `data-` attribute, or anything else). Out of the box, with
  nothing customized, a grid now follows the OS `prefers-color-scheme`
  instead of a `.dark` class.

  To keep the previous class-toggle behavior, declare it yourself, same as any
  Tailwind v4 app would:

  ```css
  @import "tailwindcss";
  @custom-variant dark (&:where(.dark, .dark *));
  @import "@gridkitjs/theme-tailwind/styles.css";
  ```

  Also new: `.gridkit-light` / `.gridkit-dark`, which pin a grid to one palette
  regardless of the ambient `dark:` state. Put either on any ancestor of the
  grid, including the grid's own root, to force a single grid's theme
  independent of the app around it.

## 0.3.2

### Patch Changes

- 29f2c39: The last row's cells no longer draw a bottom border under `borders-horizontal` or `borders-all` — previously it rendered as a stray extra edge below the table.

## 0.3.1

### Patch Changes

- 26adc6f: Added multi-column stacked sorting. A header's sort toggle cycles a column
  through ascending, descending, and off; Shift-click adds or updates a column
  in the stack instead of replacing it, sorted in priority order. Configure
  with `sortableColumns` / `column.sortable`, seed with `defaultColumnSort`,
  and listen with `onColumnSortChange`.

## 0.3.0

### Minor Changes

- f30a2a9: A focus ring on the focused header or body cell, drawn in `--gridkit-accent`.
  The grid is one tab stop with the arrow keys moving within it, so the ring is
  the only sign of where that stop is.

  Two new hooks for the styles to target: `.gridkit-sr-only`, which hides the
  grid's live region visually while leaving it in the accessibility tree, and
  `.header-cell.is-reorderable` for the grab affordance — every header is
  focusable now, so a `tabindex` no longer picks out the ones that drag.

- 4a92413: Styles for a selected row, column or cell, on two new palette tokens:
  `--gridkit-selected`, and `--gridkit-selected-strong` for one that is also
  hovered — hover already claims `--gridkit-surface-muted`, so without a second
  token a selected row would lose its highlight under the pointer.

  New classes the stylesheet targets: `is-selected` on a row, header cell or body
  cell, and `selectable-rows` / `selectable-columns` / `selectable-cells` on the
  grid itself. The last three enable rather than disable, the opposite of
  `no-hover-*` — hover is on by default and selection is off, so each class
  follows its own default.

  A grid that opts into row or cell selection also stops its cells' text being
  drag-selected, or a Shift-click meant to take a range of rows would smear the
  browser's own highlight across every cell it crossed.

## 0.2.3

### Patch Changes

- a157b54: Fixed `borders="all"` still drawing a left-edge line on the first column. The table-level `box-shadow` meant to repaint that stripped edge didn't align with `border-collapse: collapse` and left a stray line behind; the outer left/right edges are now simply left unset on the first/last cell, with nothing repainting them.

## 0.2.2

### Patch Changes

- 7dcffc9: A column with `wrap` enabled now breaks a word longer than the column instead
  of overflowing it — `white-space: normal` alone only breaks at spaces, so a
  long unbroken token (a URL, a long identifier) previously spilled past the
  column's fixed width.

## 0.2.1

### Patch Changes

- 76c62b1: Fix the grid overflowing its viewport by 1px under `borders="all"`. The first
  column's left border had no neighbour to collapse with, so it added a pixel
  the width calculations didn't account for — under `resizeMode="fit"` this
  clipped the last column's border and, in narrow layouts, its content.

## 0.2.0

### Minor Changes

- 1e112a6: Styles the new `is-wrapped` state `@gridkitjs/react` adds for a column with
  `wrap.header`/`wrap.cells` set: `overflow: visible`, `text-overflow: clip`,
  and `white-space: normal` in place of the grid's default single-line
  ellipsis, on just that column's header and/or cells.

## 0.1.0

### Minor Changes

- 7f0645b: Styles for column reordering. A header being dragged goes half-opaque and a
  copy of it trails the pointer, while the gap the column would drop into takes
  an accent line — drawn on the leading edge of the column after the gap, or the
  trailing edge of the last one. A reorderable header also takes a `grab` cursor
  and stops its label being selected mid-drag.

docs.title: Aggregation
docs.description: The reducers underneath aggregates: grand totals and per-group subtotals.
docs.body:
`computeAggregates` reduces rows to one result per aggregate, and `withGroupAggregates` gives every group header in a grouped result its own subtotals. The [view pipeline](/docs/core/view) runs both under its `aggregates` option — the grand total over every filtered row as `view.grandTotal`, and each group's on its header. Reach for them directly to total rows outside a grid, or in a custom adapter.

An `AggregateState<Row>` is `readonly AggregateSpec<Row>[]`, each spec `{ columnId, fn, id?, alignment? }`: `fn` is a built-in reducer — `"sum"`, `"avg"`, `"min"`, `"max"`, `"count"` or `"countDistinct"` — or an `AggregateFn<Row>`, `(rows) => unknown`, and `id` tells apart two aggregates on one column. The results are an `AggregateResults`, a `ReadonlyMap<string, unknown>` keyed by each spec's `id`, or its `columnId` when it has none. See [aggregate functions](/docs/react/aggregate-functions#the-six-built-in-reducers) for what each built-in computes.

## Functions

| Function                                                                        | Type                         | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `computeAggregates(rows, specs, columns)`                                       | `AggregateResults`           | Every spec in `specs` reduced over the raw `rows`. A custom `fn` is called once with `rows` as they are. Of two specs with the same key, the later wins. Always a new `Map`, empty for no specs.                                                                                                       |
| `withGroupAggregates(displayRows, flatRows, groupBy, specs, columns, display?)` | `readonly DisplayRow<Row>[]` | `displayRows` — `groupRows`'s output — with each group header's `aggregates` computed over all of its leaf rows, found again in `flatRows`, the rows `groupRows` was given. Under `display: "row"` each group also gets a summary row after its last entry. Returns `displayRows` itself for no specs. |

Each group's subtotal is computed from its own leaf rows, not combined from its children's results, so a custom aggregate that does not combine — a median, say — is right at every level. A collapsed group still gets its subtotal, though its rows are not in `displayRows`.

`display` is a `GroupAggregateDisplay`, `"inline"` by default. A summary row is a `ResolvedGroupSummaryRow` — `{ kind: "group-summary", groupId, level, rowIndex, datasetIndex, aggregates }` — sharing its group's id and results. Rows are renumbered when summary rows are added.

```ts
import { computeAggregates } from "@gridkitjs/core";

const totals = computeAggregates(
  rows,
  [
    { columnId: "Amount", fn: "sum" },
    { columnId: "Amount", fn: "avg", id: "Amount.avg" },
  ],
  dataColumns,
);
totals.get("Amount"); // the sum
totals.get("Amount.avg"); // the mean
```

Format a result the way the grid does with [`formatAggregateValue`](/docs/core/column-definitions#formatting-values).

## In the React grid

The `aggregates` and `groupAggregateDisplay` props — see [aggregate functions](/docs/react/aggregate-functions).

## See also

- [Row grouping](/docs/core/grouping) for the group rows aggregates are computed over.
- [The view pipeline](/docs/core/view) for where aggregation runs.
- [Aggregate functions](/docs/react/aggregate-functions) for the React grid's props.

docs.title: Column definitions
docs.description: The column definition shape, formatting values as text, and inferring columns from row data.
docs.body:
`defineColumnsFromRows` inspects your row data and infers a type and alignment per field, one level into nested objects. Use it as a starting point, then override or extend individual columns.

## Column definition shape

| Prop               | Type                                                     | Description                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `field`            | `FieldPath<Row> \| string`                               | Path to this column's value, e.g. "Application.Id".                                                                                                                                                    |
| `id`               | `string`                                                 | Stable identity for sizing/order state. Defaults to field.                                                                                                                                             |
| `header`           | `string`                                                 | The column name as plain text. Shown when there is no headerTemplate, and used for announcements either way.                                                                                           |
| `headerTemplate`   | `Node \| (() => Node)`                                   | Header content, or a function returning it at render time.                                                                                                                                             |
| `cellTemplate`     | `(context: CellTemplateContext<Row>) => Node`            | Renders this column's cells in place of the formatted value.                                                                                                                                           |
| `footerTemplate`   | `(context: FooterTemplateContext<Row>) => Node`          | Renders this column's own aggregate result in a group header or the grand-total footer, in place of the formatted value. `FooterTemplateContext<Row>` is `{ value, rows }`.                            |
| `type`             | `ColumnType`                                             | The value type of this column's cells, e.g. "currency".                                                                                                                                                |
| `format`           | `Intl.NumberFormatOptions \| Intl.DateTimeFormatOptions` | Intl options for how values read as text — see Formatting values below.                                                                                                                                |
| `valueFormatter`   | `(value: unknown, row: Row \| undefined) => string`      | Turns a value into its text, in place of format and type. `row` is `undefined` for an aggregate or a group value.                                                                                      |
| `alignment`        | `"left" \| "center" \| "right"`                          | Alignment of this column's cells. Falls back to type.                                                                                                                                                  |
| `width`            | `number`                                                 | Width in px this column starts at.                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `minWidth`         | `number`                                                 | Lower bound a resize may not drag below.                                                                                                                                                               |
| `maxWidth`         | `number`                                                 | Upper bound a resize may not drag above.                                                                                                                                                               |
| `resizable`        | `boolean`                                                | Whether this column can be resized, overriding the grid-level default.                                                                                                                                 |
| `reorderable`      | `boolean`                                                | Whether this column can be dragged to a new position, overriding the grid-level default.                                                                                                               |
| `sortable`         | `boolean`                                                | Whether this column can be sorted, overriding the grid-level `sortableColumns`.                                                                                                                        |
| `filterable`       | `boolean`                                                | Whether this column has a filter menu, overriding the grid-level `filterableColumns`. See [filter menu options](/docs/core/filtering#filter-menu-options).                                             |
| `filterMenu`       | `{ ui?, operators? }`                                    | The column's own filter menu: its editor, `"simple"` or `"excel"`, over the grid's `filterMenu.ui`, and the operators its conditions offer.                                                            |
| `groupable`        | `boolean`                                                | Whether this column can be grouped by from its header, overriding the grid-level `groupableColumns`.                                                                                                   |
| `groupToggleIcon`  | `boolean`                                                | Whether a groupable header shows its group-toggle icon, overriding the grid-level default. Purely a rendering choice: the column stays groupable.                                                      |
| `groupByDraggable` | `boolean`                                                | Whether this column's header may be dragged into the group-by bar, overriding the grid-level default. Independent of `groupable`.                                                                      |
| `wrap`             | `{ header?, cells? }`                                    | Lets this column's header and/or cell text wrap onto multiple lines instead of truncating.                                                                                                             |
| `headerClassName`  | `string`                                                 | Extra class names appended to this column's th.                                                                                                                                                        |
| `cellClassName`    | `string`                                                 | Extra class names appended to this column's td, on every row.                                                                                                                                          |
| `hidden`           | `boolean`                                                | Whether the column starts out hidden. It still sorts, filters and groups; `columnVisibility` state overrides it. See [the view pipeline](/docs/core/view).                                             |
| `hideable`         | `boolean`                                                | Whether the user may hide the column — the built-in [`column.hide` command](/docs/core/commands#built-in-commands) and the column chooser honour it. Defaults to `true`; `hideColumns` still hides it. |
| `exportable`       | `boolean`                                                | Whether the column is written to an export, a clipboard copy or a print. Defaults to `true`; `false` keeps it out of all of them, even when an export names it by id. See [export](/docs/core/export). |
| `exportValue`      | `(value: unknown, row: Row) => ExportScalar`             | The typed value an export stores for a cell — a `string`, `number`, `boolean`, `Date` or `null` — where the raw value is not the one to keep. Text still comes from `formatCellValue`.                 |

## Formatting values

A column with no `cellTemplate` shows the text `formatCellValue` makes of its value, and its aggregates read the same way. Some values always read the same:

| Value                 | Text                                           |
| --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `null` / `undefined`  | Empty.                                         |
| boolean               | `"true"` / `"false"`, or the `messages` given. |
| string                | As-is.                                         |
| plain object or array | JSON.                                          |

Dates and numbers are formatted through `Intl` only once something asks for it: the column has a `format`, or a locale is passed (the grid's `locale` prop). Without either they print as they always have, so a grid upgraded without touching its columns shows exactly what it did:

| Value                    | Without `format` or locale                                                  | With `format` or locale                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Date`                   | `toLocaleString()` — date and time.                                         | `Intl.DateTimeFormat`: the date alone under `"date"`, the time alone under `"time"`, both otherwise.                                          |
| number, numeric `type`   | As-is — `1234.5`. An aggregate reads through `toLocaleString()`: `1,234.5`. | `Intl.NumberFormat`. `"currency"` shows a symbol once `format.currency` names one, else two fraction digits; `"percent"` reads `0.25` as 25%. |
| number, any other `type` | As-is — `1001`, not `1,001`.                                                | As-is.                                                                                                                                        |

`format` is passed to the `Intl` constructor with the locale. Number options are laid over the type's defaults, so `{ maximumFractionDigits: 0 }` on a currency column keeps the symbol; date options replace the defaults outright, since `dateStyle` cannot be combined with individual fields. A `valueFormatter` decides outright. A `count` or `countDistinct` aggregate is a number of rows, so it always reads as a plain number.

```ts
import { formatCellValue } from "@gridkitjs/core";

formatCellValue(
  1234.5,
  { field: "Price", type: "currency", format: { currency: "EUR" } },
  "de-DE",
);
// "1.234,50 €"
formatCellValue(new Date(2024, 2, 15), { field: "Due", type: "date" }, "en-GB");
// "15/03/2024"
formatCellValue(1234.5, { field: "Price", type: "number" });
// "1234.5" — no format, no locale
```

| Function                                                   | Type     | Description                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ---------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `formatCellValue(value, column, locale?, row?, messages?)` | `string` | The text a value reads as in `column` — the default cell rendering, and what an export writes. `messages` gives a boolean's words (`booleanTrue`/`booleanFalse`).                                       |
| `formatAggregateValue(value, spec, column, locale?)`       | `string` | The text an aggregate result reads as. Counts read as plain numbers; everything else as one of the column's values.                                                                                     |
| `formatGroupValue(value, column, locale, messages)`        | `string` | The text a group's own value reads as — a group header's name, and an export's group label. As the column's cells read it, except that `null`/`undefined` reads `messages.blankGroupValue` ("(blank)"). |

Formatters are built once per type, locale and `format` object and reused, so keep a column's `format` defined once rather than recreating it per render.

## Inferred columns

<DataGridBasicExample />

| Function                              | Type                               | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `defineColumnsFromRows(rows)`         | `readonly ColumnDefinition<Row>[]` | Infers a type and alignment per field, one level into nested objects.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `accessDotted(obj, path)`             | `unknown`                          | Reads a value at a dotted path, e.g. "Application.Id".                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `alignmentForType(type)`              | `ColumnAlignment`                  | Alignment a column type defaults to — "right" for numbers.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `resolveColumnLabel(column)`          | `Node \| string`                   | What a column's header shows: its headerTemplate, else header, else a label read off the field path.                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `resolveColumnHeaderText(column)`     | `string`                           | The column name as text: header, else a text label, else the field path — for announcements and export.                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `buildKeyShortcuts(capabilities)`     | `string`                           | The aria-keyshortcuts string for a column header, naming only the keys that column responds to. `capabilities` is a `KeyShortcutCapabilities`, `{ reorderable, resizable, sortable, groupable, filterable?, contextMenu? }` — Alt+Shift+ArrowDown too under `filterable: true`, Shift+F10 under `contextMenu: true`. |
| `getColumnId(column)`                 | `string`                           | The key a column's state is stored and rendered under — its `id`, else its `field`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `resolveRowId(row, index, getRowId?)` | `string`                           | The key a row's state is stored and rendered under — `getRowId(row, index)`, else the position as a string. A position follows a re-sort, so data that sorts, filters or pages needs a `getRowId`.                                                                                                                   |

## See also

- [Column definitions](/docs/react/column-definition) for the React grid's column props.
- [The view pipeline](/docs/core/view) for how the definitions become resolved columns.
- [Resizing](/docs/core/resizing) and [ordering](/docs/core/ordering) for the column layout.

docs.title: Commands and menus
docs.description: GridCommand, the one implementation behind a menu item, a toolbar button and the API: built-in and app commands, their context and the menu model.
docs.body:
A command is the one implementation behind a menu item, a toolbar button and a renderer's `runCommand` — "Sort ascending", "Hide column", "Clear filters". Whether it shows and whether it can run are predicates over a context, a snapshot of the grid taken where it was asked for, and it changes the grid only through the [controller](/docs/core/controller)'s actions, so a change made from a menu reports through the same callback as the user's own gesture would.

```ts
import {
  createCommandContext,
  createGridController,
  defaultMessages,
  resolveCommands,
  runCommand,
} from "@gridkitjs/core";

const controller = createGridController<Order>({
  dataSource: orders,
  columns,
  sortableColumns: true,
});
const commands = resolveCommands<Order>(undefined);

const context = createCommandContext({
  controller,
  target: { area: "header", columnId: "Amount" },
  messages: defaultMessages,
  host: {
    autoFitColumns() {},
    openPanel() {},
    announce() {},
    saveFile() {},
    writeClipboard() {},
    print() {},
  },
});

const sortAscending = commands.get("sort.ascending");
if (sortAscending !== undefined) {
  runCommand(sortAscending, context); // true — the grid now sorts by Amount
}
```

## Commands

A `GridCommand<Row>`:

| Field       | Type                            | Description                                                                                                                 |
| ----------- | ------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`        | `string`                        | `"sort.ascending"` for a built-in, or any id of your own. Never `"separator"`, which a menu reads as one.                   |
| `label`     | `string \| (context) => string` | What a menu item or toolbar button reads.                                                                                   |
| `icon`      | `string`                        | A key the renderer maps to an icon of its own. A key it does not know draws nothing.                                        |
| `shortcut`  | `string`                        | A key-combination hint in `aria-keyshortcuts` syntax, such as `"Alt+ArrowUp"` — shown, not bound.                           |
| `isVisible` | `(context) => boolean`          | Whether the command shows here at all. Defaults to always.                                                                  |
| `isEnabled` | `(context) => boolean`          | Whether it can run. A disabled command still shows, so a user can see what is not possible. Defaults to always.             |
| `isChecked` | `(context) => boolean`          | Present for a checkable command — a checkbox item in a menu, a toggle button in a toolbar — and says whether it is checked. |
| `execute`   | `(context) => void`             | What it does.                                                                                                               |

The predicates are asked whenever a menu or toolbar is resolved, so a command follows the grid's state without being told about it.

## Targets

A `GridCommandTarget` says where a command was asked for. A built-in reads the column, row or group it acts on from here.

| Target                                 | Where                                       |
| -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| `{ area: "header", columnId }`         | A column header.                            |
| `{ area: "cell", rowId, columnId }`    | A data cell.                                |
| `{ area: "group", groupId, columnId }` | A group header row.                         |
| `{ area: "body" }`                     | Empty body space, or a grid with no rows.   |
| `{ area: "toolbar", itemId }`          | A toolbar item.                             |
| `{ area: "grid" }`                     | A renderer's API, with no particular place. |

## The context

`createCommandContext({ controller, target, messages, host })` — a `GridCommandContextInput` — builds the `GridCommandContext<Row>` every predicate and `execute` receive, from the controller's state, view and options as they are now. `messages` is the grid's messages already laid over the defaults, as [`resolveMessages`](/docs/core#messages) returns them. The controller may be of any node type, so a renderer's `GridController<Row, ReactNode>` serves as it is.

| Field          | Type                                | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| -------------- | ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `target`       | `GridCommandTarget`                 | Where the command was asked for.                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `state`        | `GridState<Row>`                    | Every slice of state.                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `view`         | `GridView<Row, unknown>`            | What the user is looking at.                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `options`      | `GridOptions<Row>`                  | The grid's options.                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `messages`     | `GridMessages`                      | The grid's strings, which every built-in label reads.                                                                                                                                                          |
| `actions`      | `GridCommandActions<Row>`           | Every action of the controller — all of it but `getOptions`, `setOptions`, `subscribe`, `getState` and `getView`. The only way a command changes the grid.                                                     |
| `host`         | `GridCommandHost`                   | What only the renderer can do — see below.                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `row`          | `ResolvedRow<Row> \| null`          | The row a cell target is on; `null` on any other target, or for a row the filter hides.                                                                                                                        |
| `column`       | `DataColumn<Row, unknown> \| null`  | The column a header, cell or group target names, hidden or not; `null` on any other target.                                                                                                                    |
| `selectedRows` | `() => readonly ResolvedRow<Row>[]` | The selected rows that pass the filter, in the order they are shown, across every page and collapsed group. Worked out on first call and remembered: it walks every filtered row, and most commands never ask. |

A context is a snapshot. A renderer builds one each time it resolves a menu or a toolbar, so its commands see the state the user sees.

### The host

A `GridCommandHost` holds what a command needs that only a renderer has. A caller with no renderer — a test, a script in Node — passes members that do nothing.

| Member                      | Description                                                                                                                                                                     |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `autoFitColumns(columnIds)` | Sizes each column to fit its content, as double-clicking its resize handle does.                                                                                                |
| `openPanel(kind, target)`   | Opens one of the grid's [panels](#panels) anchored to the target. `kind` is a `GridPanelKind`: `"columnChooser"` or `"filter"`.                                                 |
| `announce(text)`            | Reads `text` out through the grid's live region.                                                                                                                                |
| `saveFile(file)`            | Saves an [`ExportFile`](/docs/core/export#exporting-a-file) — in a browser, a download. Given a promise of one, it waits for it, and reports a rejected one rather than saving. |
| `writeClipboard(content)`   | Puts a [`CopyContent`](/docs/core/export#copying) on the clipboard as text and HTML, and announces it — `messages.copied(count, unit)` — or `messages.copyFailed`.              |
| `print(document, options)`  | Puts a [`PrintDocument`](/docs/core/export#printing) on paper — in a browser, the print dialog — under the `PrintOptions` it was built with.                                    |

## Built-in commands

`builtInCommands<Row>()` returns the grid's own commands. Each acts on a column, a row, a group or the whole grid, and is hidden on a target that has none of what it needs — so any id can be listed in any menu without checks. Their labels come from [`messages`](/docs/react/localization#every-key), and their ids form the `BuiltInCommandId` type.

| Id                        | Shown for                  | Visible when                                         | Enabled when                              | Does                                                          | Label                 |
| ------------------------- | -------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------- |
| `sort.ascending`          | header                     | the column is sortable                               | always; checked while it sorts ascending  | Sorts by this column alone, ascending.                        | `sortAscending`       |
| `sort.descending`         | header                     | the column is sortable                               | always; checked while it sorts descending | Sorts by this column alone, descending.                       | `sortDescending`      |
| `sort.clear`              | header                     | the column is sortable                               | the column is sorted                      | `clearColumnSort`, keeping the rest of the sort.              | `clearSort`           |
| `sort.clearAll`           | grid, toolbar, header      | always                                               | anything is sorted                        | `setColumnSort([])`                                           | `clearAllSorting`     |
| `group.add`               | header                     | the column is groupable and not grouped              | always                                    | `toggleGroupBy`, adding it to the end of the grouping.        | `groupByColumn`       |
| `group.remove`            | header, group              | the column is grouped                                | always                                    | `toggleGroupBy`, taking it out of the grouping.               | `removeGroupBy`       |
| `group.clearAll`          | grid, toolbar              | anything is grouped                                  | always                                    | `setGroupBy([])`                                              | `ungroupAll`          |
| `group.expandAll`         | grid, toolbar, group, cell | anything is grouped                                  | always                                    | `expandAllGroups()`                                           | `expandAllGroups`     |
| `group.collapseAll`       | grid, toolbar, group, cell | anything is grouped                                  | always                                    | `collapseAllGroups()`                                         | `collapseAllGroups`   |
| `column.hide`             | header                     | the column is `hideable`                             | another column is shown                   | `hideColumns([id])`                                           | `hideColumn`          |
| `column.autoFit`          | header                     | the column is resizable                              | always                                    | `host.autoFitColumns([id])`                                   | `autoFitColumn`       |
| `column.autoFitAll`       | grid, toolbar, header      | any shown column is resizable                        | always                                    | `host.autoFitColumns(ids)` with every shown resizable column. | `autoFitAllColumns`   |
| `column.choose`           | grid, toolbar, header      | always                                               | always                                    | `host.openPanel("columnChooser", target)`                     | `chooseColumns`       |
| `filter.open`             | header                     | the column is filterable                             | always                                    | `host.openPanel("filter", target)`                            | `openFilter`          |
| `filter.clear`            | header                     | the column is filterable                             | the column is filtered                    | `setFilter` without any entry about the column.               | `clearColumnFilter`   |
| `selection.selectAllRows` | grid, cell                 | `selectable.rows` is `"multiple"`                    | there are rows                            | `selectAllRows()`                                             | `selectAllRows`       |
| `selection.clear`         | grid, cell, header         | rows, columns or cells are selectable                | anything is selected                      | `clearSelection()`                                            | `clearSelection`      |
| `filter.clearAll`         | grid, toolbar, header      | always                                               | anything filters                          | `setFilter([])`, which clears the search too.                 | `clearFilters`        |
| `export.csv`              | grid, toolbar, body, cell  | always                                               | there are rows                            | Saves the view as CSV through `host.saveFile`.                | `exportCsv`           |
| `export.json`             | grid, toolbar, body, cell  | always                                               | there are rows                            | Saves the view as JSON through `host.saveFile`.               | `exportJson`          |
| `export.xlsx`             | grid, toolbar, body, cell  | an `xlsx` writer is registered                       | there are rows                            | Saves the view with the `xlsx` writer.                        | `exportXlsx`          |
| `export.pdf`              | grid, toolbar, body, cell  | a `pdf` writer is registered                         | there are rows                            | Saves the view with the `pdf` writer.                         | `exportPdf`           |
| `exportSelection.csv`     | grid, toolbar, body, cell  | rows are selected                                    | a selected row passes the filter          | Saves the selected rows as CSV.                               | `exportSelectionCsv`  |
| `exportSelection.json`    | grid, toolbar, body, cell  | rows are selected                                    | a selected row passes the filter          | Saves the selected rows as JSON.                              | `exportSelectionJson` |
| `exportSelection.xlsx`    | grid, toolbar, body, cell  | rows are selected and an `xlsx` writer is registered | a selected row passes the filter          | Saves the selected rows with the `xlsx` writer.               | `exportSelectionXlsx` |
| `copy.cell`               | cell                       | always                                               | the column is shown and exportable        | Copies the cell through `host.writeClipboard`.                | `copyCell`            |
| `copy.row`                | cell                       | always                                               | a shown column is exportable              | Copies the row's shown, exportable cells, without a header.   | `copyRow`             |
| `copy.selection`          | grid, toolbar, body, cell  | rows, columns or cells are selectable                | anything selected would copy              | Copies the selected rows, else columns, else cell.            | `copySelection`       |
| `print`                   | grid, toolbar, body, cell  | always                                               | a column is shown                         | Prints the view through `host.print`.                         | `print`               |

"Sortable" is the column's `sortable`, else the grid's `sortableColumns`; "groupable" the same with `groupable` and `groupableColumns`; "filterable" the same with `filterable` and `filterableColumns` — see [filter menu options](/docs/core/filtering#filter-menu-options); "resizable" is the column as rendered, after `resizableColumns`. [`hideable`](/docs/core/column-definitions#column-definition-shape) defaults to `true` and, like `sortable`, gates only the user's ways to do it: `hideColumns` still hides a column that is not hideable.

The sorting, grouping, hiding, autofit, copy and print built-ins carry an `icon` key — a `BuiltInCommandIcon`: `sortAscending` and `sortDescending` on the two sorts, `group` on `group.add` and `group.remove`, `hide` on `column.hide`, `autoFit` on both autofits, `copy` on the three copies, and `print` on `print`. @gridkitjs/react draws each as an icon of its own; a command of yours may use the same keys to look like the built-ins, and a renderer of your own maps them to its icons or leaves them out.

The export built-ins write with the grid's [export writers](/docs/core/export#writers) — CSV and JSON built in, others registered through `exportWriters` — under its `export` defaults, as [`exportFile`](/docs/core/export#exporting-a-file) does, and hand the file to `host.saveFile`. The selection exports set `scope: "selection"` over those defaults. An export acts on the whole grid, so it shows wherever the grid as a whole is asked for, a cell's menu included. GridKit ships no PDF writer — the browser's print dialog saves a PDF — so `export.pdf` shows only for a `pdf` writer of your own — see [Save as PDF](/docs/react/printing#save-as-pdf) and [PDF in code](/docs/react/export#pdf).

The copy built-ins build their content with [`copyContent`](/docs/core/export#copying) — tab-separated text and an HTML table, read from the export model as an export is — and hand it to `host.writeClipboard`, which writes it and announces it. `copy.selection` copies what a selection holds, in order of precedence: the selected rows, else the selected columns, else the selected cell.

`print` builds a print document with [`exportPrintDocument`](/docs/core/export#printing-a-grid) under the grid's `print` defaults — the rows and columns an export would hold, titled with the grid's `label` unless the defaults give a `title` — and hands it to `host.print` with those defaults, for what the host adds itself, such as `styles`. It shows where the exports do, and is enabled while a column is shown: a grid with no rows still prints its header.

The id `layout.reset` is reserved for a built-in still to come.

## Panels

A panel is a small dialog a renderer opens beside where it was asked for — the column chooser, or a column's filter menu. A command opens one through `host.openPanel(kind, target)`, passing its own target along, so the renderer can anchor it: below a header, beside a toolbar button, or at the grid's corner for `{ area: "grid" }`. The renderer holds which panel is open, one at a time; core holds what each one shows.

### The column chooser

`column.choose` opens the column chooser: a checkbox for every data column in column order, hidden ones included, a search box narrowing the list, and a "Show all" checkbox over what the search shows. `resolveColumnChooser({ columns, visibility, search })` — a `ColumnChooserInput` — works out what it draws, and what "Show all" does:

```ts
import { resolveColumnChooser } from "@gridkitjs/core";

const { dataColumns } = controller.getView();
const { columnVisibility } = controller.getState();
const chooser = resolveColumnChooser({
  columns: dataColumns,
  visibility: columnVisibility,
  search: "date",
});

for (const entry of chooser.entries) {
  drawCheckbox(entry.label, entry.visible, entry.disabled, () =>
    entry.visible
      ? controller.hideColumns([entry.columnId])
      : controller.showColumns([entry.columnId]),
  );
}
const toggle = chooser.toggleAll;
drawShowAll(chooser.selectAll, toggle === null, () => {
  if (toggle?.visible === true) controller.showColumns(toggle.columnIds);
  if (toggle?.visible === false) controller.hideColumns(toggle.columnIds);
});
```

| Field       | Type                            | Description                                                                                                                                                              |
| ----------- | ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `entries`   | `readonly ColumnChooserEntry[]` | The columns whose header text contains `search`, ignoring case, in column order: `columnId`, `label` (the header text), `visible` and `disabled`.                        |
| `selectAll` | `SelectAllState`                | "Show all"'s state — `"checked"`, `"unchecked"` or `"mixed"` — over the entries whose column is `hideable`: a column the user cannot hide is always on, and not counted. |
| `toggleAll` | `ColumnChooserToggle \| null`   | What toggling "Show all" does — `{ visible, columnIds }`, the columns to show or to hide — or `null` when it can do nothing, for a disabled checkbox.                    |

The rules every chooser keeps:

- An entry is `disabled` — its checkbox cannot be unchecked — while its column shows and is either not `hideable` or the last column shown. A hidden column can always be shown, `hideable` or not.
- "Show all" shows every hidden column the search lists once any is hidden, and hides those it lists once none is. It never touches a column that is not `hideable`, and never hides the last column shown: when that is all that would be left, the first of them stays.
- Changes go through `showColumns` and `hideColumns`, so each reports through `onColumnVisibilityChange` like any other.

### The filter menu

`filter.open` opens a column's filter menu below its header: the column's sort commands, an editor for its filter, and buttons to clear the filter, cancel or apply. It shows only for a column that has a menu, as [`resolveColumnFilterMenu`](/docs/core/filtering#filter-menu-options) settles. `filter.clear` does what the menu's "Clear filter" does — takes every entry about the column out of the filter, whichever editor wrote it — and a renderer runs it, and the sort commands, with the source `"filterMenu"`, so `onCommand` hears them.

## App commands and overrides

`resolveCommands(commands)` returns every command a grid knows, keyed by id: the built-ins, then yours. A command of yours with a built-in's id replaces it, so every menu and toolbar listing that id gets your version — translated, gated by a privilege, or doing something else entirely — without being changed itself.

```ts
import { resolveCommands, type GridCommand } from "@gridkitjs/core";

const exportSelected: GridCommand<Order> = {
  id: "orders.exportSelected",
  label: "Export selected",
  isEnabled: (context) => context.selectedRows().length > 0,
  execute: (context) => {
    exportOrders(context.selectedRows().map((entry) => entry.row));
  },
};

// Replaces the built-in: only an administrator may hide columns.
const hideColumn: GridCommand<Order> = {
  id: "column.hide",
  label: ({ messages }) => messages.hideColumn,
  isVisible: ({ target, column }) =>
    target.area === "header" && column !== null && user.isAdmin,
  execute: ({ column, actions }) => {
    if (column !== null) {
      actions.hideColumns([column.id]);
    }
  },
};

const commands = resolveCommands([exportSelected, hideColumn]);
```

A command with the id `"separator"` is left out with a `console.error` — a menu reads that string as a separator.

`runCommand(command, context)` runs a command only when it is visible and enabled on the context's target, and returns whether it ran — so a renderer reports only a command that did something, and a call through the API cannot run one the grid's state no longer allows.

| Function                       | Type                                    | Description                                                                              |
| ------------------------------ | --------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `builtInCommands()`            | `readonly GridCommand<Row>[]`           | The grid's own commands, typed for your `Row`. Two calls build equal ones.               |
| `resolveCommands(commands)`    | `ReadonlyMap<string, GridCommand<Row>>` | The built-ins, then `commands`, keyed by id — yours replacing a built-in of the same id. |
| `createCommandContext(input)`  | `GridCommandContext<Row>`               | The context for one target, over the controller as it is now.                            |
| `runCommand(command, context)` | `boolean`                               | Runs the command when visible and enabled, and says whether it did.                      |

### On a grid

A grid takes its app commands through the `commands` option, which a renderer passes to `resolveCommands` — so the grid's menus list them by id, and a built-in's id replaced there is replaced in every menu:

```ts
<DataGrid
  columns={columns}
  dataSource={orders}
  commands={[exportSelected, hideColumn]}
  contextMenu={{ cell: ["orders.exportSelected", "separator", "selection.clear"] }}
  onCommand={({ commandId, target, source }) => track(commandId, source)}
/>
```

`onCommand` is called after a command runs, with a `GridCommandEvent` — and after an inline menu item runs, with that item's id. A hidden or disabled one, which does not run, is not reported.

| Field       | Type                                                  | Description                                                                                      |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `commandId` | `string`                                              | The command's id, or the inline item's.                                                          |
| `target`    | `GridCommandTarget`                                   | Where it was asked for — `{ area: "grid" }` for a call through the API with none.                |
| `source`    | `"contextMenu" \| "toolbar" \| "api" \| "filterMenu"` | A `GridCommandSource`: a context menu, the toolbar, a renderer's API, or a column's filter menu. |

## Menus

A menu is a list of `MenuEntry<Row>`s, the one vocabulary every grid menu and [toolbar](/docs/core/toolbar) is written in:

| Entry                                      | Description                                                                                                            |
| ------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `"sort.ascending"`                         | A command id — a built-in's or one of yours. Typed as `BuiltInCommandId` or any string, so the built-ins autocomplete. |
| `"separator"`                              | A separator.                                                                                                           |
| `{ type: "item", id, label, onSelect, … }` | A `MenuItemEntry`: an item written into this menu alone rather than registered as a command.                           |
| `{ type: "submenu", id, label, items }`    | A `MenuSubmenuEntry`: an item that opens a menu of its own.                                                            |

An inline item has a command's fields under the names a menu reads naturally: `label`, `icon` and `shortcut`; `hidden`, `disabled` and `checked`, each a boolean or a function of the context, with `checked` present only on a checkable item; and `onSelect(context)` in place of `execute`. A submenu has a `label`, an optional `icon` and its `items`.

```ts
import { resolveMenu, type MenuEntry } from "@gridkitjs/core";

const headerMenu: readonly MenuEntry<Order>[] = [
  "sort.ascending",
  "sort.descending",
  "sort.clear",
  "separator",
  {
    type: "submenu",
    id: "grouping",
    label: "Grouping",
    items: ["group.add", "group.remove", "group.clearAll"],
  },
  "separator",
  {
    type: "item",
    id: "orders.pin",
    label: "Pin column",
    checked: ({ column }) => column !== null && pinned.has(column.id),
    onSelect: ({ column }) => {
      if (column !== null) {
        togglePin(column.id);
      }
    },
  },
];

const entries = resolveMenu(headerMenu, { commands, context });
```

`resolveMenu(entries, { commands, context })` — a `MenuResolveOptions` — resolves a menu against the grid as the context sees it, and returns the `ResolvedMenuEntry[]` a renderer draws:

- A command id becomes its command's item. A hidden command or inline item is left out, and so is an id naming no command, reported once per command map with a `console.error`.
- Labels become strings and flags booleans; `checked` stays `undefined` for an item that is not checkable.
- A submenu is resolved the same way, and left out when nothing in it shows.
- Separators never lead, trail or sit next to another, however the items around them came and went.

An empty result means there is nothing to show, so a renderer shows no grid menu there.

| Resolved entry          | Fields                                                                                                                |
| ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ResolvedMenuItem`      | `type: "item"`, `id`, `label`, `icon`, `shortcut`, `disabled`, `checked` (`boolean \| undefined`), `run()`            |
| `ResolvedMenuSubmenu`   | `type: "submenu"`, `id`, `label`, `icon`, `items` — never empty                                                       |
| `ResolvedMenuSeparator` | `type: "separator"`, `key` — the separator's place among the entries it came from, unique among its menu's separators |

`run()` runs an item against the context its menu was resolved in — a command through `runCommand`, so only while it is visible and enabled; an inline item unless it is disabled — and returns whether it ran.

## Context menus

A grid's `contextMenu` option — `boolean | GridContextMenuOptions<Row>` — says which context menus it shows, by area. It is off by default, leaving the browser's menu. `true` shows each area's defaults; an object gives an area's entries in the menu vocabulary above — or a function working them out, below — an area left out keeping its defaults and `[]` leaving the browser's menu there.

| Area     | Where                                                       | Target                                 |
| -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `header` | A column header.                                            | `{ area: "header", columnId }`         |
| `cell`   | A data cell — a menu for its row and cell.                  | `{ area: "cell", rowId, columnId }`    |
| `group`  | A group header row.                                         | `{ area: "group", groupId, columnId }` |
| `body`   | The body's empty space, below the last row or with no rows. | `{ area: "body" }`                     |

A `GridContextMenuTarget` is a command target in one of these areas.

```ts
<DataGrid
  columns={columns}
  dataSource={orders}
  sortableColumns
  contextMenu={{
    header: ["sort.ascending", "sort.descending", "separator", "column.hide"],
    cell: ["selection.selectAllRows", "selection.clear"],
  }}
/>
```

`defaultContextMenu` holds each area's defaults — each item hidden where it has nothing to act on, and the separators collapsing around what is left:

| Area     | Defaults                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `header` | `sort.ascending`, `sort.descending`, `sort.clear`, a separator, `filter.open`, `filter.clear`, a separator, `group.add`, `group.remove`, a separator, `column.autoFit`, `column.autoFitAll`, a separator, `column.hide` and `column.choose`. |
| `cell`   | `copy.cell`, `copy.row`, `copy.selection`, a separator, `selection.selectAllRows`, `selection.clear`, a separator, `group.expandAll` and `group.collapseAll`.                                                                                |
| `group`  | `group.expandAll`, `group.collapseAll`, a separator and `group.remove` — which stops grouping by the row's column.                                                                                                                           |
| `body`   | None: empty space keeps the browser's menu until the grid lists entries for it.                                                                                                                                                              |

An area takes a `GridContextMenuEntries<Row, Area>`: its entries, or a function asked each time its menu opens with a `GridContextMenuRequest<Row, Area>` and returning the entries to show — or `null`, like `[]`, for no grid menu there.

| Field      | Type                          | Description                                                                                    |
| ---------- | ----------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `target`   | `GridContextMenuTarget<Area>` | Where the menu opens, typed for the area: a header's carries `columnId`, a cell's `rowId` too. |
| `defaults` | `readonly MenuEntry<Row>[]`   | The area's defaults, to keep, trim, reorder or add to.                                         |
| `context`  | `GridCommandContext<Row>`     | The grid as the menu sees it — the context its items resolve and run in.                       |

```ts
contextMenu={{
  cell: ({ target, defaults, context }) =>
    target.columnId === "Id"
      ? null
      : [
          { type: "item", id: "orders.open", label: "Open", onSelect: ({ row }) => open(row) },
          "separator",
          ...defaults,
        ],
}}
```

For a renderer of your own, two functions read the option:

| Function                                   | Type                        | Description                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ------------------------------------------ | --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `contextMenuEntries(contextMenu, context)` | `readonly MenuEntry<Row>[]` | The entries the option gives the place `context.target` names — asking the area's function, if it has one — for `resolveMenu` to resolve in the same context. None for a target outside the four areas. |
| `hasContextMenu(contextMenu, area)`        | `boolean`                   | Whether the option opens a grid menu on `area` at all: it is on, and the area has entries or a function rather than `[]`. For an `aria-keyshortcuts` that lists `Shift+F10`.                            |

No entries, or none left once resolved, means no grid menu there: the renderer leaves the browser's.

```ts
import {
  contextMenuEntries,
  createCommandContext,
  resolveMenu,
} from "@gridkitjs/core";

const context = createCommandContext({
  controller,
  target: { area: "header", columnId },
  messages,
  host,
});
const entries = resolveMenu(
  contextMenuEntries(controller.getOptions().contextMenu, context),
  { commands, context },
);
if (entries.length > 0) {
  event.preventDefault();
  showMenu(entries);
}
```

`onContextMenuOpenChange` is called as a grid's context menu opens and closes, with a `ContextMenuOpenChangeEvent` — `{ open, target }`, where the menu opened or where the one closing had. A menu opened in place of another reports that one closing first. The open state itself is the renderer's: no option holds it.

@gridkitjs/react draws them and opens them for you — see its [context menu](/docs/react/context-menu).

## Keyboard

Grid menus follow the [WAI-ARIA menu pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menubar/). A disabled item stays focusable, so a screen reader can find it, and does nothing when activated; a checkable item is a `menuitemcheckbox` with `aria-checked`.

| Key                                              | Does                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| <Kbd>ArrowDown</Kbd> / <Kbd>ArrowUp</Kbd>        | The next or previous item, wrapping round the ends and skipping separators.                  |
| <Kbd>Home</Kbd> / <Kbd>End</Kbd>                 | The first or last item.                                                                      |
| <Kbd>Enter</Kbd> / <Kbd>Space</Kbd>              | Runs the item and closes every menu; on a submenu item, opens it and focuses its first item. |
| <Kbd>ArrowRight</Kbd>                            | On a submenu item, opens it and focuses its first item.                                      |
| <Kbd>ArrowLeft</Kbd>                             | In a submenu, closes it and focuses the item that opened it.                                 |
| <Kbd>Escape</Kbd>                                | Closes the current menu only; focus goes back one level.                                     |
| <Kbd>Tab</Kbd> / <Kbd>Shift</Kbd>+<Kbd>Tab</Kbd> | Closes every menu; focus returns to where the menu was opened from.                          |
| A printable character                            | Typeahead: the next item whose label starts with what was typed.                             |

Hovering over an item moves focus to it, and hovering over a submenu item opens it after a short delay.

The two decisions those keys need are pure, and live here; the behaviour that holds a menu's focus — @gridkitjs/dom's [`attachMenu`](/docs/dom/menus-and-toolbar#menu) — calls them:

| Function                              | Type     | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `nextMenuIndex(entries, from, move)`  | `number` | The item focus moves to from index `from`, `-1` for none. `move` is a `MenuMove`: `"next"`, `"previous"`, `"first"` or `"last"`. Skips separators, wraps round the ends and counts disabled items; `-1` when there is no item.                                                                                           |
| `typeaheadIndex(labels, from, query)` | `number` | The item `query` picks, matched case-insensitively against the start of each label, wrapping. One letter, or one letter typed again and again, searches from the item after `from`, so repeating it steps through every item it starts; a longer query keeps the focused item while it still matches. `-1` for no match. |

## See also

- [Toolbar](/docs/core/toolbar) for the toolbar's resolved items.
- [Context menu](/docs/react/context-menu) and [toolbar](/docs/react/toolbar) for the React components that show them.
- [Export](/docs/core/export) for the export and print commands.

docs.title: Controller
docs.description: createGridController: a grid's state, view and actions, without a renderer.
docs.body:
`createGridController` is a whole grid minus the drawing. It holds the grid's state, derives the view from it with [resolveGridView](/docs/core/view), and carries every action a user can take — sorting, filtering, row grouping, expanding, pagination, resizing, reordering, hiding columns, selecting. @gridkitjs/react's DataGrid creates one per grid, hands it its props on every render, draws its view and calls its actions from event handlers; a renderer for another framework does the same, so none of them decides anything the user can see.

```ts
import { createGridController } from "@gridkitjs/core";

const controller = createGridController<Row>({
  dataSource: rows,
  getRowId: (row) => String(row.Id),
  columns,
  paginated: true,
  onColumnSortChange: (event) => console.log(event.sort),
});

controller.subscribe(() => draw(controller.getView()));

controller.toggleColumnSort("Amount"); // ascending; draw() runs, then the callback above
controller.nextPage();
controller.getState().pagination; // { pageIndex: 1, pageSize: 25 }
```

## Options

createGridController takes a `GridControllerOptions<Row, Node>`: every [`GridOptions`](/docs/core#grid-options) field and selection callback — `SelectionCallbacks<Row, Node>`, the thirteen of `onRowSelect`, `onRowSelectionChange` and the rest — plus `columns` (inferred from `dataSource` when omitted or empty, as `defineColumnsFromRows` does) and `viewportWidth`, the width `resizeMode: "fit"` fills — `null` or absent where there is none, such as an export in Node — and `onSelectionDiff`, called after each row or column selection change with the ids it added and removed, including those with no row on screen, for a renderer's own feedback such as a live-region count.

`setOptions(options)` replaces them all, as a renderer does with its current props on each update. Calling it again with equal options changes nothing, so it is safe to call on every render. It does not call subscribers: the renderer calling it is already drawing the result.

## Controlled and uncontrolled state

Each slice of `GridState` is controlled or not on its own, the way a form input is. Leave the slice's option out and the controller keeps the slice itself, starting from its default. Give the option and the controller shows exactly that value; an action then only asks for a change, through the slice's callback, and the change takes effect when the next `setOptions` carries it.

| Slice              | Controlled option  | Default                   | Callback                                                  |
| ------------------ | ------------------ | ------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `columnSizing`     | `columnSizing`     | `defaultColumnSizing`     | `onColumnResize`                                          |
| `columnOrder`      | `columnOrder`      | `defaultColumnOrder`      | `onColumnOrderChange`                                     |
| `columnVisibility` | `columnVisibility` | `defaultColumnVisibility` | `onColumnVisibilityChange`                                |
| `filter`           | `filter`           | `defaultFilter`           | `onFilterChange`                                          |
| `rowSelection`     | `rowSelection`     | `defaultRowSelection`     | `onRowSelectionChange` and the other row callbacks        |
| `columnSelection`  | `columnSelection`  | `defaultColumnSelection`  | `onColumnSelectionChange` and the other column callbacks  |
| `cellSelection`    | `cellSelection`    | `defaultCellSelection`    | `onCellSelectionChange`, `onCellSelect`, `onCellDeselect` |
| `columnSort`       | `columnSort`       | `defaultColumnSort`       | `onColumnSortChange`                                      |
| `groupBy`          | `groupBy`          | `defaultGroupBy`          | `onGroupByChange`                                         |
| `groupExpansion`   | `groupExpansion`   | `defaultGroupExpansion`   | `onGroupExpansionChange`                                  |
| `pagination`       | `pagination`       | `defaultPagination`       | `onPaginationChange`                                      |

Giving both the controlled option and its default reports a `console.error` once; the controlled value wins.

A change to the filter, the sort or the grouping sends an uncontrolled pagination back to the first page, so a user is never left on a page the change emptied. That reset reports nothing of its own — the change that caused it already did. A controlled pagination is the caller's to reset; until it is, the view shows the last page that exists.

## Reading

| Method          | Type                               | Description                                                                                                          |
| --------------- | ---------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `getState()`    | `GridState<Row>`                   | Every slice as the grid applies it — the controlled value where one is given. The same object until a slice changes. |
| `getView()`     | `GridView<Row, Node>`              | What the user is looking at. The same object until something in it changes.                                          |
| `getOptions()`  | `GridControllerOptions<Row, Node>` | The options last given.                                                                                              |
| `subscribe(fn)` | `() => void`                       | Calls `fn` after every action that changed something, synchronously. Returns the unsubscribe function.               |

Because both snapshots keep their identity until something changes, either can serve as the snapshot of a subscription that compares by reference — React's `useSyncExternalStore`, an Angular signal, a Svelte store.

## Actions

Every action works out the next value, stops if it is the value the slice already holds, keeps it unless the slice is controlled, fires the slice's callback with the same payload a user's interaction fires, then calls the subscribers.

| Action                                                             | Callback                   | Description                                                                                                                                |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
