| `resizeColumn(columnId, width, phase)`                             | `onColumnResize`           | Sets one column's width, as a drag does: `"move"` while it lasts, `"end"` once. Never skipped for an unchanged width.                      |
| `cancelColumnResize(columnId, startSizing, startWidth)`            | `onColumnResize`           | Puts a column back as it was when a resize began, keeping other columns' changes, reported as the `"end"` at `startWidth`.                 |
| `setColumnSizing(sizing)`                                          | `onColumnResize`           | Replaces the widths, reported as the `"end"` of a resize of the first column that changed.                                                 |
| `moveColumn(columnId, beforeId)`                                   | `onColumnOrderChange`      | Moves a column in front of another, or to the end for `null`. Hidden columns keep their place.                                             |
| `setColumnOrder(order)`                                            | `onColumnOrderChange`      | Replaces the order, naming the first column whose position changed.                                                                        |
| `showColumns(ids)` / `hideColumns(ids)`                            | `onColumnVisibilityChange` | One report per call, naming every column it touched in display order.                                                                      |
| `setColumnVisibility(visibility)`                                  | `onColumnVisibilityChange` | Replaces the visibility state.                                                                                                             |
| `setFilter(filter)`                                                | `onFilterChange`           | Replaces the filter.                                                                                                                       |
| `selectRow(rowId, intent)`                                         | row callbacks              | One click or key press — `"replace"`, `"toggle"` or `"range"` from the last non-range selection, across the data rows on the current page. |
| `selectRows(rowIds, intent?)`                                      | row callbacks              | Selects rows as a user could, within `selectable.rows`: `"replace"` (only the last id under `"single"`) or `"toggle"`.                     |
| `selectAllRows()`                                                  | row callbacks              | Every data row on the current page, under `"multiple"`.                                                                                    |
| `setRowSelection(selection)`                                       | row callbacks              | Replaces the selected ids as given.                                                                                                        |
| `selectColumn(columnId, intent)` / `setColumnSelection(selection)` | column callbacks           | The same, for the columns as rendered.                                                                                                     |
| `selectCell(cell, intent)` / `setCellSelection(selection)`         | cell callbacks             | Selects a cell, or lets go of it on `"toggle"`; or replaces it, `null` for none.                                                           |
| `clearSelection()`                                                 | all three                  | Lets go of every row, column and cell selection, as <Kbd>Escape</Kbd> does.                                                                |
| `toggleColumnSort(columnId, { stack? })`                           | `onColumnSortChange`       | Cycles a column ascending → descending → off. `stack` adds it to the sort instead of replacing it.                                         |
| `clearColumnSort(columnId)`                                        | `onColumnSortChange`       | Takes one column out of the sort, keeping the rest, and names that column — even when it was the first key.                                |
| `setColumnSort(sort)`                                              | `onColumnSortChange`       | Replaces the sort, naming the first column whose place or direction changed.                                                               |
| `toggleGroupBy(columnId)`                                          | `onGroupByChange`          | Adds a column to the end of the group-by stack, or removes it.                                                                             |
| `moveGroupBy(columnId, beforeColumnId)`                            | `onGroupByChange`          | Puts a column in front of another in the stack, or at the end for `null`.                                                                  |
| `setGroupBy(groupBy)`                                              | `onGroupByChange`          | Replaces the stack, naming the first level that changed.                                                                                   |
| `toggleGroupExpansion(groupId)`                                    | `onGroupExpansionChange`   | Collapses an expanded group, or expands a collapsed one.                                                                                   |
| `expandAllGroups()` / `collapseAllGroups()`                        | `onGroupExpansionChange`   | Every group at once, reported with `groupId: null`.                                                                                        |
| `setGroupExpansion(expansion)`                                     | `onGroupExpansionChange`   | Replaces the collapsed groups, reported with `groupId: null`.                                                                              |
| `goToPage(pageIndex)`                                              | `onPaginationChange`       | Moves to a page, clamped into range.                                                                                                       |
| `nextPage()` / `previousPage()`                                    | `onPaginationChange`       | One page on or back.                                                                                                                       |
| `setPageSize(pageSize)`                                            | `onPaginationChange`       | Changes the page size and goes back to the first page.                                                                                     |
| `setPagination(pagination)`                                        | `onPaginationChange`       | Replaces the page and page size as given.                                                                                                  |

Every `set*` action also stops for a value equal to the current one, so setting what is already there reports nothing. The page actions do the same: `nextPage()` on the last page, `previousPage()` on the first, `goToPage()` to the page already shown (or one that clamps to it) and `setPageSize()` with the current size on the first page leave the pagination as it is, so they neither fire `onPaginationChange` nor call subscribers.

## Saving and restoring state

`restoreState(saved)` puts back state read earlier with `getState()`. Every slice it is given is set as its own `set*` action would set it — each one that changes fires its callback, and a controlled one only asks — while slices left out keep their value. Subscribers are called once, after every slice is in place, and a restored pagination is kept even when the same call changed the sort, filter or grouping.

`getState()` holds plain data except in the filter, where a `Date` value does not survive JSON and a predicate entry is a function. `serializeGridState(state)` returns a `SerializedGridState<Row>`, state that does survive it: a `Date` becomes its ISO string, which `restoreState` turns back into a `Date` — in a value entry always, in an operator entry when its column is a date, date-time or time column — and a predicate entry is left out with a `console.error` naming its column — along with any group it leaves empty.

```ts
import { serializeGridState } from "@gridkitjs/core";

localStorage.setItem(
  "orders-grid",
  JSON.stringify(serializeGridState(controller.getState())),
);

const stored = localStorage.getItem("orders-grid");
if (stored !== null) {
  controller.restoreState(JSON.parse(stored));
}
```

A saved state may be partial — `{ columnSizing, columnOrder, columnVisibility }` restores a column layout and leaves the sort, filter and selection alone.

## See also

- [Controlled and uncontrolled state](/docs/react/state) for the React grid's view of the same slices.
- [The view pipeline](/docs/core/view) for how the controller's state becomes rows and columns.
- [Imperative handle](/docs/react/imperative-handle) for the controller's surface on the React grid.

docs.title: Export
docs.description: buildExportTable: the grid's view as data — columns, typed and formatted cells, group and aggregate rows — for any export format.
docs.body:
`buildExportTable` turns what the grid shows into an `ExportTable`: the columns, every row as typed and formatted cells, the group header and aggregate rows, and the grand total. Every export format, the clipboard and print are written from this one model, and it is built from the grid's view and state rather than from the page, so rows that are virtualised, on another page or inside a collapsed group still export, and no two outputs can disagree. ```ts import { buildExportTable, createGridController, defaultMessages, } from "@gridkitjs/core"; const controller = createGridController({ dataSource: rows, columns }); const table = buildExportTable({ view: controller.getView(), state: controller.getState(), options: controller.getOptions(), messages: defaultMessages, }); table.columns.map((column) => column.header); // ["Name", "Region", "Amount"] table.rows[0]; // { kind: "data", rowId: "0", cells: [{ value: 1234.5, text: "1234.5" }, …] } ``` A command's `GridCommandContext` already has every field the source needs, so a command passes its context as it is: `buildExportTable(context, { scope: "selection" })`. ## What an export holds By default, what the user sees, minus what only hides it: - **Rows:** every row the filter, search and sort leave, in sorted order, across every page. - **Groups:** in a grouped grid, a header row per group, and every group expanded whatever its state on screen. Each group's rows follow its header, as on screen. - **Columns:** the visible columns in their current order. A column with `exportable: false` is always left out. - **Cells:** the text `formatCellValue` makes of each value — the column's `format`, `valueFormatter` and the grid's `locale` all apply, so the export reads as the screen does — beside a typed value for formats that keep types. - **Aggregates:** a group's aggregates where the grid shows them — under their columns in the group's header row for `groupAggregateDisplay: "inline"`, or in a summary row after the group for `"row"` — and the grand total as the footer. Groups, subtotals and the total are worked out from the exported rows, not copied from the screen, so under `scope: "selection"` a group counts and totals only the selected rows in it. ## Options The second argument, an `ExportOptions`, narrows the export. Every field is optional. | Option | Type | Default | Description | | ------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `scope` | `"all" \| "page" \| "selection"` | `"all"` | Which rows: every page, the data rows on the current page, or the selected rows the filter leaves. | | `columns` | `"visible" \| "all" \| readonly string[]` | `"visible"` | Which columns: those shown, every column including hidden ones, or a list of column ids in the order given. An id the grid does not have is skipped. | | `includeGroups` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether a grouped grid writes its group header rows. `false` keeps the rows in grouped order without the headers. | | `includeAggregates` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether group aggregates, summary rows and the grand total are written. | | `includeHeader` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether a header row of column names leads the output. Sets `ExportTable.header`, which every format reads. | ## The model `ExportTable` is `{ columns, header, rows, footer }`. Every row has one cell per column, in the order of `columns`. | Type | Shape | Description | | ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `ExportColumn` | `{ id, header, type, format?, alignment, width }` | `header` is the column's name as text (`resolveColumnHeaderText`), never header markup. `type` is `"string"` when the column has none. `width` is as rendered, or as a hidden column would start. | | `ExportCell` | `{ value, text }` | `text` is what the grid shows. `value` is an `ExportScalar` — `string \| number \| boolean \| Date \| null` — for a format that stores types, such as a spreadsheet. | | `ExportRow` | `ExportDataRow \| ExportGroupRow \| ExportGroupSummaryRow` | A body row. Discriminate on `kind`. | | `ExportDataRow` | `{ kind: "data", rowId, cells }` | One row of data. | | `ExportGroupRow` | `{ kind: "group", level, groupId, label, count, cells }` | A group header. `label` reads `"Region: West"`, a missing value as `messages.blankGroupValue`. `count` is the data rows under it, at every depth. `cells` hold its aggregates when shown inline. | | `ExportGroupSummaryRow` | `{ kind: "groupSummary", level, cells }` | A group's aggregates as a row of their own, under `groupAggregateDisplay: "row"`. | | `ExportTotalRow` | `{ kind: "total", cells }` | The grand total, in `footer` — `null` when there are no aggregates. | A cell's `value` is the column's `exportValue(value, row)` when it has one, else the raw value when it is a string, number, boolean or `Date`. A missing value is `null`, and anything else — an object, an array — is stored as its text, so no writer ever meets a value it cannot represent. An aggregate cell's text is empty for an empty result rather than the dash the grid shows, and two aggregates on one column share the cell, comma-separated, as they do in the grid's footer. ```ts const columns: readonly ColumnDefinition[] = [ { field: "Name" }, { field: "CustomerId", header: "Customer", valueFormatter: (id) => customerNames.get(String(id)) ?? "", exportValue: (id) => customerNames.get(String(id)) ?? null, }, { field: "Id", id: "Actions", exportable: false, cellTemplate: renderActions, }, ]; ``` ## Source The first argument is an `ExportSource`, the few fields of the grid an export reads: | Field | Type | Description | | ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `view` | `GridView` | The view, from `resolveGridView` or a controller's `getView()`. | | `state` | `{ groupBy, rowSelection, columnSizing }` | Any `GridState` serves. | | `options` | `{ locale?, aggregates?, groupAggregateDisplay?, columnSizeDefaults? }` | Any `GridOptions` serves. | | `messages` | `{ booleanTrue, booleanFalse, blankGroupValue }` | The words for booleans and a blank group — any `GridMessages`, such as `defaultMessages`. | | Function | Type | Description | | ------------------------------------ | ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | | `buildExportTable(source, options?)` | `ExportTable` | The grid's view as an export model, narrowed by `options`. | ## Writing it out A serialiser turns an `ExportTable` into the text of one format. Each returns a `string` rather than a file, so core needs no browser: making a `Blob` of it and saving or copying it is the renderer's job. ```ts import { buildExportTable, toCsv } from "@gridkitjs/core"; const table = buildExportTable(source); const csv = toCsv(table, { delimiter: "auto", locale: "mk" }); const blob = new Blob([csv], { type: "text/csv;charset=utf-8" }); ``` | Function | Returns | Description | | ------------------------------ | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `toCsv(table, options?)` | `string` | A CSV file a spreadsheet opens as it is, guarded against formula injection. | | `toTsv(table, options?)` | `string` | Tab-separated text, the plain-text form the clipboard carries. | | `toJson(table, options?)` | `string` | The data rows as an array of objects with typed values. | | `toHtmlTable(table, options?)` | `string` | A ``, escaped, for pasting into a spreadsheet or a document. | The delimited formats lay the rows out the same way: the header row when `table.header` is `true`, then every body row, then the footer. A group row writes its label, `"Region: West"`, in the first column and any inline aggregates under their own columns after it — an aggregate under the first column gives way to the label there, and still appears in the footer. Summary rows and the footer write their aggregates under their columns and leave the rest empty. ## CSV `toCsv` quotes per RFC 4180: a field is quoted when it holds the delimiter, a `"` or a line break, and a `"` inside it is doubled, so a cell with a line break in it stays one cell. Records end with `"\r\n"`, and the last one has no line break after it. | Option | Type | Default | Description | | -------------------- | ----------------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `delimiter` | `string` | `","` | The field separator. `"auto"` picks `";"` when `locale` writes a decimal with a comma and `","` otherwise. | | `locale` | `FormatLocale` | — | The locale `delimiter: "auto"` reads — pass the grid's `locale`. The runtime's own when absent. | | `eol` | `string` | `"\r\n"` | What ends each record. | | `bom` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether the file starts with a UTF-8 byte order mark. | | `neutralizeFormulas` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether a field a spreadsheet would run as a formula gets a leading `'`. | | `values` | `"text" \| "raw"` | `"text"` | `"text"` writes each cell as the grid shows it; `"raw"` writes its typed value — numbers plain, dates in ISO 8601, booleans as `true` and `false`. | `"text"` makes a file that reads like the screen, with the column's `format` and the grid's `locale` applied: `1.234,50 €` rather than `1234.5`. Use `"raw"` for a file another program reads back, where a formatted number or a localised date would have to be parsed again. A CSV file has no header of its own saying how to read it, and spreadsheets guess. The defaults are chosen so that Excel, the usual reader, gets each guess right. - **Encoding.** Without a byte order mark, Excel reads a CSV in the system's legacy code page, so `Ćirilica`, `ш` or `€` arrive garbled. `bom: true` writes one; turn it off only for a program that does not expect it. - **Delimiter.** Excel splits a CSV on the system's list separator, which is `;` wherever a decimal is written with a comma — most of Europe, Macedonian and Croatian included. A comma-separated file opens there as one column. `delimiter: "auto"` with the user's `locale` writes `;` in those locales and `,` elsewhere. - **Formula injection.** A spreadsheet runs a field that starts with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` as a formula, and a leading tab or carriage return can hide such a start. A value a user typed into the data — `=HYPERLINK(…)`, or a call that runs a command — would then run on the machine of whoever opens the export. `neutralizeFormulas: true` writes such a field with a leading `'`, which the spreadsheet shows as text. A cell whose typed value is a number keeps a leading `-` or `+`, so `-5` stays a number; every other field, the header and group labels included, is guarded. ## TSV `toTsv` writes the table tab-separated with `"\n"` between records: the form a spreadsheet splits into cells when text is pasted into it, which is what a clipboard copy carries. There is no quoting a paste target agrees on, so a tab or line break inside a cell becomes a space. Unlike CSV it writes no byte order mark and leaves formulas alone: what is copied is exactly what the grid shows. Its one option is `values`, `"text"` or `"raw"`, as for CSV. ## JSON `toJson` writes the data rows as a JSON array of objects, one property per column holding the cell's typed value: a number stays a number, a boolean a boolean, a `Date` becomes its ISO 8601 string and a missing value `null`. Group headers, summary rows and the footer are left out — JSON is read by programs, which group and total for themselves. ```ts toJson(table, { space: 2 }); // [{ "Name": "Ana", "Amount": 1234.5, "Shipped": "2024-03-15T09:30:00.000Z" }, …] ``` | Option | Type | Default | Description | | ------- | ------------------ | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | `keys` | `"id" \| "header"` | `"id"` | What each property is named after: the column's id, which stays the same whatever the header says, or its header text. A repeated header is suffixed ` (2)`, ` (3)` and so on. | | `space` | `number \| string` | — | Indentation, as `JSON.stringify` takes it. None by default. | ## HTML table `toHtmlTable` writes the table as a `
` string: a `` of column names when `table.header` is `true`, every row in ``, and the grand total in ``. Every piece of text is HTML-escaped, so a cell holding `

docs.title: Filter state and the editor model
docs.description: The headless model a filter editor is drawn over (describeColumnFilter, columnValueOptions, filterEditorReducer) and the helpers behind a search box.
docs.body:
A grid's filter is one `FilterState` — entries ANDed together, described with every entry kind on [Column filtering](/docs/react/column-filtering). A filter editor, whether a list of conditions or an Excel-style checklist of values, is a UI over one column's part of that state. Core holds everything such an editor decides, so a renderer only draws it and every renderer's editor behaves the same:

1. `describeColumnFilter` reads which form the column's filter is in.
2. `columnValueOptions` lists the values a checklist offers.
3. `initialFilterEditorDraft` and `filterEditorReducer` hold the user's edits as a draft.
4. `draftToFilter` turns the draft into the next `FilterState` when the user applies it.

```ts
import {
  columnValueOptions,
  describeColumnFilter,
  draftToFilter,
  filterEditorReducer,
  initialFilterEditorDraft,
} from "@gridkitjs/core";

const { filter } = controller.getState();
const { dataColumns } = controller.getView();

// When the editor opens:
let draft = initialFilterEditorDraft(
  describeColumnFilter(filter, "Region"),
  columnValueOptions(rows, dataColumns, filter, "Region"),
);

// As the user works:
draft = filterEditorReducer(draft, { type: "search", search: "we" });
draft = filterEditorReducer(draft, { type: "toggleAll" });

// On apply (cancelling is just dropping the draft):
controller.setFilter(draftToFilter(draft, "Region", filter));
```

## A column's filter shape

`describeColumnFilter(filter, columnId)` returns a `ColumnFilterShape` — the one form an editor can show the column's filter in. Only entries **about the column** count: those naming it, and any group with such an entry anywhere inside. Entries about other columns and entries across every column (a global search) are someone else's.

| `kind`         | Holds                      | When the column's entries are…                                                                                   |
| -------------- | -------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `"none"`       | —                          | absent                                                                                                           |
| `"values"`     | `values`, `includeBlanks`  | one `in` entry, or one `"or"` group of an `in` and an `isEmpty` (`includeBlanks: true`)                          |
| `"conditions"` | `conditions`, `combinator` | one or two operator entries other than `in` — at the top level (`"and"`), or alone in one group (its combinator) |
| `"custom"`     | —                          | anything else: a text query, a predicate, a group reaching into another column, three conditions                 |

An editor shows a custom filter as such; applying its draft replaces it.

`isColumnFiltered(filter, columnId)` asks only whether that shape is anything but `"none"` — what a header reads to show its column as filtered. A global search filters every column alike, so it marks none.

## The values a checklist offers

`columnValueOptions(rows, dataColumns, filter, columnId, { search?, limit?, locale?, messages? })` lists the column's distinct values, each with its `label` and the `count` of rows holding it:

- **It cascades.** Values are counted over the rows that pass every entry _except_ those about this column, so one column's list narrows with the filters on the others, while its own pick never hides the values the user unchecked.
- Values are told apart as an `in` entry tells them apart — as [grouping](/docs/react/row-grouping) does, except that on a date, date-time or time column a date string and the `Date` it names are one value — ordered as the column sorts (`compareValues` under its `type`), and labelled as its cells print (`formatCellValue`, with the column's `format`, `valueFormatter` and the `locale` given).
- Pass the grid's own `messages` (a partial `GridMessages`, filled in from the defaults) so a boolean is labelled `booleanTrue`/`booleanFalse`, the same words its cells use. Without it, a boolean reads `"true"`/`"false"`. `search` matches those labels.
- Blank cells — `null`, `undefined` and `""` — are counted apart, in `blanks`. A cell holding an object or an array is not offered: an `in` entry can't hold it.
- `search` keeps the values whose label contains it, ignoring case; `total` is how many matched. `limit` cuts the list after that many, and `truncated` says it did.

`rows` are the grid's own rows, unfiltered — its `dataSource`. One call is a single pass over them: tens of milliseconds at 100k rows. Make it when the editor opens, not on every render, and hand the whole list to the draft, whose own search needs no recount.

## Caching the value lists

`createColumnValueOptionsCache()` remembers each column's list, so reopening a column's checklist doesn't count its values again. Hold one per grid and ask it in place of `columnValueOptions`:

```ts
import { createColumnValueOptionsCache } from "@gridkitjs/core";

const valueCache = createColumnValueOptionsCache<Order>();

// When a checklist opens:
const values = valueCache.get(rows, dataColumns, filter, "Region", {
  locale,
  messages,
});
```

`get(rows, dataColumns, filter, columnId, query?)` takes a `ColumnValueCacheQuery` — `{ locale?, messages? }` — and returns the column's whole list — no `search` or `limit`, which the draft applies — and hands back the very object it returned last time while nothing the list depends on has changed:

- the `rows` and `dataColumns`, by identity;
- the `locale` and `messages`, by identity — pass the grid's own, not an object made on each render;
- the filter's entries **not about the column**, one by one, by identity. `draftToFilter` keeps every entry it doesn't replace as it was, so applying one column's filter leaves its own list cached — a column's list never depends on its own entries — and the other columns' lists recount when they next open.

Each column keeps its latest list. New rows, columns, locale or messages drop every list, so the cache never holds on to rows the grid has let go of.

## The editor draft

`initialFilterEditorDraft(shape, values)` opens a `FilterEditorDraft` over a shape and the list from `columnValueOptions`. With no filter (or a custom one) every value is checked, the blanks too when there are any; a checklist opens with its own values checked, kept even when the other filters now hide them; conditions open as they are.

The draft keys its checked values the way the column's `in` entry matches them, using the `columnType` that `columnValueOptions` returns. So a saved checklist on a date column whose cells hold ISO strings, which `restoreState` reads back as `Date`s, opens with those dates checked.

`filterEditorReducer(draft, action)` is a plain reducer, so a renderer keeps the draft in whatever state it has — `useReducer`, a signal, a store:

| Action                                               | Does                                                                                                              |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `{ type: "search", search }`                         | Narrows the values shown; what is checked stays checked.                                                          |
| `{ type: "toggleValue", value }`                     | Checks or unchecks one value.                                                                                     |
| `{ type: "toggleAll" }`                              | Checks every value the search shows — or unchecks them, once all are. The blanks count while nothing is searched. |
| `{ type: "setIncludeBlanks", includeBlanks }`        | Checks or unchecks the blanks.                                                                                    |
| `{ type: "setConditions", conditions, combinator? }` | Replaces the conditions, keeping the combinator unless one is given.                                              |
| `{ type: "clear" }`                                  | Back to no filter: every value checked, no conditions, no search.                                                 |

A value or blanks action switches the draft to its checklist (`mode: "values"`); `setConditions` switches it to its conditions. `visibleFilterOptions(draft)` returns the values the search shows, and `selectAllState(draft)` the select-all checkbox's `"checked"`, `"unchecked"` or `"mixed"` over them.

## A checklist's window

`filterChecklist(draft, options)`, with `FilterChecklistOptions` — `{ valueLimit, blanksLabel }` — is the list a checklist editor draws under its search box and select-all — what each row says and whether it is checked:

```ts
import { filterChecklist } from "@gridkitjs/core";

// With `menu` from resolveColumnFilterMenu and the grid's resolved messages:
const { items, needsSearch, hiddenCount, total } = filterChecklist(draft, {
  valueLimit: menu.valueLimit,
  blanksLabel: messages.filterBlanks,
});
```

| Field         | Type                             | Description                                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------- | -------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `items`       | `readonly FilterChecklistItem[]` | The values the search shows, in sort order, cut to `valueLimit`; then the blanks, while nothing is searched and some cells are blank. Empty while `needsSearch`.     |
| `needsSearch` | `boolean`                        | The column holds more than `valueLimit` values and nothing is searched yet: show `filterSearchFirst(total)` — "Type to search 12,000 values" — in place of the list. |
| `hiddenCount` | `number`                         | How many of a search's matches `valueLimit` left out: show `filterMoreValues(hiddenCount)` — "250 more, refine the search". `0` while `needsSearch`.                 |
| `total`       | `number`                         | How many values the search matches — every value while nothing is searched. Blanks aside.                                                                            |

Each item is `{ kind, key, label, count, checked }`. A `kind: "value"` item carries its `value`, toggled with `{ type: "toggleValue", value }`; the `kind: "blanks"` item stands for the column's blank cells, labelled `blanksLabel`, and is toggled with `{ type: "setIncludeBlanks", includeBlanks: !checked }`. `key` tells the items apart: a value's is the key the draft checks it under, and the blanks have their own.

A column can hold far more values than a list is worth scrolling, so the list stops at `valueLimit` — 10,000 by default, Excel's own cap. Past that it waits for a search, while every value stays in the draft and select-all still checks or unchecks them all; a search matching more than `valueLimit` lists the first of its matches. `Infinity` lists everything.

The blanks item comes last, as in Excel, and only while nothing is searched — exactly when select-all counts the blanks, so the checkbox acts on what the list shows.

## Applying a draft

`draftToFilter(draft, columnId, current)` returns `current` with the column's entries replaced by the draft's, in the place of the first one so the others keep their order:

- A checklist with **everything checked** is no filter: the column's entries are removed.
- A **partial pick** is one `in` entry, OR-grouped with an `isEmpty` when the blanks are checked.
- One condition is stored as itself, two or more as one group with the draft's combinator; no conditions is no filter.

What `draftToFilter` writes, `describeColumnFilter` reads back as the same shape. When nothing changes it returns `current` itself, and `setFilter` reports nothing for a filter equal to the one it has.

## Filter menu options

A renderer draws a filter menu in each filterable column's header; these options say which columns get one and what it opens. They follow the grid's other column features: a grid-level default that a column overrides, as `sortableColumns` and `sortable` do.

| Option                  | Type                  | Default    | Description                                                                                                                                         |
| ----------------------- | --------------------- | ---------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `filterableColumns`     | `boolean`             | `false`    | Whether columns get a filter menu. The filter applies either way — from `defaultFilter`, `setFilter` or a search box.                               |
| `filterMenu.ui`         | `"simple" \| "excel"` | `"simple"` | Which editor the menu opens: one or two conditions joined by and/or, or a search box over a checklist of values with the conditions a submenu away. |
| `filterMenu.showCounts` | `boolean`             | `false`    | Whether the checklist shows how many rows hold each value.                                                                                          |
| `filterMenu.valueLimit` | `number`              | `10000`    | How many distinct values the checklist lists before it asks for a search first — `DEFAULT_FILTER_VALUE_LIMIT`.                                      |
| `column.filterable`     | `boolean`             |            | Per-column override of `filterableColumns`.                                                                                                         |
| `column.filterMenu`     | `{ ui?, operators? }` |            | The column's own editor, over `filterMenu.ui`, and the operators its conditions offer, in place of its type's defaults.                             |

`ui` is a `FilterMenuUi`, `"simple"` or `"excel"`. Both editors edit the one `FilterState`, so switching `ui` at runtime keeps every filter, and a filter set in code shows in whichever editor is open. A column's `operators` drop `in`, the checklist's own operator; `[]` offers no condition, leaving the excel editor its checklist alone.

`resolveColumnFilterMenu(options, column)` settles all of this for one column — what a renderer draws from:

```ts
import { resolveColumnFilterMenu } from "@gridkitjs/core";

const menu = resolveColumnFilterMenu(
  { filterableColumns: true, filterMenu: { ui: "excel", showCounts: true } },
  { field: "Placed", type: "dateTime" },
);
// { ui: "excel", operators: ["lt", "gt", "between", "isEmpty", "isNotEmpty"],
//   family: "date", showCounts: true, valueLimit: 10000 }
```

It returns `null` for a column with no filter menu, else a `ResolvedColumnFilterMenu`:

| Field        | Type                        | Description                                                                                         |
| ------------ | --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ui`         | `"simple" \| "excel"`       | The column's `filterMenu.ui`, else the grid's, else `"simple"`.                                     |
| `operators`  | `readonly FilterOperator[]` | The column's `filterMenu.operators` without `in`, else its type's `defaultFilterOperators` (below). |
| `family`     | `FilterOperatorFamily`      | The family the column's `type` falls in, which its operators are labelled by.                       |
| `showCounts` | `boolean`                   | The grid's `filterMenu.showCounts`, else `false`.                                                   |
| `valueLimit` | `number`                    | The grid's `filterMenu.valueLimit`, else `DEFAULT_FILTER_VALUE_LIMIT` (10,000, Excel's own cap).    |

## Presets

`excelFilter` is the options for the Excel-style popup as one plain value — `{ filterableColumns: true, filterMenu: { ui: "excel", showCounts: true } }`. A preset is data, not a component or a hook, so any renderer takes it the way it takes its other options, and an option given after it wins. `filterMenu` is replaced whole, not merged: `{ ...excelFilter, filterMenu: { ui: "simple" } }` also drops `showCounts`.

```ts
import { excelFilter, resolveColumnFilterMenu } from "@gridkitjs/core";

resolveColumnFilterMenu(excelFilter, { field: "Region" });
// { ui: "excel", operators: [...], family: "text", showCounts: true, ... }
```

In React it is spread into the grid — see [Presets](/docs/react/column-filter-menu#presets).

## Operators by column type

The conditions a filter menu offers depend on what the column holds. `filterOperatorFamily(type)` reads a column's `type` as one of four families — the filter engine's own reading, so a menu never offers a condition the column would compare differently:

| Family      | Column types                                       |
| ----------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `"text"`    | `"string"`, or no `type`                           |
| `"number"`  | `"number"`, `"decimal"`, `"currency"`, `"percent"` |
| `"date"`    | `"date"`, `"dateTime"`, `"time"`                   |
| `"boolean"` | `"boolean"`                                        |

`defaultFilterOperators(type)` lists the operators a column offers, in order, unless it names its own:

| Column type            | Operators                                                                                |
| ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| text                   | `contains`, `notContains`, `eq`, `ne`, `startsWith`, `endsWith`, `isEmpty`, `isNotEmpty` |
| numeric                | `eq`, `ne`, `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`, `between`, `isEmpty`, `isNotEmpty`                 |
| `"date"`               | `eq`, `ne`, `lt`, `gt`, `between`, `isEmpty`, `isNotEmpty`                               |
| `"dateTime"`, `"time"` | `lt`, `gt`, `between`, `isEmpty`, `isNotEmpty`                                           |
| `"boolean"`            | `eq`, `isEmpty`, `isNotEmpty`                                                            |

A date-time or time cell is an instant, which a typed day or minute seldom equals to the millisecond, so those columns offer before, after and between rather than equals. `in` is never a condition: a list of values is the checklist's to pick. What each operator matches is on [Column filtering](/docs/react/column-filtering#the-fifth-kind-operators).

A menu labels each operator with the `filterOperatorLabel(operator, family)` message, so a translation can word each family its own way. In English a date reads its order as time — `lt` is "Before", `gte` "On or after" — and every other family as size — "Less than", "Greater than or equal to"; `isEmpty` reads "Is blank".

## Condition rows

A simple editor shows a column's conditions as two rows — an operator and its operand each — joined by "and" or "or". Its inputs hold text, so a half-typed number or date stays as typed until the editor is applied. Three functions turn that text into operands and back, each reading the column's `type`:

| Function                           | Type                        | Description                                                                                                        |
| ---------------------------------- | --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `filterOperandArity(operator)`     | `0 \| 1 \| 2`               | How many inputs a row shows: none for `isEmpty` and `isNotEmpty`, two for `between`'s ends, one for the rest.      |
| `parseFilterOperand(text, type)`   | `FilterScalar \| undefined` | The operand `text` stands for on a column of `type`, or `undefined` when the text is empty or doesn't read as one. |
| `formatFilterOperand(value, type)` | `string`                    | The text an input shows for an operand — `parseFilterOperand`'s inverse, for opening a condition already applied.  |

| Family      | Reads                                                                                                                                                          | Writes back                                                                                                     |
| ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `"text"`    | The text as typed, spaces and all.                                                                                                                             | The text.                                                                                                       |
| `"number"`  | Digits with a `.` for decimals and an optional exponent, as a number input gives them. `"12abc"` and `"1,5"` read as nothing rather than as a guess.           | The number as `String` writes it.                                                                               |
| `"date"`    | `yyyy-mm-dd`, as a date input gives it, at that day's local midnight; `yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm`, seconds optional, as a date-time input gives it, at that local time. | `yyyy-mm-dd` on a `"date"` column; `yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm` on a `"dateTime"` or `"time"` one, with seconds when set. |
| `"boolean"` | `"true"` or `"false"`.                                                                                                                                         | `"true"` or `"false"`.                                                                                          |

A row is a `ConditionRowDraft` — `{ operator, text, textTo }`, `textTo` holding `between`'s upper end:

- `conditionRowsFrom(shape, operators, type)` opens the rows over the column's `describeColumnFilter` shape: its conditions, when its filter is conditions, and each row they don't fill at the first of `operators` with no text. A condition keeps its operator even when `operators` doesn't list it. With no operator to offer, only the rows the filter fills.
- `conditionsFromRows(rows, columnId, type)` reads them back as a `ParsedConditionRows` — `{ conditions, invalid }`. A row needs every operand its operator takes, or its index is listed in `invalid` for the editor to mark. A second row left empty is dropped, not invalid; an empty first row is invalid — clearing the filter is the editor's clear action, not an apply with nothing typed.

Apply the conditions only once `invalid` is empty, through the draft, with the combinator the editor shows:

```ts
import {
  conditionRowsFrom,
  conditionsFromRows,
  describeColumnFilter,
  draftToFilter,
  filterEditorReducer,
} from "@gridkitjs/core";

// When the editor opens, with `menu` from resolveColumnFilterMenu:
let rows = conditionRowsFrom(
  describeColumnFilter(filter, "Amount"),
  menu.operators,
  "number",
);

// The user picks "Between" and types both ends:
rows = rows.with(0, { operator: "between", text: "10", textTo: "100" });

// On apply:
const { conditions, invalid } = conditionsFromRows(rows, "Amount", "number");
if (invalid.length === 0) {
  draft = filterEditorReducer(draft, {
    type: "setConditions",
    conditions,
    combinator: "and",
  });
  controller.setFilter(draftToFilter(draft, "Amount", filter));
}
```

What the rows apply, `describeColumnFilter` reads back as conditions, and `conditionRowsFrom` opens as the same rows.

## A search box

A search box over every column is a UI over the filter's global text entry — the `{ query }` that names no column, matched against the raw value of every data column, hidden ones included. Two functions read and write it, so a box always shows what the filter holds — after a restored layout or `filter.clearAll`, too:

| Function                      | Type               | Description                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `searchTextOf(filter)`        | `string`           | The global text entry's query without its leading and trailing `%`, or `""` when there is none. A `%` inside the text stays.                                                            |
| `setSearchText(filter, text)` | `FilterState<Row>` | `filter` with the global text entry set to `%text%` — contains `text` — or removed for `""`. Entries naming a column stay as they are; `filter` itself comes back when nothing changes. |

```ts
import { searchTextOf, setSearchText } from "@gridkitjs/core";

input.value = searchTextOf(controller.getState().filter);

input.addEventListener("input", () => {
  controller.setFilter(
    setSearchText(controller.getState().filter, input.value),
  );
});
```

`setSearchText` writes the text as typed, spaces and all: trimming would take a space from under the caret of a box that reads its text back. A [toolbar](/docs/core/toolbar)'s `"search"` entry is this box.

## Filter state helpers

Smaller transforms over a whole `FilterState`, for a filter bar of plain text boxes, and the functions that apply one:

| Function                                   | Type                          | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `filterQueryFor(filter, columnId?)`        | `string \| null`              | The query of the text entry naming `columnId`, or of the global one with no `columnId`. `null` when no text entry holds that key, including when an entry of another kind does.                                   |
| `setColumnFilter(filter, columnId, query)` | `FilterState<Row>`            | `filter` with the text entry for `columnId` — `undefined` for the global one — set to `query`, replacing whatever entry held that key. An empty `query` removes it. Returns `filter` itself when nothing changes. |
| `clearAllFilters(filter)`                  | `FilterState<Row>`            | Empty. Returns `filter` itself when already empty.                                                                                                                                                                |
| `filterRows(rows, filter, columns)`        | `readonly ResolvedRow<Row>[]` | The rows every entry lets through, in their order, with `rowIndex` renumbered. Returns `rows` itself for an empty filter, or one naming only absent columns.                                                      |
| `matchesQuery(value, query)`               | `boolean`                     | Whether one value matches one text query, as a text entry matches it.                                                                                                                                             |

Unlike `setSearchText`, `setColumnFilter` stores `query` as given, so a bare word is an exact match; wrap it in `%` for "contains".

## See also

- [Column filtering](/docs/react/column-filtering) and [column filter menu](/docs/react/column-filter-menu) for the React grid.
- [The view pipeline](/docs/core/view) for where the filter runs.
- [Toolbar](/docs/core/toolbar) for the search box.

docs.title: Row grouping
docs.description: The row grouping transforms underneath groupBy, groupExpansion and the group-by bar.
docs.body:
`groupRows` reshapes filtered, sorted rows into nested groups, and the other functions here change the two pieces of state it reads: the group-by stack and which groups are collapsed. The [view pipeline](/docs/core/view) and the [controller](/docs/core/controller) call them for you; reach for them directly in a custom adapter or group-by bar.

A `GroupByState` is `readonly GroupByEntry[]`, outer level first, each entry `{ columnId, direction? }` — a level's own `direction` orders its group values, not the rows inside a group. A `GroupExpansionState` is `readonly string[]`: the ids of the groups collapsed, so a group absent from it is expanded.

## Grouping rows

| Function                                       | Type                         | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `groupRows(rows, groupBy, expansion, columns)` | `readonly DisplayRow<Row>[]` | `rows` regrouped into `groupBy`'s levels: a header per distinct value at each level, ordered with `compareValues`, then its nested groups or data rows, depth first. A collapsed group contributes its header only. Returns `rows` itself when `groupBy` is empty or names only absent columns. |
| `groupRowId(path)`                             | `string`                     | A group's id, from the values of its levels outer to inner. Build ids with this, never by hand.                                                                                                                                                                                                 |

Filter and sort run first — [`resolveShownRows`](/docs/core/view#functions) does both — and grouping keeps their order within each group. `rowIndex` is renumbered across the output, headers included.

A `DisplayRow<Row>` is a data row (`ResolvedRow<Row>`, with no `kind`), a group header (`ResolvedGroupRow`, `kind: "group"`), or a group's summary row (`ResolvedGroupSummaryRow`, `kind: "group-summary"`, only from [`withGroupAggregates`](/docs/core/aggregation)). Tell them apart with `"kind" in entry`, then `entry.kind`. A `ResolvedGroupRow` carries:

| Field          | Type                 | Description                                                                         |
| -------------- | -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `groupId`      | `string`             | Its id — `groupRowId(path)` — the entry `GroupExpansionState` holds when collapsed. |
| `level`        | `number`             | Nesting depth, `0` for a top-level group.                                           |
| `columnId`     | `string`             | The column this level groups by.                                                    |
| `value`        | `unknown`            | This level's value — the last entry of `path`.                                      |
| `path`         | `readonly unknown[]` | The value at every level from the top down to this one.                             |
| `expanded`     | `boolean`            | Whether the group is open.                                                          |
| `count`        | `number`             | Its leaf rows, collapsed or not.                                                    |
| `rowIndex`     | `number`             | Its position among the rows as rendered.                                            |
| `datasetIndex` | `number`             | Its position in the whole grouped result, on any page.                              |
| `aggregates`   | `AggregateResults`   | Its own aggregate results, once `withGroupAggregates` has run; empty otherwise.     |

## The group-by stack

| Function                                               | Type           | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `moveGroupByBefore(groupBy, columnId, beforeColumnId)` | `GroupByState` | `columnId` placed in front of `beforeColumnId`, or at the end for `null` — inserted when it is not grouped yet, moved when it is, so a header dropped on the bar and a chip dragged within it both use it. Returns `groupBy` itself for a move that changes nothing. |
| `movesGroupBy(groupBy, columnId, beforeColumnId)`      | `boolean`      | Whether that move would change anything, for a drop indicator that promises only real moves.                                                                                                                                                                         |

A moved level keeps its entry, and so its `direction`. To add or remove one level, the controller's `toggleGroupBy(columnId)` appends a column or takes it out.

## Expanding and collapsing

| Function                                   | Type                  | Description                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------------------ | --------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `toggleGroupExpansion(expansion, groupId)` | `GroupExpansionState` | `groupId` collapsed if it was open, opened if it was collapsed.                                                                                                                   |
| `expandAllGroups(expansion)`               | `GroupExpansionState` | Empty — every group open. Returns `expansion` itself when already empty.                                                                                                          |
| `collapseAllGroups(rows)`                  | `GroupExpansionState` | The id of every group header in `rows`, an already-grouped display. A group hidden under a collapsed one is not in `rows`, so it keeps its own state for when its parent reopens. |

## The group-by bar

`groupByBarVisibility` takes a `GroupByBarVisibility` — `"auto"` (the default) shows the bar while anything is grouped or a header that can be dropped on it is being dragged, `"always"` shows it regardless, and `"never"` hides it.

## In the React grid

`groupableColumns`, `groupByDraggableColumns` and `defaultGroupBy` turn grouping on — see [row grouping](/docs/react/row-grouping).

## See also

- [Row grouping](/docs/react/row-grouping) for the React grid.
- [Aggregation](/docs/core/aggregation) for the values shown on group rows.
- [The view pipeline](/docs/core/view) for where grouping runs.

docs.title: Focus and virtualization
docs.description: The arithmetic behind the grid's single tab stop and its virtualized rows.
docs.body:
`nextFocusForKey` works out where a navigation key moves the grid's tab stop, and `visibleRange` which rows a virtualized body draws. Both are plain arithmetic over numbers; @gridkitjs/dom's [`createGridFocus`](/docs/dom/gestures-and-focus#focus-movement) and [`createRowVirtualizer`](/docs/dom/observers-and-virtualizer#row-virtualizer) do the DOM side and call them for you. Reach for them directly in a renderer that keeps its own focus or scroll.

## Focus

One coordinate space covers the header and the body: a `GridFocus` is `{ rowIndex, columnIndex }`, with body rows from `0` and the header at `HEADER_ROW`, `-1`, so arrowing up out of the first row reaches the header without a case of its own.

| Function                                                                                   | Type                | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `nextFocusForKey(key, modifiers, focus, rowCount, columnCount, pageSize, isSkippableRow?)` | `GridFocus \| null` | Where `key` moves `focus`, or `null` when the key is not the grid's — any key but the arrows, <Kbd>Home</Kbd>, <Kbd>End</Kbd>, <Kbd>PageUp</Kbd> and <Kbd>PageDown</Kbd>, anything with <Kbd>Alt</Kbd>, and <Kbd>Ctrl</Kbd> with a left or right arrow, which resize and reorder. |
| `clampFocus(focus, rowCount, columnCount)`                                                 | `GridFocus`         | `focus` held inside the grid, so a tab stop left behind by a removed column or a shorter page still lands on a cell.                                                                                                                                                              |

`modifiers` is a `NavigationModifiers`, `{ ctrlKey, metaKey, altKey, shiftKey }` — a `KeyboardEvent` will do. `pageSize` is how many rows <Kbd>PageUp</Kbd> and <Kbd>PageDown</Kbd> move, measured once by the caller. <Kbd>Ctrl</Kbd>+<Kbd>Home</Kbd> and <Kbd>Ctrl</Kbd>+<Kbd>End</Kbd> go to the grid's first and last cells, plain <Kbd>Home</Kbd> and <Kbd>End</Kbd> to the row's.

`isSkippableRow(rowIndex)` names rows the vertical moves step over — a group's summary row under `groupAggregateDisplay: "row"`, which holds a row's place but is no tab stop. A move with nowhere to land stays where it was. The left and right moves can run past the grid's edges, so pass the result through `clampFocus`:

```ts
import { clampFocus, nextFocusForKey } from "@gridkitjs/core";

const next = nextFocusForKey(
  event.key,
  event,
  focus,
  rowCount,
  columnCount,
  10,
);
if (next !== null) {
  focus = clampFocus(next, rowCount, columnCount);
  event.preventDefault();
}
```

## Virtualization

| Function                                                                      | Type           | Description                                                                                                                                                     |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `visibleRange(heights, estimatedHeight, scrollTop, viewportHeight, overscan)` | `VisibleRange` | The rows inside `[scrollTop, scrollTop + viewportHeight)`, padded by `overscan` rows each side and kept within the rows there are. Rows need not be one height. |

`heights` is a `RowHeights`, one entry per row: its measured height once known, `undefined` until then, which counts as `estimatedHeight`. A `VisibleRange` is what to draw and the space to leave around it:

| Field          | Type     | Description                                                      |
| -------------- | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `startIndex`   | `number` | The first row to draw.                                           |
| `endIndex`     | `number` | The last row to draw, inclusive — `-1` when there are no rows.   |
| `offsetBefore` | `number` | The height of every row before `startIndex`: the leading spacer. |
| `offsetAfter`  | `number` | The height of every row after `endIndex`: the trailing spacer.   |

## In the React grid

See [accessibility](/docs/react/accessibility#keyboard-navigation) for the keys and [row virtualization](/docs/react/row-virtualization) for `virtualized`.

## See also

- [Accessibility](/docs/react/accessibility) for the keys and the ARIA grid pattern.
- [Row virtualization](/docs/react/row-virtualization) for `virtualized` in the React grid.
- [@gridkitjs/dom](/docs/dom) for the focus and virtualizer behaviours.

docs.title: Ordering
docs.description: The reordering logic underneath reorderableColumns.
docs.body:
`applyColumnOrder` and `moveColumnBefore` are the functions DataGrid calls internally when `reorderableColumns` is enabled — the first puts a column list in the order an order state gives, the second moves one column id to sit before another. Reach for them directly if you're building a custom grid adapter.

## Functions

| Function                                                     | Type                               | Description                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `applyColumnOrder(columns, order)`                           | `readonly ColumnDefinition<Row>[]` | Puts columns in the order order gives. Ids it omits keep their position among the definitions and follow those listed.                            |
| `resolveDataColumns(columns, order)`                         | `readonly DataColumn<Row>[]`       | applyColumnOrder, with each column paired with its id as `{ id, column }` — the width-free list filtering, sorting, grouping and aggregates read. |
| `moveColumnBefore(orderedIds, movedId, beforeId)`            | `ColumnOrderState`                 | Moves one column id to sit before another, or to the end when beforeId is null. Returns the same reference for a move that changes nothing.       |
| `movesColumn(orderedIds, movedId, beforeId)`                 | `boolean`                          | Whether moving movedId in front of beforeId would rearrange anything, for a drop indicator that promises only real moves.                         |
| `resolveDropBefore(orderedIds, targetId, side)`              | `string \| null`                   | "After C" and "before D" name the same gap — this collapses either side of a drop to the one id it lands in front of.                             |
| `resolveKeyboardDropTarget(orderedIds, columnId, direction)` | `string \| null \| undefined`      | The beforeId a keyboard nudge (-1 or 1) produces, matching the pointer-drag drop path. undefined means the nudge is a no-op.                      |
