| A group header                          | A bold row with the group's label, `Region: West`, in the first column and its aggregates under their columns.    |
| The rows of a group                     | Outlined under their header, so Excel's outline buttons collapse and expand them; nested groups nest the outline. |
| A group summary row and the grand total | Bold rows, the totals in their columns' formats.                                                                  |

Every group is written expanded, and Excel's outline buttons sit beside each group header, above its rows, as the grid draws them.

### Number and date formats

The format follows the column's `type` and `format`, the options the grid formats its cells with, so a cell reads in Excel as it does on screen while holding a number a formula can sum:

| Column                                                  | Excel format                                                                |
| ------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `type: "number"` or `"decimal"`, no fraction digits set | General — the number as it is stored, as the grid prints it.                |
| `"number"`/`"decimal"` with `maximumFractionDigits: 2`  | `#,##0.00` — or `0.00` with `useGrouping: false`.                           |
| `type: "percent"`                                       | `0%`, or `0.0%` and so on for the fraction digits set. `0.25` reads as 25%. |
| `type: "currency"` with `format.currency`               | The currency's symbol where the grid's `locale` puts it: `"€"#,##0.00`.     |
| `type: "currency"` without one                          | `#,##0.00`.                                                                 |
| `type: "date"`                                          | `yyyy-mm-dd`.                                                               |
| `type: "time"`                                          | `hh:mm:ss`, or `hh:mm` when the column's `format` leaves the seconds out.   |
| `type: "dateTime"`, or a `Date` in any other column     | `yyyy-mm-dd hh:mm:ss`, or `yyyy-mm-dd hh:mm` without seconds.               |

A format the codes cannot follow — a compact or scientific notation, a unit — is General. Fraction digits are fixed: where the grid shows "up to two", Excel shows two. Dates are written in ISO order, which reads the same in every language; the grouping and decimal marks show as the reader's own Excel settings write them.

An aggregate is written in its column's format — a sum of a currency column is currency — except a count, which is a number of rows whatever the column holds.

## Limits

- One sheet, holding the one table. No formulas: a total is its value, not a `SUM`.
- No styling beyond bold and the number formats: no colours, borders or fonts from the theme.
- Dates before 1 March 1900 or after 9999 are written as their text, since Excel's dates cannot hold them; so is a number that is not finite.
- A cell holds at most 32,767 characters, Excel's limit; longer text is cut.
- The outline goes seven groups deep, as far as Excel's does.

To write something this writer does not, write a writer of your own: see [writers](/docs/core/export#writers).

## See also

- [Core export](/docs/core/export) for the writer contract and the other formats.
- [Export in React](/docs/react/export) for the toolbar and the context menu.
- [Choosing packages](/docs/react/choosing-packages) for when to install it.

docs.title: Accessibility
docs.description: The keyboard model, ARIA attributes and live announcements built into DataGrid, and what has and has not been tested.
docs.body:
DataGrid implements the [WAI-ARIA grid pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/grid/): `role="grid"`, a single [roving tab stop](/docs/react#terms), and a live region for changes no visual cue alone would reach a screen reader with. A grid with an active `groupBy` switches to `role="treegrid"` — the WAI-ARIA pattern for expandable, collapsible rows — instead; an ungrouped grid is unaffected either way.

## Conformance and testing

GridKit makes no WCAG conformance claim yet. It has not been audited against WCAG 2.2, by its authors or by anyone else, and conformance is a property of a whole page, which the grid is only part of. What it is built and tested to:

- **Built to the WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices.** The grid, treegrid, menu, menu button, toolbar and listbox patterns, as described on this page.
- **Operable from the keyboard.** Every built-in feature has a key, listed below and on each feature's page.
- **Tested in a real browser.** A Playwright component suite, run on every push, checks the grid's roles and ARIA attributes, keyboard navigation, focus movement in its menus and dialogs, and what its live region announces. It also runs an [axe](https://github.com/dequelabs/axe-core) scan of a grouped grid, which must report no violations. It runs in Chromium only.

What has not been tested:

- **Screen readers.** No one has yet worked through the grid with NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver or TalkBack, so how its announcements and attributes read in practice is unverified. Reports from screen-reader users are welcome as issues.
- **Beyond the one scan.** The axe scan covers a grouped grid, not every feature, and no automated scan can judge how the grid reads in a screen reader.
- **Colour contrast.** The axe scan leaves it out, since it depends on your theme, and the contrast of the `@gridkitjs/theme-tailwind` palette has not been measured against WCAG's ratios; check it, and any colours you override, in your own theme.
- **Other browsers.** Firefox and Safari are not part of the test suite.

Your part: give every grid an accessible name with `label` or `labelledBy` (without either, it has none), give a `cellTemplate` that renders a control its own accessible name, and test the page your grid lives on.

## Roles

The grid is drawn with `<table>` elements for layout, but its semantics are ARIA's alone. Each `<table>` is `role="presentation"`, and every part inside carries its role explicitly, so the rows belong to the `grid` or `treegrid` element rather than to a native table:

| Element                         | Role                 | Notes                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------- | -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `div.gridkit-data-grid-tables`  | `grid` or `treegrid` | `treegrid` while `groupBy` is non-empty. Carries the label, `aria-rowcount` and `aria-colcount`.            |
| `<table>`                       | `presentation`       | The header, body and grand-total footer tables. Not exposed as tables.                                      |
| `<thead>`, `<tbody>`, `<tfoot>` | `rowgroup`           | One per table.                                                                                              |
| `<tr>`                          | `row`                | Header, data, group header, group summary and footer rows alike. Spacer and loading rows are `aria-hidden`. |
| `<th>`                          | `columnheader`       | Headers relate to cells by their shared `aria-colindex`, not by native table association.                   |
| `<td>`                          | `gridcell`           | A group header row has one, spanning every column.                                                          |

Because a group header is a `row` owned by a `treegrid`, its `aria-level`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-posinset` and `aria-setsize` are permitted there. In a test, find the grid with `getByRole("grid")` or `getByRole("treegrid")`, not `getByRole("table")`.

## Keyboard navigation

One cell holds the grid's tab stop at a time — <Kbd>Tab</Kbd> reaches the grid once, and the arrow keys move within it from there.

| Key                                                                                      | Moves to                                          |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| <Kbd>ArrowUp</Kbd> / <Kbd>ArrowDown</Kbd> / <Kbd>ArrowLeft</Kbd> / <Kbd>ArrowRight</Kbd> | The adjacent cell in that direction.              |
| <Kbd>Home</Kbd> / <Kbd>End</Kbd>                                                         | The first / last cell of the current row.         |
| <Kbd>Ctrl</Kbd>+<Kbd>Home</Kbd> / <Kbd>Ctrl</Kbd>+<Kbd>End</Kbd>                         | The first / last cell of the whole grid.          |
| <Kbd>PageUp</Kbd> / <Kbd>PageDown</Kbd>                                                  | Up or down by however many rows fit the viewport. |

On a focused header, <Kbd>Alt</Kbd>+<Kbd>ArrowLeft</Kbd> / <Kbd>Alt</Kbd>+<Kbd>ArrowRight</Kbd> and <Kbd>Ctrl</Kbd>+<Kbd>ArrowLeft</Kbd> / <Kbd>Ctrl</Kbd>+<Kbd>ArrowRight</Kbd> resize and reorder its column rather than move focus — see [column resizing](/docs/react/column-resizing) and [column reordering](/docs/react/column-reordering) for what they do there. <Kbd>Alt</Kbd>+<Kbd>ArrowDown</Kbd> is likewise reserved on a groupable header, for adding or removing it from the group-by stack — see [row grouping](/docs/react/row-grouping) — and <Kbd>Alt</Kbd>+<Kbd>Shift</Kbd>+<Kbd>ArrowDown</Kbd> on a header with a [filter menu](/docs/react/column-filter-menu), for opening it.

With [`contextMenu`](/docs/react/context-menu) on, <Kbd>Shift</Kbd>+<Kbd>F10</Kbd> or the <Kbd>ContextMenu</Kbd> key on a focused header, cell or group row opens its menu, the keyboard's way to a right-click. The menu follows the [WAI-ARIA menu pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menubar/): the arrow keys, <Kbd>Home</Kbd> and <Kbd>End</Kbd> move between its items, typing a letter jumps to an item starting with it, <Kbd>Enter</Kbd>/<Kbd>Space</Kbd> runs one, and <Kbd>Escape</Kbd> or <Kbd>Tab</Kbd> closes it — focus goes back to where it was opened either way. A disabled item still takes focus, so it can be found.

Pressing <Kbd>Ctrl</Kbd>+<Kbd>C</Kbd> (<Kbd>Cmd</Kbd>+<Kbd>C</Kbd> on a Mac) anywhere in the grid copies the selection to the clipboard, or the focused cell when nothing is selected — see [clipboard](/docs/react/clipboard). It is left to the browser in a text field inside a cell, or while text is highlighted on the page, so copying highlighted text works as it does anywhere else.

The [toolbar](/docs/react/toolbar) follows the [WAI-ARIA toolbar pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/toolbar/): it is one tab stop of its own, before the grid's, and <Kbd>ArrowLeft</Kbd>/<Kbd>ArrowRight</Kbd> move between its controls, wrapping round, with <Kbd>Home</Kbd>/<Kbd>End</Kbd> to the first and last. The search box keeps the keys that move its caret, and the arrows lead out of it at either end of its text. A dropdown — or "More" — follows the [WAI-ARIA menu button pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menu-button/): it opens its menu on its first item on <Kbd>Enter</Kbd>, <Kbd>Space</Kbd> or <Kbd>ArrowDown</Kbd>, and on its last on <Kbd>ArrowUp</Kbd>, and the menu works as the context menu's does. A disabled button still takes focus.

The [column chooser](/docs/react/column-chooser) is a dialog (`role="dialog"`, named "Columns") of native controls: focus starts in its search box, <Kbd>Tab</Kbd> moves through "Show all" and a checkbox per column, <Kbd>Space</Kbd> toggles one, and <Kbd>Escape</Kbd> closes it, giving focus back to where it was opened from. "Show all" is a tri-state checkbox, mixed while only some of the columns its search lists show.

A column's [filter menu](/docs/react/column-filter-menu) is a dialog too (`role="dialog"`, named after its column, "Name filter"), opened below its header. It holds a draft, so it keeps focus: <Kbd>Tab</Kbd> and <Kbd>Shift</Kbd>+<Kbd>Tab</Kbd> move through its controls and wrap round inside it. Focus starts on the first condition's value box. <Kbd>Enter</Kbd> in a box, a picker or a radio button applies it, as OK does, and <Kbd>Escape</Kbd> closes it without applying, giving focus back to the header. Each condition is a group ("Condition 1") of native controls, and And/Or a radio group; a value that doesn't read keeps the menu open, its box `aria-invalid` and described by the message saying so ("Enter a number"), and takes focus.

Its [excel editor](/docs/react/column-filter-menu#the-excel-editor) starts on a search box, over a native tri-state "Select all" checkbox, mixed while only some of the values its search shows are checked. The values are one `listbox` (`aria-multiselectable`, named "Values") and one stop for <Kbd>Tab</Kbd>: <Kbd>ArrowDown</Kbd>/<Kbd>ArrowUp</Kbd>, <Kbd>Home</Kbd>/<Kbd>End</Kbd> and <Kbd>PageDown</Kbd>/<Kbd>PageUp</Kbd> move among them, <Kbd>Space</Kbd> checks or unchecks one, and <Kbd>Enter</Kbd> applies. Each value is an `option` whose `aria-checked` says whether the filter keeps it; only the values near the list's scroll position are drawn, so each carries `aria-posinset` and `aria-setsize` for its place in the whole list.

Above the search box, "Text filters" — "Number filters", "Date filters" — is a menu button (`aria-haspopup="menu"`, `aria-expanded`), following the menu button pattern as the toolbar's dropdowns do: its menu of the column's conditions sits above the filter menu, so <Kbd>Escape</Kbd> or <Kbd>Tab</Kbd> closes that menu alone, giving focus back to the button. While the column is filtered by conditions, the menu's items are `menuitemcheckbox`es, the operators in use checked. Choosing one shows the conditions in the checklist's place, focus on the first one's value box, and "Back to values" brings the checklist back, focus on the button.

A group header renders as one cell spanning every column, so it holds the tab stop as a single unit rather than N per-column cells: <Kbd>ArrowLeft</Kbd>/<Kbd>ArrowRight</Kbd> are a no-op on it, and <Kbd>Space</Kbd>/<Kbd>Enter</Kbd> expand or collapse it in place of selecting anything.

Under `groupAggregateDisplay: "row"` (see [aggregate functions](/docs/react/aggregate-functions)), a group's own summary row is presentational rather than an addressable stop: <Kbd>ArrowUp</Kbd>/<Kbd>ArrowDown</Kbd>/<Kbd>PageUp</Kbd>/<Kbd>PageDown</Kbd>/<Kbd>Ctrl</Kbd>+<Kbd>End</Kbd> step straight over it, landing on the nearest row that isn't one. It still occupies a real position for `aria-rowindex`/`aria-rowcount` — see below — only the tab stop skips it.

The group-by bar sits outside the grid's own table and its single-roving-tab-stop model entirely — there's no shared position for a chip to keep in sync the way a cell has, so each chip (and its own remove button) is simply, always its own tab stop, in plain DOM order. Drag a chip to reorder the stack, or focus one and press <Kbd>Ctrl</Kbd>+<Kbd>ArrowLeft</Kbd> / <Kbd>Ctrl</Kbd>+<Kbd>ArrowRight</Kbd> — the same modifier and semantics a column header's own reorder shortcut uses. A groupable header whose column sets `groupByDraggable` can also be dragged straight into the bar, landing at whichever position among the existing chips it's released.

## ARIA attributes

| Attribute                        | Where                         | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| -------------------------------- | ----------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `aria-rowcount`                  | The grid                      | Total rows: the header, every row of `dataSource` as filtered, sorted and grouped, every group row, one summary row per group under `groupAggregateDisplay: "row"`, and the grand-total footer while `aggregates` is set. The full dataset count, not just the current page's, once `paginated` is on.                                              |
| `aria-colcount`                  | The grid                      | Total columns as currently sized and ordered.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `aria-rowindex`                  | Every row                     | 1-based and in order, one per row; the header is row 1, so the first body row is row 2, and the grand-total footer is the last. Built from each row's position in the whole result, not its page-relative one, so it holds on every page and in a virtualized grid; see [pagination](/docs/react/pagination#rowindex-vs-the-rows-dataset-position). |
| `aria-colindex`                  | Every header and body cell    | 1-based, following the current column order.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `aria-multiselectable`           | The grid                      | Set to `true` when `selectable.rows` or `selectable.columns` is `"multiple"`. Omitted otherwise.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `aria-selected`                  | Row, column header, and cell  | Reflects whether that row/column/cell is selected — but only when that dimension's selection is enabled at all. Omitted, not `false`, when it isn't: a display-only grid never claims to have an unselected anything.                                                                                                                               |
| `aria-sort`                      | Column headers                | `"ascending"` or `"descending"` once a sortable column has an active sort direction. Omitted — not `"none"` — for an unsorted or unsortable column.                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `aria-description`               | Column headers                | "Filtered" while a column with a filter menu is filtered — the `columnFiltered` message.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `aria-keyshortcuts`              | Column headers and body cells | Lists whichever shortcuts that column or cell actually responds to (below), so they're discoverable rather than assumed.                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `aria-expanded`                  | Group header rows             | Whether that group is currently expanded or collapsed.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `aria-level`                     | Group header rows             | 1-based nesting depth — 1 for a top-level group, 2 for one nested inside it, and so on.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `aria-label`                     | The context menu              | Names the menu: a header's after its column, "Name column menu"; a cell's "Row menu"; a group row's "Group menu"; empty body space's "Grid menu" — the `headerMenuLabel`, `cellMenuLabel`, `groupMenuLabel` and `bodyMenuLabel` messages.                                                                                                           |
| `aria-disabled` / `aria-checked` | Context menu items            | A disabled item, which stays focusable; and a checkable item's state — "Sort ascending" is checked while the column sorts ascending.                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `aria-label`                     | The filter menu               | Names the dialog after its column, "Name filter" — the `filterMenuLabel` message.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `aria-pressed`                   | Filter menu sort entries      | "Sort ascending" or "Sort descending", pressed while the column sorts that way.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `aria-invalid`                   | Filter menu value boxes       | Set on a box whose value is missing or doesn't read once OK is pressed, with `aria-describedby` pointing at the message saying so — the `filterValueInvalid` message.                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `aria-checked`                   | Filter checklist values       | Whether the filter keeps the value, on each `role="option"` of the excel editor's `listbox`, which is `aria-multiselectable`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `aria-posinset` / `aria-setsize` | Filter checklist values       | The value's 1-based place among, and the count of, the values the list holds — only those near its scroll position are drawn.                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `aria-expanded`                  | Filter menu "Text filters"    | Whether the excel editor's menu of conditions is open, on the button opening it, which carries `aria-haspopup="menu"`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `aria-label` / `aria-controls`   | The toolbar                   | Names the toolbar — "Grid toolbar", the `toolbarLabel` message, or its `label` — and points it at the grid it acts on.                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `aria-disabled` / `aria-pressed` | Toolbar buttons               | A disabled button, which stays focusable; and a toggle's state. A dropdown carries `aria-haspopup="menu"` and `aria-expanded`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `aria-posinset` / `aria-setsize` | Group header rows             | That group's 1-based position among, and count of, the group headers sharing its level and immediate parent.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |

A column header's `aria-keyshortcuts` names whichever of these apply, space-separated:

- `Control+ArrowLeft Control+ArrowRight` when the column is [reorderable](/docs/react/column-reordering).
- `Alt+ArrowLeft Alt+ArrowRight Alt+Enter` when the column is [resizable](/docs/react/column-resizing) — the first two nudge its width, the last sizes it to its content.
- `Alt+ArrowUp` when the column is [sortable](/docs/react/column-sorting).
- `Alt+ArrowDown` when the column is [groupable](/docs/react/row-grouping).
- `Alt+Shift+ArrowDown` when the column has a [filter menu](/docs/react/column-filter-menu).
- `Shift+F10` while a header opens the grid's [context menu](/docs/react/context-menu).

A body cell's `aria-keyshortcuts` is `Space Enter` when cell selection is on — see [cell selection](/docs/react/cell-selection), and lists `Shift+F10` too while a cell opens the grid's context menu. A group row's is `Space Enter`, and `Space Enter Shift+F10` while a group row opens one.

## Live announcements

A `role="status" aria-live="polite"` region, outside the table itself, reports changes that have no visual cue a screen reader could otherwise pick up on:

- **Column resize** — only on release (`phase: "end"`), not on every frame of the drag: a live region updated on each pointermove would say nothing an assistive technology could keep up with. Announces the column's name and its new width in pixels. Autofitting one column announces the same way.
- **Autofit** — fitting more than one column at once, as "Autofit all columns" or the ref's `autoFitColumns` does, announces how many in place of each one's width ("3 columns autofitted").
- **Column reorder** — on drop. Announces the column's name and its new position, as "column _n_ of _total_".
- **Sort change** — a toggle, a stack, or a clear back to unsorted are each phrased differently: a plain toggle announces the column and its new direction; adding or updating a column in a multi-column sort also announces its priority ("key _n_ of _total_"); clearing a column's sort announces that its sort was cleared.
- **Row and column selection changes** — only when more than one row or column changes in the same interaction (a range, a select-all, <Kbd>Ctrl</Kbd>+<Kbd>A</Kbd>). A single selection is already carried by that row's or column's own `aria-selected`, so announcing it too would talk over what a screen reader just read. Announces the resulting total, e.g. "3 rows selected".
- **Cell selection** — every time a selection lands on a cell. Unlike row and column selection, a cell selection is always exactly one cell, so there's no multi-item threshold to cross — the announcement fires on every commit instead, naming the column and row the selected cell is in.
- **Group-by change** — adding, removing, or repositioning a level (via the header toggle, a header dropped on the bar, a dragged chip, or a chip's own <Kbd>Ctrl</Kbd>+<Kbd>ArrowLeft</Kbd> / <Kbd>Ctrl</Kbd>+<Kbd>ArrowRight</Kbd>) announces the column and, once two or more levels are stacked, its position ("level _n_ of _total_"); removing any column from the grouping announces that its grouping was removed ("Region, grouping removed"). Every path funnels through the same announcement, so a drag and a click read identically.
- **Column visibility** — hiding or showing one column, from the context menu, the column chooser or the ref's `hideColumns`/`showColumns`, announces the column and which ("Name, column hidden"); hiding or showing several at once, as the chooser's "Show all" does, announces how many ("3 columns hidden").
- **Copy** — once a copy is on the clipboard, announces what it holds ("3 rows copied", "1 cell copied"), as nothing on screen shows it; a copy the browser refuses announces "Copy failed".
- **Search** — once a search typed into the toolbar's box applies, announces how many rows it found ("3 rows found").
- **Filter menu** — once a column's [filter menu](/docs/react/column-filter-menu) applies and the grid has drawn the rows its filter keeps, announces how many of all the rows they are ("2 of 3 rows").
- **Group expand/collapse** — a single group toggle announces "Group expanded"/"Group collapsed"; `expandAllGroups()`/`collapseAllGroups()` announce the whole-tree result instead ("All groups expanded"/"All groups collapsed").
- **Page change** — moving to another page or changing the page size announces where the grid is now, as the `pageStatus` message has it ("Page 2 of 5"). The silent reset to the first page a filter, sort or regroup causes is not announced on its own.

Each announcement's wording is a `messages` key, so it can be translated — see [localization](/docs/react/localization).

## See also

- [DataGrid](/docs/react/data-grid) for the props these behaviors are built on.
- [Row](/docs/react/row-selection), [column](/docs/react/column-selection), and [cell](/docs/react/cell-selection) selection, each in depth.
- [Column resizing](/docs/react/column-resizing), [reordering](/docs/react/column-reordering), and [sorting](/docs/react/column-sorting), each in depth.
- [Row grouping](/docs/react/row-grouping) for the `treegrid` role and group-by/expansion state, in depth.
- [Context menu](/docs/react/context-menu) for the header, cell and group menus and their keys.
- [Toolbar](/docs/react/toolbar) for the toolbar, its search box and its keys.
- [Pagination](/docs/react/pagination) for how `aria-rowindex`/`aria-rowcount` behave once `paginated` is on.
- [Aggregate functions](/docs/react/aggregate-functions) for `groupAggregateDisplay: "row"` and why its summary row is skipped by the arrow keys.
- [Live data](/docs/react/live-data) for why changes to the data are not announced.

docs.title: Cell selection
docs.description: Letting the user select one cell at a time with selectable.cells.
docs.body:
`selectable.cells` takes a `CellSelectionMode`: only `false` or `"single"`. A cell addresses one value, so there is no "multiple" and no range to take. A click moves the selection to that cell; <Kbd>Ctrl</Kbd>+click on the selected cell clears it.

## Single-select cells

<CellSelectionExample />

## Props

| Prop                            | Type                                        | Default | Description                                                                                                                                               |
| ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `selectable.cells`              | `false \| "single"`                         | `false` | How many cells the user may select at once — no "multiple": a cell addresses one value, so there is no range to take.                                     |
| `defaultCellSelection`          | `CellSelectionState`                        |         | The cell selected to start with — a `SelectedCellRef` (`{ rowId, columnId }`), or `null` for none. Uncontrolled.                                          |
| `cellSelection`                 | `CellSelectionState`                        |         | The selected cell, controlled — `null` for none, changed only through the cell callbacks. See [controlled state](/docs/react/state).                      |
| `onCellSelect / onCellDeselect` | `(event: CellSelectEvent) => void`          |         | Once for the cell selected, once for the cell deselected.                                                                                                 |
| `onCellSelectionChange`         | `(event: CellSelectionChangeEvent) => void` |         | Once per change with what was selected and what was deselected — one interaction can fill both, since moving between cells deselects and selects at once. |

## Payload shapes

`onCellSelect`/`onCellDeselect` fire a `CellSelectEvent<Row>`, `onCellSelectionChange` a `CellSelectionChangeEvent<Row>`:

| Type                            | Field        | Type                        | Description                                                                 |
| ------------------------------- | ------------ | --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `CellSelectEvent<Row>`          | `cell`       | `SelectedCell<Row>`         | The cell selected or deselected.                                            |
|                                 | `selection`  | `CellSelectionState`        | The selected cell's address, at that point.                                 |
| `CellSelectionChangeEvent<Row>` | `selected`   | `SelectedCell<Row> \| null` | The cell now selected, or `null` if this change only cleared one.           |
|                                 | `deselected` | `SelectedCell<Row> \| null` | The cell that was selected before, or `null` if there wasn't one.           |
|                                 | `selection`  | `CellSelectionState`        | The same as `selected`, reduced to its address — `SelectedCellRef \| null`. |

Each carries the cell as a `SelectedCell<Row>`, resolved down to the value it shows:

| Field         | Type                  | Description                                                                                           |
| ------------- | --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `rowId`       | `string`              | The cell's row id.                                                                                    |
| `columnId`    | `string`              | The cell's column id.                                                                                 |
| `row`         | `Row`                 | The whole row this cell belongs to.                                                                   |
| `column`      | `ResolvedColumn<Row>` | The resolved column — see [imperative handle](/docs/react/imperative-handle#resolved-row-and-column). |
| `rowIndex`    | `number`              | Position among the rows as rendered.                                                                  |
| `columnIndex` | `number`              | Position among the columns as displayed.                                                              |
| `value`       | `unknown`             | The cell's value, read off the column's `field` path.                                                 |

## Reading selection outside the grid's own tree

`useSelectionState`, documented on [row selection](/docs/react/row-selection#reading-selection-outside-the-grids-own-tree), covers row, column, and cell selection together as one hook rather than three — its `cellSelection` field is this page's `CellSelectionState`.

## Keyboard

With the arrow keys, move focus to a cell and press <Kbd>Enter</Kbd> to select it. <Kbd>Space</Kbd> toggles it, so on the selected cell it clears the selection, as <Kbd>Ctrl</Kbd>+click does. See [accessibility](/docs/react/accessibility#keyboard-navigation) for the full keyboard model.

## See also

- [Row selection](/docs/react/row-selection) and [column selection](/docs/react/column-selection) for the other two areas.
- [Accessibility](/docs/react/accessibility) for the keyboard model.
- [core: Selection](/docs/core/selection) for the framework-free primitives.

docs.title: Choosing packages
docs.description: What each GridKit package does, which ones a React app installs, and when to add core, dom or export-xlsx yourself.
docs.body:
GridKit is split into five published packages, so an app installs only what it uses. A React app needs two of them: `@gridkitjs/react` and `@gridkitjs/theme-tailwind`.

## The packages

| Package                     | What it holds                                                                                                                     | Install it                                                                |
| --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `@gridkitjs/react`          | The `DataGrid` component, its hooks and its types.                                                                                | In every React app.                                                       |
| `@gridkitjs/theme-tailwind` | The stylesheet: palette tokens, dark mode and the grid's styles, for Tailwind CSS v4.                                             | In every app that uses Tailwind. See [theming](/docs/theme-tailwind).     |
| `@gridkitjs/core`           | The grid's logic in plain TypeScript: column definitions, sorting, filtering, row grouping, aggregates, pagination and the state. | Comes with `react`. Add it yourself to import from it, as below.          |
| `@gridkitjs/dom`            | Browser behaviours with no framework: pointer gestures, keyboard focus, observers, the virtualizer, overlays and menus.           | Comes with `react`. Needed directly only to build a renderer of your own. |
| `@gridkitjs/export-xlsx`    | The Excel export writer.                                                                                                          | Only to offer "Export to Excel". See [Excel export](/docs/export-xlsx).   |

The split follows what each layer needs to run. `core` needs no DOM, so it runs in Node, in tests and on a server. `dom` needs a browser but no framework. `react` only draws: every decision the grid makes comes from `core`, and every browser behaviour from `dom`, so a renderer for another framework reuses both.

## A React app

<PackageInstall pkg="@gridkitjs/react @gridkitjs/theme-tailwind" />

That is the whole install for every feature in the React docs except Excel export. Import the stylesheet once, as the [quick start](/docs/react) shows, and import components and types from `@gridkitjs/react`, which re-exports the types its props use, such as `ColumnDefinition`, `FilterState` and `SelectionState`.

## Importing from core

Some helpers live only in `@gridkitjs/core`: `defineColumnsFromRows`, `resolveGridView`, `sortRows`, `filterRows`, and the state types `ColumnSortState` and `PaginationState`. To import them, add `core` to your own dependencies:

<PackageInstall pkg="@gridkitjs/core" />

Install the same version `@gridkitjs/react` depends on (`npm ls @gridkitjs/core` shows it), so the app keeps one copy. With npm a transitive import often resolves anyway, but pnpm and Yarn Plug'n'Play refuse an import of a package you did not list.

## Excel export

<PackageInstall pkg="@gridkitjs/export-xlsx" />

Register its writer on the grid with `exportWriters`, and "Export to Excel" joins the grid's export commands. CSV and JSON export are built in and need no extra package. See [Excel export](/docs/export-xlsx) and [export](/docs/react/export).

## Without Tailwind

The theme is compiled by Tailwind CSS v4; there is no plain-CSS build yet. Without Tailwind, keep `@gridkitjs/react` and write a stylesheet of your own against the grid's class names. See [without Tailwind](/docs/theme-tailwind#without-tailwind).

## Versions

Each package carries its own version and changelog, so `react` and `theme-tailwind` need not share a number. Until 1.0, a minor release may break: read the changelog before upgrading across one.

## See also

- [Quick start](/docs/react) to install, style and render a first grid.
- [Core overview](/docs/core) for the logic `DataGrid` is built on.
- [Dom overview](/docs/dom) for the browser behaviours, and for writing a renderer.
- [Theming](/docs/theme-tailwind) for the stylesheet's tokens and class names.
- [From Syncfusion or AG Grid](/docs/react/migrating) for moving an existing grid across.

docs.title: Clipboard
docs.description: Copy a cell, a row or the selection to the clipboard from the context menu, Ctrl+C or the ref, as text a spreadsheet splits into cells and as an HTML table.
docs.body:
The grid copies what the user sees to the clipboard in two forms at once: tab-separated text, which a spreadsheet such as Excel or Google Sheets splits into cells when pasted, and an HTML table, which a word processor pastes as a table. The context menu's copy items, <Kbd>Ctrl</Kbd>+<Kbd>C</Kbd> and `ref.current.runCommand("copy.selection")` all run the same built-in commands.

A copy is built from the grid's state, never from its page, the same way an [export](/docs/react/export) is: each cell's text as the grid formats it, the shown columns in their current order, and never a hidden column or one with `exportable: false`. Selected rows on another page or inside a collapsed group still copy. The text is exactly what the grid shows — no byte order mark, and no guard against formulas as a CSV export has — so what you copy is what you see. Group header rows and aggregates are not copied; a copy holds data rows only.

## From the context menu

<ClipboardExample />

The cell menu starts with three copy items whenever [`contextMenu`](/docs/react/context-menu) is on:

```ts
<DataGrid
  columns={columns}
  dataSource={orders}
  selectable={{ rows: "multiple" }}
  contextMenu
/>
```

| Item           | Command          | Copies                                                                                                                         |
| -------------- | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Copy cell      | `copy.cell`      | The cell's text. Disabled on a column with `exportable: false`.                                                                |
| Copy row       | `copy.row`       | The row's cells, without a header.                                                                                             |
| Copy selection | `copy.selection` | What is selected, below. Shown once anything is [selectable](/docs/react/row-selection); disabled until something is selected. |

Opening the menu on a row that is not selected selects it first, where rows are selectable, so Copy selection then copies that row.

## The selection

`copy.selection` copies, in order of precedence:

1. **The selected rows** the filter leaves, in the order the grid shows them, under a header row once there are two or more.
2. **The selected columns** over every row the filter leaves, under their header.
3. **The selected cell**.

## With the keyboard

Pressing <Kbd>Ctrl</Kbd>+<Kbd>C</Kbd> — <Kbd>Cmd</Kbd>+<Kbd>C</Kbd> on a Mac — with focus anywhere in the grid copies the selection, or the focused cell when nothing is selected. It needs no `contextMenu`.

It is left to the browser while focus is in a text field inside a cell, or while text is highlighted on the page — so highlighting part of a cell and pressing <Kbd>Ctrl</Kbd>+<Kbd>C</Kbd> copies that text, as it would anywhere else — and when there is nothing to copy, as on a header with nothing selected.

## Announcements

Nothing on screen shows that a copy happened, so a screen reader hears what was copied — "3 rows copied", "1 cell copied", "2 columns copied" — once it is on the clipboard. When the browser refuses the clipboard, as it may outside a secure (`https`) page or without the user's gesture, it hears "Copy failed" and the error is logged with a `console.error`.

## From the ref

`runCommand` copies from code, on a target of your choosing. Browsers only allow the clipboard during a user's gesture, so call it from a click or key handler:

```ts
const gridRef = useRef<DataGridApi<Order>>(null);

<button onClick={() => gridRef.current?.runCommand("copy.selection")}>
  Copy selected
</button>;

gridRef.current?.runCommand("copy.row", {
  area: "cell",
  rowId: "42",
  columnId: "Name",
});
```

`copy.cell` and `copy.row` take a `{ area: "cell", rowId, columnId }` target; `copy.selection` runs on the default `{ area: "grid" }`. Each returns whether it ran — not when there is nothing to copy.

<Callout type="note" title="Browser support">

The grid writes through the async Clipboard API with both formats where the browser has it, falls back to plain text alone where it cannot write HTML, and to the older `copy` event on a page outside a secure context. See @gridkitjs/dom's [`writeClipboard`](/docs/dom/downloads-clipboard-print#clipboard).

</Callout>

## Paste

There is no paste: the grid copies out, but does not take clipboard content in.

## Localization

The item labels and announcements are messages — `copyCell`, `copyRow`, `copySelection`, `copied` and `copyFailed` — see [localization](/docs/react/localization).

## See also

- [Context menu](/docs/react/context-menu) for the copy items.
- [Row selection](/docs/react/row-selection) for copying a selection.
- [core: Export](/docs/core/export) for the table a copy is written from.

docs.title: Column chooser
docs.description: A dialog for choosing which columns show — a checkbox per column, a search box and Show all — opened from the toolbar, a header's context menu or the ref.
docs.body:
The column chooser is a small dialog listing every data column, hidden ones included, each with a checkbox: checked while the column shows. A search box narrows the list, and a "Show all" checkbox shows or hides every column the search lists at once. Each change applies as it is made — there is nothing to confirm or cancel.

## Opening it

<ColumnChooserExample />

It is the built-in `column.choose` command, "Choose columns", so it opens wherever that command is offered:

- **The toolbar.** `toolbar` alone lists it at the far end, after "Clear filters"; an object lists it as `"column.choose"`. It opens below its button — or below "More", while the toolbar is too narrow for it.
- **A header's context menu.** `contextMenu` lists it last in the header menu, after "Hide column". It opens below the header the menu was opened on.
- **The ref.** `openColumnChooser()` opens it at the grid's top-end corner, as does `runCommand("column.choose")`.

```tsx
const gridRef = useRef<DataGridApi<Order>>(null);

<DataGrid
  ref={gridRef}
  columns={[
    { field: "Id", hideable: false },
    { field: "Customer" },
    { field: "Region" },
    { field: "Notes", hidden: true },
  ]}
  dataSource={orders}
  toolbar
  contextMenu
/>;

<button onClick={() => gridRef.current?.openColumnChooser()}>Columns</button>;
```

Only one panel is open at a time: opening the chooser again replaces it. Opened from a context menu, the menu closes first. Closing the chooser gives focus back to where it was opened from — the toolbar button, the header, or, from the ref, whatever had focus — or to the grid's focused cell when that header has gone with a column the chooser hid.

To leave the chooser out, list your own items without `column.choose`: `toolbar={{ items: ["search", "spacer", "filter.clearAll"] }}`, or a header menu built from `defaultContextMenu.header` with it filtered out — see [choosing the items](/docs/react/context-menu#choosing-the-items). A [command of your own](/docs/react/context-menu#commands-of-your-own) with the id `column.choose` replaces it everywhere at once.

## What it shows

- **Every data column, in column order**, by its header text — a column with `hidden: true` included, unchecked, so it can be shown.
- **A search box** that narrows the list to the columns whose header text contains what is typed, ignoring case. When it matches nothing, the chooser says "No matching columns".
- **"Show all"**, over the columns the search lists: checked while all of them show, unchecked while none does, and mixed in between. Toggling it shows every hidden one, or, once all show, hides them.

## The rules

- A column with [`hideable: false`](/docs/react/column-definition#column-visibility) shows checked and disabled while it shows: the user cannot hide it. "Show all" leaves it alone, and does not count it. Hidden some other way — `hidden: true`, or the ref's `hideColumns` — it can still be shown.
- The last column shown cannot be hidden: its checkbox is disabled, and "Show all" keeps the first of the columns it would hide rather than leave none.
- Each change goes through `showColumns` and `hideColumns`, so it fires `onColumnVisibilityChange` and, with a controlled `columnVisibility`, only asks — as any change to the columns does.
- A screen reader hears each change: "Score, column hidden" for one column, "3 columns hidden" for "Show all".

The chooser does not reorder columns; drag a header for that — see [column reordering](/docs/react/column-reordering).

## Keyboard & pointer interactions

The chooser is a dialog of native controls, so it works as a form does.

| Key or action                                    | Does                                                                                                               |
| ------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Opening it                                       | Focus goes to the search box.                                                                                      |
| <Kbd>Tab</Kbd> / <Kbd>Shift</Kbd>+<Kbd>Tab</Kbd> | The next or previous control — the search box, "Show all", then each column.                                       |
| <Kbd>Space</Kbd>, or a click                     | Toggles the checkbox. A disabled one does nothing.                                                                 |
| <Kbd>Escape</Kbd>                                | Closes it, giving focus back to where it was opened from.                                                          |
| A click outside it, a scroll or a resize         | Closes it — but not the scroll its own change causes, a grid scrolled to its end scrolling back as a column hides. |

<Kbd>Escape</Kbd> closes only the chooser: it never reaches the grid, so the
selection stays.

## Messages

Every string the chooser shows or announces is a message — see [localization](/docs/react/localization):

| Key                        | Default                                      |
| -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `chooseColumns`            | "Choose columns" — the command's label.      |
| `columnChooserLabel`       | "Columns" — the dialog's accessible name.    |
| `columnChooserSearchLabel` | "Search columns" — the search box's name.    |
| `searchPlaceholder`        | "Search…" — shown in the empty search box.   |
| `showAllColumns`           | "Show all"                                   |
| `noMatchingColumns`        | "No matching columns"                        |
| `columnShown`              | "Name, column shown" — one column shown.     |
| `columnHidden`             | "Name, column hidden" — one column hidden.   |
| `columnsShown`             | "3 columns shown" — several shown at once.   |
| `columnsHidden`            | "3 columns hidden" — several hidden at once. |

The theme's classes for it are listed under [column chooser](/docs/theme-tailwind#column-chooser). For a chooser of your own, @gridkitjs/core's [`resolveColumnChooser`](/docs/core/commands#the-column-chooser) works out the list, the "Show all" state and what it does.

## See also

- [Column definitions](/docs/react/column-definition) for column visibility.
- [Column reordering](/docs/react/column-reordering) for the order the chooser follows.
- [Context menu](/docs/react/context-menu) and [toolbar](/docs/react/toolbar) for where it is shown.

docs.title: Column definitions
docs.description: The full ColumnDefinition<Row> field reference — field, id, type, and the rest, with links to where each has more to say.
docs.body:
Every entry in `columns` is a `ColumnDefinition<Row>`, the same shape `defineColumnsFromRows` produces automatically for a column left undeclared. This page lists every field; several have a whole page of their own, linked from the description below.

## Fields

| Field                   | Type                                                                                                          | Default                          | Description                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `field`                 | `FieldPath<Row> \| string`                                                                                    |                                  | Path to this cell's value: a key of `Row`, or `"Parent.Child"` for a leaf one level inside a nested object.                                                                      |
| `id`                    | `string`                                                                                                      | `field`                          | Stable identity for state keyed by this column. Needed when two columns render the same field differently.                                                                       |
| `type`                  | `"dateTime" \| "date" \| "time" \| "number" \| "string" \| "boolean" \| "decimal" \| "currency" \| "percent"` | `"string"`                       | The value type of this column's cells.                                                                                                                                           |
| `alignment`             | `"left" \| "center" \| "right"`                                                                               | `"left"` (`"right"` for numbers) | Alignment of this column's cells.                                                                                                                                                |
| `header`                | `string`                                                                                                      | the field path                   | The column's name as plain text. The header shows it when there is no `headerTemplate`; announcements use it either way.                                                         |
| `format`                | `Intl.NumberFormatOptions \| Intl.DateTimeFormatOptions`                                                      |                                  | How this column's values read as text, with the grid's `locale`. See [formatting values](#formatting-values).                                                                    |
| `valueFormatter`        | `(value: unknown, row: Row \| undefined) => string`                                                           |                                  | Turns a value into its text, in place of `format` and `type`. See [formatting values](#formatting-values).                                                                       |
| `headerTemplate`        | `Node \| (() => Node)`                                                                                        |                                  | Header content, or a function returning it at render time. See [column templates](/docs/react/column-templates).                                                                 |
| `cellTemplate`          | `(context: CellTemplateContext<Row>) => Node`                                                                 |                                  | Renders this column's cells in place of the formatted value. See [column templates](/docs/react/column-templates).                                                               |
| `footerTemplate`        | `(context: FooterTemplateContext<Row>) => Node`                                                               |                                  | Renders this column's own aggregate result in a group header or the grand-total footer. See [aggregate functions](/docs/react/aggregate-functions).                              |
| `width`                 | `number`                                                                                                      |                                  | Width in px this column starts at. See [column resizing](/docs/react/column-resizing).                                                                                           |
| `minWidth` / `maxWidth` | `number`                                                                                                      |                                  | Bounds a resize may not drag past. See [column resizing](/docs/react/column-resizing).                                                                                           |
| `resizable`             | `boolean`                                                                                                     | `resizableColumns`               | Whether this column can be resized, overriding the grid-level default. See [column resizing](/docs/react/column-resizing).                                                       |
| `reorderable`           | `boolean`                                                                                                     | `reorderableColumns`             | Whether this column can be dragged to a new position. See [column reordering](/docs/react/column-reordering).                                                                    |
| `sortable`              | `boolean`                                                                                                     | `sortableColumns`                | Whether this column can be sorted. See [column sorting](/docs/react/column-sorting).                                                                                             |
| `groupable`             | `boolean`                                                                                                     | `groupableColumns`               | Whether this column can be grouped by. See [row grouping](/docs/react/row-grouping).                                                                                             |
| `filterable`            | `boolean`                                                                                                     | `filterableColumns`              | Whether this column has a filter menu. See [column filter menu](/docs/react/column-filter-menu).                                                                                 |
| `filterMenu`            | `ColumnFilterMenuOptions`                                                                                     |                                  | This column's filter menu, over the grid's `filterMenu`: `{ ui, operators }`. See [filter menu options](/docs/react/column-filter-menu#options).                                 |
| `groupToggleIcon`       | `boolean`                                                                                                     | `groupToggleIconColumns`         | Whether a groupable header shows its group-toggle icon. Purely a rendering choice. See [row grouping](/docs/react/row-grouping).                                                 |
| `groupByDraggable`      | `boolean`                                                                                                     | `groupByDraggableColumns`        | Whether this column's header may be dragged into the group-by bar. See [row grouping](/docs/react/row-grouping).                                                                 |
| `wrap`                  | `{ header?, cells? }`                                                                                         | `all off`                        | Lets this column's header and/or cell text wrap onto multiple lines instead of eliding to one.                                                                                   |
| `hidden`                | `boolean`                                                                                                     | `false`                          | Whether this column starts out hidden. See [column visibility](#column-visibility).                                                                                              |
| `hideable`              | `boolean`                                                                                                     | `true`                           | Whether the user may hide this column — honoured by the header's context menu and the column chooser. `hideColumns` still hides it. See [column visibility](#column-visibility). |
| `exportable`            | `boolean`                                                                                                     | `true`                           | Whether this column is written to an export, a clipboard copy or a print. `false` keeps it out of all of them — a column of action buttons, say.                                 |
| `exportValue`           | `(value: unknown, row: Row) => string \| number \| boolean \| Date \| null`                                   |                                  | The typed value an export stores for this column's cells, for a format that keeps types, such as a spreadsheet. The text every format writes is still the formatted value.       |
| `headerClassName`       | `string`                                                                                                      |                                  | Extra class names appended to this column's `th`.                                                                                                                                |
| `cellClassName`         | `string`                                                                                                      |                                  | Extra class names appended to this column's `td`, on every row.                                                                                                                  |

## Formatting values

A column with no `cellTemplate` shows its value as text, and its aggregates in the footer and group headers read the same way. Booleans read `true` / `false`, and `null` and `undefined` leave the cell empty.

Dates and numbers are formatted through `Intl` only once you ask for it, by giving the column a `format` or the grid a [`locale`](/docs/react/data-grid#props). Until then they print as they always have: a number as-is (`1234.5`), a total in the footer or a group header with digit grouping (`1,234.5`), a date through `toLocaleString()`. Once asked, the column's `type` picks how:

- **Dates** go through `Intl.DateTimeFormat`: the date alone for `type: "date"`, the time alone for `"time"`, both otherwise.
- **Numbers** in a `number`, `decimal`, `currency` or `percent` column go through `Intl.NumberFormat`. A `currency` column shows a symbol once `format.currency` names one, and two fraction digits until then; a `percent` column reads `0.25` as 25%. A number in any other column is always shown as it is, so a numeric id stays `1001`.

`format` takes the options of whichever `Intl` formatter applies, and `locale` picks the language for every column at once:

```tsx
const columns: readonly ColumnDefinition<Row>[] = [
  { field: "Name", header: "Product" },
  { field: "Price", type: "currency", format: { currency: "EUR" } },
  { field: "Shipped", type: "date", format: { dateStyle: "medium" } },
  { field: "Margin", type: "percent", format: { maximumFractionDigits: 1 } },
];

<DataGrid columns={columns} dataSource={rows} locale="de-DE" />;
// Price reads "1.234,50 €", Shipped "15.03.2024", Margin "12,5 %"
```

Number options are laid over the type's defaults, so `{ maximumFractionDigits: 0 }` on a currency column keeps its symbol. Date options replace the defaults, since `dateStyle` cannot be combined with individual fields.

`valueFormatter` decides the text outright, for anything `Intl` cannot express. It receives the row too — `undefined` when the value is an aggregate result or a group's value, which belong to no single row:

```tsx
{
  field: "Weight",
  valueFormatter: (value) => `${String(value)} kg`,
}
```

A `count` or `countDistinct` aggregate is a number of rows rather than a value from the column, so it always reads as a plain number. The same text is what `formatCellValue` in `@gridkitjs/core` returns, for building it outside the grid. Reach for a [`cellTemplate`](/docs/react/column-templates) when a cell needs markup — a link, a badge, a conditional style — rather than different text.

## Column visibility

A column with `hidden: true` is not rendered, but it is still a column of the grid: a sort, filter or grouping on it still applies, and it keeps its place in the column order, so showing it again puts it back where it was. `defaultColumnVisibility` overrides `hidden` per column id to start with, and the ref's `showColumns` and `hideColumns` change it afterwards:

```tsx
const gridRef = useRef<DataGridApi<Row>>(null);

<DataGrid
  ref={gridRef}
  columns={[
    { field: "Name" },
    { field: "Region" },
    { field: "Notes", hidden: true },
  ]}
  dataSource={rows}
  defaultColumnVisibility={{ Region: false }}
  onColumnVisibilityChange={({ columnIds, visibility }) => persist(visibility)}
/>;

gridRef.current?.showColumns(["Notes"]);
gridRef.current?.hideColumns(["Name", "Region"]);
```

The state is a `ColumnVisibilityState` — column id to `true` (shown) or `false` (hidden) — holding only the columns that were changed; one absent from it follows its definition. `onColumnVisibilityChange` fires once per call that changes something, listing every column it touched. `getColumnVisibility()` reads the state, `useColumnVisibilityState(gridRef)` follows it from a component outside the grid, `getColumns()` lists what is shown, and `getDataColumns()` lists every column, hidden ones included. `aria-colcount` counts only the columns shown. To hold the state yourself, pass it as the controlled `columnVisibility` prop — `showColumns` and `hideColumns` then ask through `onColumnVisibilityChange` instead of changing it; see [controlled state](/docs/react/state).

`hideable: false` keeps the user from hiding a column: the header's context menu leaves out its "Hide column" command, and the [column chooser](/docs/react/column-chooser) shows the column checked and disabled. Like `sortable`, it gates only the user's ways to do it — `hideColumns` still hides the column.

## See also

- [DataGrid](/docs/react/data-grid) for the `columns` prop itself, and the grid-level defaults (`resizableColumns`, `reorderableColumns`, `sortableColumns`, `groupableColumns`, `groupToggleIconColumns`, `groupByDraggableColumns`) each per-column override falls back to.
- [Column templates](/docs/react/column-templates), [resizing](/docs/react/column-resizing), [reordering](/docs/react/column-reordering), [sorting](/docs/react/column-sorting), [filtering](/docs/react/column-filtering), and the [column chooser](/docs/react/column-chooser), each in depth.
- [Row grouping](/docs/react/row-grouping) for `groupable`, `groupToggleIcon`, and `groupByDraggable`, in depth.
- [Aggregate functions](/docs/react/aggregate-functions) for `footerTemplate`, in depth.
- [TypeScript](/docs/react/typescript) for what `field` accepts and typing a column list.

docs.title: Column filter menu
docs.description: A filter popup per column, opened from its header — its sort entries, its editor, and Clear filter, Cancel and OK — turned on with filterableColumns.
docs.body:
A column with a filter menu opens a small dialog below its header for filtering that column: the column's sort entries at the top, an editor for its filter, and buttons to clear the filter, cancel or apply. It edits the grid's one [filter](/docs/react/column-filtering), so the menu, the toolbar's search box, `setFilter` and a controlled `filter` always agree.

Three things open it, each [described below](#opening-it): the funnel button in a filterable header, <Kbd>Alt</Kbd>+<Kbd>Shift</Kbd>+<Kbd>ArrowDown</Kbd> on a focused header, and "Filter…" in a header's context menu. `<DataGrid {...excelFilter} />` turns the whole feature on in its Excel-style form — see [presets](#presets).

<FilterMenuExample />

## Turning it on

```tsx
<DataGrid
  columns={[
    { field: "Id", filterable: false },
    { field: "Customer" },
    { field: "Amount", type: "number" },
  ]}
  dataSource={orders}
  sortableColumns
  filterableColumns
  contextMenu
/>
```

`filterableColumns` gives every column a filter menu unless the column's own `filterable` says otherwise; it is off by default, like `sortableColumns`. The filter applies either way: a column without a menu is still filtered by `defaultFilter`, `setFilter` or a search.

| Prop                | Type                      | Default | Description                                                                     |
| ------------------- | ------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `filterableColumns` | `boolean`                 | `false` | Whether columns get a filter menu, unless a column says otherwise.              |
| `column.filterable` | `boolean`                 |         | Per-column override of `filterableColumns`.                                     |
| `filterMenu`        | `GridFilterMenuOptions`   |         | How the grid's filter menus look — see [options](#options).                     |
| `column.filterMenu` | `ColumnFilterMenuOptions` |         | Per-column override of `filterMenu.ui`, and the operators its conditions offer. |

### Options

`filterMenu` sets every filter menu of the grid; a column's own `filterMenu` overrides it, setting by setting.

| Option                        | Type                        | Default         | Description                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ----------------------------- | --------------------------- | --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `filterMenu.ui`               | `"simple" \| "excel"`       | `"simple"`      | Which editor the menu opens: [conditions](#the-simple-editor) or a [checklist of values](#the-excel-editor). Every editor edits the one filter, so switching keeps it intact. |
| `filterMenu.showCounts`       | `boolean`                   | `false`         | For the checklist editor: whether each value shows how many rows hold it.                                                                                                     |
| `filterMenu.valueLimit`       | `number`                    | `10000`         | For the checklist editor: how many values it lists before asking for a search first.                                                                                          |
| `column.filterMenu.ui`        | `"simple" \| "excel"`       | `filterMenu.ui` | Which editor this column's menu opens.                                                                                                                                        |
| `column.filterMenu.operators` | `readonly FilterOperator[]` | by `type`       | The conditions this column offers, in order, in place of its type's — see [the simple editor](#the-simple-editor). `in` is dropped, since only a checklist picks values.      |

## Opening it

- **The header's filter button.** A filterable header shows a funnel at its end, beside the sort toggle — faint until the header is hovered or focused, and marked while the column is filtered. Pressing it opens the menu, and pressing it again closes it.
- **The keyboard.** <Kbd>Alt</Kbd>+<Kbd>Shift</Kbd>+<Kbd>ArrowDown</Kbd> on a focused header opens it. The header's `aria-keyshortcuts` lists the key, as it does its others.
- **A header's context menu.** With [`contextMenu`](/docs/react/context-menu) on, a filterable header's menu lists "Filter…" after its sort entries, then "Clear filter", which clears the column's filter without opening anything — disabled while the column is not filtered.
- **The ref.** `openFilterMenu(columnId)` opens it, and returns whether it did: not for a column with no filter menu, nor a hidden one, which has no header to open below. `closeFilterMenu()` closes it, leaving the column chooser alone. `runCommand("filter.open", { area: "header", columnId })` opens it too, reporting to `onCommand` as the API's.

It opens below the header and gives focus back to it when it closes. Only one panel is open at a time: opening a filter menu replaces the column chooser, or another column's filter menu.

```tsx
const gridRef = useRef<DataGridApi<Order>>(null);

<DataGrid
  ref={gridRef}
  columns={columns}
  dataSource={orders}
  filterableColumns
/>;

<button onClick={() => gridRef.current?.openFilterMenu("Customer")}>
  Filter customers
</button>;
```

## The filtered state

While a column with a filter menu is filtered — by the menu, `setFilter`, a controlled `filter` or anything else naming the column — its header's filter button stays shown, in accent, and the header carries `aria-description="Filtered"`, so a screen reader says so as it reads the header. A search across every column marks none, and a column without a filter menu shows no filtered state, however it is filtered.

## What it shows

- **The column's sort entries** — "Sort ascending", "Sort descending" and "Clear sort", the header menu's own — while the column [sorts](/docs/react/column-sorting). Choosing one sorts the column and closes the menu; "Sort ascending" or "Sort descending" is pressed while the column sorts that way.
- **The editor**, for the column's filter — [the simple editor](#the-simple-editor), or with `filterMenu.ui: "excel"` [the excel editor](#the-excel-editor).
- **"Clear filter"**, which takes every entry about the column out of the filter and closes the menu — whichever editor wrote them, or none did, as with a predicate set in code. Disabled while the column is not filtered.
- **Cancel** and **OK**. The editor edits a draft, so nothing filters until OK applies it; Cancel drops it.

## The simple editor

One condition — an operator and a value — and an optional second, joined to the first by **And** or **Or**:

- **The operator** lists the conditions the column offers, in its type's words: "Before" and "After" on a date column where a number reads "Less than" and "Greater than".
- **The value** goes in a box made for the column's `type`: a number box, a date picker on a `"date"` column, a date-and-time picker on a `"dateTime"` or `"time"` one, a true/false choice on a `"boolean"` one, and a text box on the rest. "Between" takes two, From and To; "Is blank" and "Is not blank" take none.
- **The second condition** is optional: left empty, it is dropped.

| Column `type`                                      | Its conditions, by default                                                                                                        |
| -------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `"string"`, or none                                | Contains, Does not contain, Equals, Does not equal, Starts with, Ends with, Is blank, Is not blank                                |
| `"number"`, `"decimal"`, `"currency"`, `"percent"` | Equals, Does not equal, Greater than, Greater than or equal to, Less than, Less than or equal to, Between, Is blank, Is not blank |
| `"date"`                                           | Equals, Does not equal, Before, After, Between, Is blank, Is not blank                                                            |
| `"dateTime"`, `"time"`                             | Before, After, Between, Is blank, Is not blank — a moment seldom equals a typed minute to the millisecond                         |
| `"boolean"`                                        | Equals, Is blank, Is not blank                                                                                                    |

A column's `filterMenu.operators` lists its own instead — `{ field: "Amount", type: "number", filterMenu: { operators: ["gt", "lt", "between"] } }`.

OK, or <Kbd>Enter</Kbd>, applies the conditions in place of every entry about the column, keeping every other column's: one condition as one operator entry, two as a group with their combinator.

```ts
// "Score" between 10 and 25
[{ columnId: "score", operator: "between", value: [10, 25] }];

// "Name" contains "Ch" or starts with "Al"
[
  {
    combinator: "or",
    entries: [
      { columnId: "name", operator: "contains", value: "Ch" },
      { columnId: "name", operator: "startsWith", value: "Al" },
    ],
  },
];
```

Once the grid has drawn the rows the filter keeps, the live region announces how many of all the rows they are — "2 of 3 rows", the `filterResults` message, its counts in the grid's [`locale`](/docs/react/localization#counts) ("1,204 of 10,000 rows") — so a screen reader hears the result as focus returns to the header. A controlled `filter` that doesn't take the change announces nothing.

Opened again, the menu shows the conditions as they are applied, whatever applied them: the menu itself, `defaultFilter`, `setFilter` or a controlled `filter`. A condition set in code with an operator the column doesn't offer still shows, its operator listed for it.

- **A value that doesn't read** — a condition left without one, a number the box can't read, a date missing its year, a "Between" missing an end — keeps the menu open. The box is marked invalid, described by a message ("Enter a number"), and takes focus. OK on conditions left as they opened, with nothing typed in them, just closes the menu.
- **A filter the editor can't show** — a text query, a predicate, a group across columns, or a list of values — reads "Custom filter" above empty conditions. It stays as it is until conditions are applied in its place, or "Clear filter" takes it out.

## The excel editor
