With `filterMenu.ui: "excel"` — the grid's, or a column's own — the menu lists the values the column holds, each with a checkbox, as a spreadsheet's filter does:

```tsx
<DataGrid
  columns={columns}
  dataSource={orders}
  filterableColumns
  filterMenu={{ ui: "excel", showCounts: true }}
/>
```

- **The values** are the column's distinct values, in the order the column sorts, labelled as its cells print them — a date as the column formats it, a boolean in the `booleanTrue` and `booleanFalse` words. With `showCounts`, each shows how many rows hold it. Blank cells — `null`, `undefined` or `""` — are one item of their own, "(Blanks)", last.
- **They cascade.** The list holds the values of the rows the _other_ columns' filters keep, so with "Region" filtered to "North", "Customer" lists only the customers in the north. A column's own filter never hides its values: the ones it leaves out stay listed, to be checked again.
- **The search box** narrows the list to the values whose label holds what is typed, ignoring case.
- **"Select all"** checks every value the search shows, or unchecks them once all are — "(Blanks)" too while nothing is searched. It is a native checkbox, shown mixed while only some are checked.
- **A long list** draws only the values near its scroll position, so a column of thousands of values opens as quickly as one of ten. Past `filterMenu.valueLimit` values — 10,000 by default — it lists none until something is searched ("Type to search 12,000 values"), and a search matching more lists the first of them, saying how many it left out ("250 more, refine the search"). "Select all" still covers every value meanwhile.
- **"Text filters"** — "Number filters", "Date filters" or "Boolean filters", by the column's `type` — sits above the search box and opens a menu of the conditions the column offers, the simple editor's, beside the filter menu. Choosing one shows [the simple editor](#the-simple-editor) in place of the checklist, its first condition at the one chosen, under "Back to values", which brings the checklist back as it was left. A column whose `filterMenu.operators` is empty offers no menu.

OK, or <Kbd>Enter</Kbd>, applies the checked values in place of every entry about the column, keeping every other column's. Every value checked is no filter at all; anything less is one `in` entry holding the values checked, OR-ed with "is blank" while "(Blanks)" stays checked:

```ts
// "Name": Alice and Bravo checked
[{ columnId: "name", operator: "in", value: ["Alice", "Bravo"] }];

// "Joined": one day and the blanks checked
[
  {
    combinator: "or",
    entries: [
      { columnId: "joined", operator: "in", value: [new Date(2024, 4, 20)] },
      { columnId: "joined", operator: "isEmpty" },
    ],
  },
];
```

The `in` entry holds the values checked rather than the ones left out, so a value that turns up later, in a new row, stays filtered out until it is checked. The rows the filter keeps are announced as [the simple editor's](#the-simple-editor) are.

With a condition chosen from "Text filters", OK applies the conditions instead, as the simple editor does — in place of the values checked, since a column is filtered by its values or by conditions, never both, as in Excel.

Opened again, the menu shows the values checked as they are applied, whatever applied them.

- **Conditions**, as the simple editor or `setFilter` writes them, open with every value checked under "Filtered by condition", the "Text filters" button ticked and the operators they use checked in its menu — choosing one opens the conditions as applied, the first at that operator, its value kept. **A filter the editor can't show** — a text query, a predicate, a group across columns — opens under "Custom filter". Either stays as it is until a value is checked or unchecked, or a condition applied, replacing it, or "Clear filter" takes it out.
- **OK on checks left as they opened**, whatever was searched, just closes the menu.

### Switching editors

`filterMenu.ui` can change at any time — from a toggle in your app, say — and every filter stays as it is, since both editors edit the one filter. Each opens on as much of it as it can show: conditions in the simple editor, or through the excel editor's "Text filters" menu; checked values in the excel editor, which the simple editor reads as "Custom filter". A filter set in code — `defaultFilter`, `setFilter` or a controlled `filter` — shows in whichever editor is on.

```tsx
const [ui, setUi] = useState<"simple" | "excel">("simple");

<button onClick={() => setUi(ui === "simple" ? "excel" : "simple")}>
  Switch filter editor
</button>;
<DataGrid
  columns={columns}
  dataSource={orders}
  filterableColumns
  filterMenu={{ ui }}
/>;
```

## Presets

`excelFilter` is the options for the excel editor as one plain value — `{ filterableColumns: true, filterMenu: { ui: "excel", showCounts: true } }` — so a grid takes the whole feature in a spread:

```tsx
import { DataGrid, excelFilter } from "@gridkitjs/react";

<DataGrid {...excelFilter} columns={columns} dataSource={orders} />;
```

A prop written after the spread overrides the preset, and one written before it is overridden by it. `filterMenu` is replaced whole, not merged setting by setting, so `filterMenu={{ ui: "simple" }}` after the spread brings the simple editor back and also drops the counts. To change one setting and keep the rest, spread the preset's own:

```tsx
<DataGrid {...excelFilter} filterMenu={{ ...excelFilter.filterMenu, ui }} />
```

The preset is core's, with the same names in every renderer — see [filtering](/docs/core/filtering#presets).

## Keyboard & pointer interactions

The menu is a dialog that holds a draft, so it keeps focus: tabbing out of it would drop the draft.

| Key or action                                                            | Does                                                                                          |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| <Kbd>Alt</Kbd>+<Kbd>Shift</Kbd>+<Kbd>ArrowDown</Kbd> on a focused header | Opens its filter menu.                                                                        |
| Opening it                                                               | Focus goes to the first condition's value box — or its operator, when that takes no value.    |
| Opening the excel editor                                                 | Focus goes to its search box.                                                                 |
| <Kbd>Tab</Kbd> / <Kbd>Shift</Kbd>+<Kbd>Tab</Kbd>                         | The next or previous control, wrapping round inside the menu. A disabled button is passed by. |
| <Kbd>ArrowDown</Kbd> / <Kbd>ArrowUp</Kbd> in the checklist               | The next or previous value. The checklist is one stop for <Kbd>Tab</Kbd>.                     |
| <Kbd>Home</Kbd> / <Kbd>End</Kbd> in the checklist                        | The first or last value, however long the list.                                               |
| <Kbd>PageDown</Kbd> / <Kbd>PageUp</Kbd> in the checklist                 | As many values down or up as the list shows at once.                                          |
| <Kbd>Space</Kbd> in the checklist, or a click on a value                 | Checks or unchecks the value.                                                                 |
| <Kbd>Enter</Kbd> or <Kbd>ArrowDown</Kbd> on "Text filters"               | Opens its menu of conditions on the first; <Kbd>ArrowUp</Kbd> on the last.                    |
| <Kbd>ArrowDown</Kbd> / <Kbd>ArrowUp</Kbd> in that menu                   | The next or previous condition. <Kbd>Enter</Kbd> chooses it, in place of the checklist.       |
| <Kbd>Escape</Kbd> or <Kbd>Tab</Kbd> in that menu                         | Closes only the menu, giving focus back to "Text filters".                                    |
| <Kbd>Enter</Kbd>                                                         | Anywhere but on a button — a box, a picker, a checkbox, the checklist — applies, as OK does.  |
| <Kbd>Escape</Kbd>                                                        | Closes it without applying, giving focus back to the header.                                  |
| A click outside it, a scroll or a resize                                 | Closes it without applying.                                                                   |

<Kbd>Escape</Kbd> closes only the menu: it never reaches the grid, so the
selection stays.

## Commands and `onCommand`

"Filter…" and "Clear filter" are the [built-in commands](/docs/core/commands#built-in-commands) `filter.open` and `filter.clear`, shown only on the header of a column with a filter menu. The menu's sort entries and its "Clear filter" run the same commands, so a [command of your own](/docs/react/context-menu#commands-of-your-own) with one of their ids replaces it inside the menu too, and `onCommand` hears each one with the source `"filterMenu"`:

```tsx
<DataGrid
  columns={columns}
  dataSource={orders}
  filterableColumns
  onCommand={({ commandId, target, source }) => {
    // "filterMenu" for a sort entry or "Clear filter" chosen in the menu.
    track(commandId, source);
  }}
/>
```

## Messages

Every string the menu shows is a message — see [localization](/docs/react/localization):

| Key                        | Default                                                                    |
| -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `openFilter`               | "Filter…" — `filter.open`'s label.                                         |
| `clearColumnFilter`        | "Clear filter" — `filter.clear`'s label, and the menu's button.            |
| `filterMenuLabel`          | "Name filter" — the dialog's accessible name, after its column.            |
| `columnFiltered`           | "Filtered" — a filtered column's header's description.                     |
| `applyFilter`              | "OK"                                                                       |
| `cancelFilter`             | "Cancel"                                                                   |
| `filterOperatorLabel`      | "Before" — a condition's operator, in its column type's words.             |
| `filterConditionLabel`     | "Condition 1" — a condition's accessible name.                             |
| `filterOperatorFieldLabel` | "Operator" — its operator picker's accessible name.                        |
| `filterValueLabel`         | "Value" — its value box's accessible name.                                 |
| `filterFromLabel`          | "From" — a "Between" condition's first box.                                |
| `filterToLabel`            | "To" — its second box.                                                     |
| `filterCombinatorLabel`    | "Combine conditions" — the And/Or choice's accessible name.                |
| `filterAnd`                | "And"                                                                      |
| `filterOr`                 | "Or"                                                                       |
| `filterValueInvalid`       | "Enter a number" — under a value that doesn't read, by the column's type.  |
| `customFilter`             | "Custom filter" — above either editor, for a filter it can't show itself.  |
| `filterResults`            | "2 of 3 rows" — announced once the rows an applied filter keeps are drawn. |
| `filterSearchLabel`        | "Search values" — the excel editor's search box's accessible name.         |
| `searchPlaceholder`        | "Search…" — its placeholder, shared with the toolbar's search box.         |
| `filterSelectAll`          | "Select all" — the checkbox over the values the search shows.              |
| `filterValuesLabel`        | "Values" — the checklist's accessible name.                                |
| `filterBlanks`             | "(Blanks)" — the checklist's item for blank cells.                         |
| `filterSearchFirst`        | "Type to search 12,000 values" — in place of a list past `valueLimit`.     |
| `filterMoreValues`         | "250 more, refine the search" — under a search matching more.              |
| `filterByCondition`        | "Filtered by condition" — above the checklist, for conditions.             |
| `filterOperatorMenu`       | "Number filters" — the button opening the column's conditions, by type.    |
| `filterBackToValues`       | "Back to values" — the button from a condition back to the checklist.      |

The theme's classes for it are listed under [filter menu](/docs/theme-tailwind#filter-menu), and the header's filter button under [header](/docs/theme-tailwind#header).

## See also

- [Column filtering](/docs/react/column-filtering) for the filter value the menu edits.
- [Column sorting](/docs/react/column-sorting) for the sort items in the same menu.
- [core: Filtering](/docs/core/filtering) for the editor model.

docs.body:
`selectable.columns` takes a `SelectionMode`: `false`, `"single"` or `"multiple"`. It is off by default, since selection claims the click a display-only grid shouldn't. A column click replaces the selection, <Kbd>Ctrl</Kbd>+click toggles one column in or out, and <Kbd>Shift</Kbd>+click takes every column between the last click and this one.

## Multi-select columns

## Props

| Prop                                   | Type                                          | Default | Description                                                                                                                 |
| -------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `selectable.columns`                   | `false \| "single" \| "multiple"`             | `false` | How many columns the user may select at once.                                                                               |
| `defaultColumnSelection`               | `SelectionState`                              |         | Column ids selected to start with. Uncontrolled.                                                                            |
| `columnSelection`                      | `SelectionState`                              |         | The selected column ids, controlled — changed only through the column callbacks. See [controlled state](/docs/react/state). |
| `onColumnSelect / onColumnsSelect`     | `(event) => void`                             |         | Once per column newly selected, and once per interaction with every column it selected.                                     |
| `onColumnDeselect / onColumnsDeselect` | `(event) => void`                             |         | The deselecting counterpart of each, above.                                                                                 |
| `onColumnSelectionChange`              | `(event: ColumnSelectionChangeEvent) => void` |         | Once per change with what it added, what it removed, and everything selected after — the one to persist from.               |

## Payload shapes

`onColumnSelect`/`onColumnDeselect` fire a `ColumnSelectEvent<Row>`, `onColumnsSelect`/`onColumnsDeselect` a `ColumnsSelectEvent<Row>`, and `onColumnSelectionChange` a `ColumnSelectionChangeEvent<Row>` — the one to persist from:

| Type                              | Field       | Type                             | Description                                                    |
| --------------------------------- | ----------- | -------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ColumnSelectEvent<Row>`          | `column`    | `SelectedColumn<Row>`            | The column selected or deselected.                             |
|                                   | `selection` | `SelectionState`                 | Every selected column's id, at that point.                     |
| `ColumnsSelectEvent<Row>`         | `columns`   | `readonly SelectedColumn<Row>[]` | Every column this interaction selected or deselected.          |
|                                   | `selection` | `SelectionState`                 | Every selected column's id, at that point.                     |
| `ColumnSelectionChangeEvent<Row>` | `added`     | `readonly SelectedColumn<Row>[]` | Columns this interaction newly selected.                       |
|                                   | `removed`   | `readonly SelectedColumn<Row>[]` | Columns this interaction deselected.                           |
|                                   | `selected`  | `readonly SelectedColumn<Row>[]` | Every selected column, not only what this interaction changed. |
|                                   | `selection` | `SelectionState`                 | The same columns, as ids only.                                 |

Each carries the column as a `SelectedColumn<Row>`:

| Field         | Type                  | Description                                                                                           |
| ------------- | --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `columnId`    | `string`              | The column's id.                                                                                      |
| `column`      | `ResolvedColumn<Row>` | The resolved column — see [imperative handle](/docs/react/imperative-handle#resolved-row-and-column). |
| `columnIndex` | `number`              | Position among the columns as displayed, so after any reorder.                                        |

## Reading selection outside the grid's own tree

`useSelectionState`, documented on [row selection](/docs/react/row-selection#reading-selection-outside-the-grids-own-tree), covers row, column, and cell selection together as one hook rather than three — its `columnSelection` field is this page's `SelectionState`.

## Keyboard

Focus a header with the arrow keys, then press <Kbd>Enter</Kbd> to select its column alone, or <Kbd>Space</Kbd> to add it to the selection or remove it, as <Kbd>Ctrl</Kbd>+click does. <Kbd>Shift</Kbd> with either takes every column between the last one selected and this one. See [accessibility](/docs/react/accessibility#keyboard-navigation) for the full keyboard model.

## See also

- [Row selection](/docs/react/row-selection) and [cell selection](/docs/react/cell-selection) for the other two areas.
- [Accessibility](/docs/react/accessibility) for the keyboard model.
- [core: Selection](/docs/core/selection) for the framework-free primitives.

docs.title: Context menu
docs.description: The grid's own menu on headers, rows and group rows: sort, filter, group, copy, select, autofit, hide and choose columns, opened by right-click or Shift+F10.
docs.body:
`contextMenu` gives the grid a menu of its own in place of the browser's. A right-click or a touch long-press on a column header, a data cell or a group row — or <Kbd>Shift</Kbd>+<Kbd>F10</Kbd> or the <Kbd>ContextMenu</Kbd> key on a focused one — opens a menu of what can be done there: sort the column, filter it, group by it, size it to its content, hide it or open the column chooser; copy the cell, its row or the selection to the clipboard; select every row on the page or clear the selection; expand or collapse every group. It is off by default, like every other GridKit feature: without `contextMenu`, a right-click shows the browser's menu.

## Turning it on

```ts
<DataGrid
  columns={columns}
  dataSource={rows}
  sortableColumns
  resizableColumns
  groupableColumns
  selectable={{ rows: "multiple" }}
  contextMenu
/>
```

`contextMenu` alone shows the default menus. Each item is a [built-in command](/docs/core/commands#built-in-commands) and shows only where it has something to act on, so a column that cannot sort has no sort items and a grid without `resizableColumns` no autofit.

### Areas

Each part of the grid that opens a menu is an **area**, with its own menu:

| Area     | Where                                                                                                             | Menu name          |
| -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------ |
| `header` | A column header.                                                                                                  | "Name column menu" |
| `cell`   | A data cell — a menu for its row and cell.                                                                        | "Row menu"         |
| `group`  | A group header row.                                                                                               | "Group menu"       |
| `body`   | The body's empty space: below the last row of a grid with a `height`, or a grid with no rows. No menu by default. | "Grid menu"        |

A group's summary row, the footer, the pager and the group-by bar keep the browser's menu.

### Default items

The header menu:

| Item                      | Command             | Shown when                                                                                   |
| ------------------------- | ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Sort ascending            | `sort.ascending`    | The column is sortable. Checked while it sorts ascending.                                    |
| Sort descending           | `sort.descending`   | The column is sortable. Checked while it sorts descending.                                   |
| Clear sort                | `sort.clear`        | The column is sortable; disabled until it is sorted. Leaves the rest of a multi-column sort. |
| Filter…                   | `filter.open`       | The column is filterable. Opens its [filter menu](/docs/react/column-filter-menu).           |
| Clear filter              | `filter.clear`      | The column is filterable; disabled until it is filtered.                                     |
| Group by _column_         | `group.add`         | The column is groupable and not grouped.                                                     |
| Stop grouping by _column_ | `group.remove`      | The column is grouped.                                                                       |
| Autofit column            | `column.autoFit`    | The column is resizable.                                                                     |
| Autofit all columns       | `column.autoFitAll` | Any column is resizable.                                                                     |
| Hide column               | `column.hide`       | The column's `hideable` is not `false`; disabled for the last column shown.                  |
| Choose columns            | `column.choose`     | Always. Opens the [column chooser](/docs/react/column-chooser) below the header.             |

The cell menu:

| Item                | Command                   | Shown when                                                    |
| ------------------- | ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Copy cell           | `copy.cell`               | Always; disabled on a column with `exportable: false`.        |
| Copy row            | `copy.row`                | Always. Copies the row's shown cells.                         |
| Copy selection      | `copy.selection`          | Anything is selectable; disabled until something is selected. |
| Select all rows     | `selection.selectAllRows` | `selectable.rows` is `"multiple"`; disabled with no rows.     |
| Clear selection     | `selection.clear`         | Anything is selectable; disabled until something is selected. |
| Expand all groups   | `group.expandAll`         | The grid is grouped.                                          |
| Collapse all groups | `group.collapseAll`       | The grid is grouped.                                          |

The copy items put the cell, the row or the selection on the clipboard — see [clipboard](/docs/react/clipboard).

The group menu:

| Item                      | Command             | Shown when                                     |
| ------------------------- | ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| Expand all groups         | `group.expandAll`   | Always — there is a group to open it on.       |
| Collapse all groups       | `group.collapseAll` | Always.                                        |
| Stop grouping by _column_ | `group.remove`      | Always: it stops grouping by the row's column. |

Separators fall between the groups of items, and collapse when the items around them are hidden. A place whose menu would be empty — an area given only items that hide there, say — shows the browser's menu instead.

## Choosing the items

An object lists an area's menu yourself, in the menu vocabulary of [@gridkitjs/core](/docs/core/commands#menus) — command ids and `"separator"`. An area left out keeps its defaults:

```ts
<DataGrid
  columns={columns}
  dataSource={rows}
  sortableColumns
  contextMenu={{
    header: ["sort.ascending", "sort.descending", "separator", "column.hide"],
    cell: ["selection.clear"],
  }}
/>
```

`[]` turns an area's menu off and leaves the browser's there — `{ header: [] }` keeps the menu on rows and group rows alone. `defaultContextMenu`, exported from @gridkitjs/core, holds each area's defaults, to build on.

No default menu exports. The export commands — `export.csv`, `export.json`, `exportSelection.csv` and the rest — show in the `cell` and `body` menus when you list them, and download the whole grid's export from either: see [export](/docs/react/export#from-the-context-menu). `print` does the same for [printing](/docs/react/printing#from-the-context-menu).

### Items of your own

Beside command ids, a menu holds items written into it — `{ type: "item", id, label, onSelect }` — and submenus — `{ type: "submenu", id, label, items }`. An item with `checked` is a checkable one, drawn as a `menuitemcheckbox`; `hidden`, `disabled` and `checked` each take a boolean or a function of the context. `onSelect` receives the [command context](/docs/core/commands#the-context): the grid's state, its actions, the target, and the `row` and `column` a cell's menu opened on.

```ts
<DataGrid
  columns={columns}
  dataSource={orders}
  getRowId={(order) => order.id}
  selectable={{ rows: "multiple" }}
  contextMenu={{
    cell: [
      {
        type: "item",
        id: "orders.open",
        label: "Open order",
        onSelect: ({ row }) => openOrder(row?.row),
      },
      {
        type: "submenu",
        id: "orders.mark",
        label: "Mark as",
        items: [
          { type: "item", id: "orders.markPaid", label: "Paid", onSelect: markPaid },
          { type: "item", id: "orders.markSent", label: "Sent", onSelect: markSent },
        ],
      },
      "separator",
      "selection.clear",
    ],
  }}
/>
```

### Working the items out each time

An area also takes a function, asked each time its menu opens with a `GridContextMenuRequest` — `{ target, defaults, context }`: where the menu opens, the area's default entries, and the grid as the menu sees it. It returns the entries to show, or `null` (or `[]`) for the browser's menu there. That is how to add to the defaults, take some out, reorder them, or vary the menu by column or row:

```ts
<DataGrid
  columns={columns}
  dataSource={orders}
  sortableColumns
  contextMenu={{
    // "Hide column" first, no autofit, and a "Pin column" of your own.
    header: ({ target, defaults }) => [
      "column.hide",
      "separator",
      ...defaults.filter(
        (entry) =>
          entry !== "column.hide" &&
          entry !== "column.autoFit" &&
          entry !== "column.autoFitAll",
      ),
      "separator",
      {
        type: "item",
        id: "pin",
        label: "Pin column",
        checked: pinned.includes(target.columnId),
        onSelect: () => togglePin(target.columnId),
      },
    ],
    // No grid menu on the Id column.
    cell: ({ target, defaults }) =>
      target.columnId === "Id" ? null : defaults,
  }}
/>
```

`target` is typed for the area — a header's carries `columnId`, a cell's `rowId` and `columnId`, a group row's `groupId` and `columnId`. A function is asked again once the menu has selected the row or column it opened on, so what it reads of the selection is what the menu acts on.

## Commands of your own

<ContextMenuExample />

An action more than one menu offers is better registered once as a [command](/docs/core/commands#commands) than written into each menu. `commands` registers them, and a menu lists one by its id, like a built-in:

```ts
const commands: readonly GridCommand<Order>[] = [
  {
    id: "orders.exportSelected",
    label: "Export selected",
    isEnabled: ({ selectedRows }) => selectedRows().length > 0,
    execute: ({ selectedRows }) => exportOrders(selectedRows()),
  },
  // Replaces the built-in everywhere it is listed: only an admin may hide.
  {
    id: "column.hide",
    label: ({ messages }) => messages.hideColumn,
    isVisible: ({ target }) => target.area === "header" && user.isAdmin,
    execute: ({ column, actions }) => {
      if (column !== null) actions.hideColumns([column.id]);
    },
  },
];

<DataGrid
  columns={columns}
  dataSource={orders}
  selectable={{ rows: "multiple" }}
  commands={commands}
  contextMenu={{
    cell: ({ defaults }) => ["orders.exportSelected", "separator", ...defaults],
  }}
  onCommand={({ commandId, source }) => analytics.track(commandId, source)}
/>;
```

A command of yours with a built-in's id replaces it in every menu that lists that id, the defaults included — a translated label, a privilege check, or different behaviour, without listing the menus again.

`onCommand` is called after a command runs — and after an inline item runs, with that item's id — with `{ commandId, target, source }`: `source` is `"contextMenu"` for a menu, `"toolbar"` for the [toolbar](/docs/react/toolbar) and `"api"` for the ref's [`runCommand`](#from-the-ref). An item that did not run — a disabled one — is not reported. The change the command made reports through its own callback too, as it always does: `onColumnSortChange` for a sort.

## Open state

The grid keeps which menu is open; there is no prop to hold it, as a context menu's open state carries a place and a position a parent rarely wants to own. `onContextMenuOpenChange` tells you as it changes, with `{ open, target }` — where the menu opened, or where the one closing had — however it opened or closed: a right-click, a key, choosing an item, <Kbd>Escape</Kbd>, a click outside, or the ref. A menu opened in place of another reports that one closing first.

```ts
<DataGrid
  columns={columns}
  dataSource={rows}
  contextMenu
  onContextMenuOpenChange={({ open, target }) => {
    setHighlighted(open && target.area === "cell" ? target.rowId : null);
  }}
/>
```

### From the ref

The [imperative handle](/docs/react/imperative-handle) opens and closes the menu, and runs a command, from your own code — a "⋯" button in a cell template, a keyboard shortcut of your own, a test:

| Member                             | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ---------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `openContextMenu(target, anchor?)` | Opens the menu `target` has — a `GridContextMenuTarget` such as `{ area: "cell", rowId, columnId }` — as a right-click there would: it selects and focuses the cell first, and closes back to it. It opens beside `anchor`, a point `{ x, y }` in viewport coordinates or an element, or else below the cell — at the edge of the grid's view nearest it for a cell the grid has scrolled out of view, and at the body's top-left corner for `{ area: "body" }`. Returns whether it opened: not for a column, row or group that is not on screen, nor where `contextMenu` gives that place no menu. |
| `closeContextMenu()`               | Closes the menu, if one is open; focus goes back to where it opened.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `runCommand(commandId, target?)`   | Runs a command — a built-in or one of `commands` — on `target`, `{ area: "grid" }` when left out, when it is visible and enabled there. Fires `onCommand` with `source: "api"`, and returns whether it ran.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |

```ts
const gridRef = useRef<DataGridApi<Order>>(null);

// A cell template's own button, opening the row's menu beside itself.
cellTemplate: ({ rowId }) => (
  <button
    type="button"
    aria-label="Row actions"
    onClick={(event) => {
      gridRef.current?.openContextMenu(
        { area: "cell", rowId, columnId: "actions" },
        event.currentTarget,
      );
    }}
  >
    ⋯
  </button>
);

gridRef.current?.runCommand("column.hide", { area: "header", columnId: "Notes" });
```

Each is safe to call from an effect: opening a menu renders nothing synchronously.

## What opening it does

- **Focus** moves to the header, cell or group row first, so closing the menu — by choosing an item, <Kbd>Escape</Kbd>, <Kbd>Tab</Kbd> or a click outside — puts focus back on it. When the item hid that column, focus goes to the header now in its place. A menu opened in the body's empty space leaves focus where it was.
- **Selection** follows the menu, kind by kind, as a click would: opening it on a column, row or cell that is not selected selects it alone, where that kind is selectable; opening it on one already in the selection keeps the selection as it is, so the menu acts on everything selected. A cell's row and the cell itself each follow their own `selectable` mode.
- **Placement** is at the pointer for a right-click or a long-press, and 4 pixels below the header, cell or group row for a key — the same gap a toolbar dropdown's menu and the column chooser leave below what they open from.
- **Changes** report and announce exactly as the user's own gesture would: "Sort ascending" fires `onColumnSortChange` and says "Name sorted ascending", "Hide column" fires `onColumnVisibilityChange` and says "Name, column hidden", "Collapse all groups" says "All groups collapsed".

The menu renders into `document.body`, so no scrolling ancestor clips it, and takes the grid's `.gridkit-light`/`.gridkit-dark` palette with it — see the [theme](/docs/theme-tailwind#overlays-and-menus) for its classes.

A cell or header template with a menu of its own keeps it: a `contextmenu` event the template's `onContextMenu` already prevented is left to it.

## Keyboard & pointer interactions

| Key or action                                            | Does                                                                                                      |
| -------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Right-click a header, cell or group row                  | Opens its menu at the pointer.                                                                            |
| Touch and hold a header, cell or group row               | Opens its menu at the touch after half a second, if the finger stays put. Lifting it then clicks nothing. |
| <Kbd>Shift</Kbd>+<Kbd>F10</Kbd> / <Kbd>ContextMenu</Kbd> | On a focused header, cell or group row, opens its menu below it.                                          |
| <Kbd>ArrowDown</Kbd> / <Kbd>ArrowUp</Kbd>                | The next or previous item, wrapping round the ends.                                                       |
| <Kbd>Home</Kbd> / <Kbd>End</Kbd>                         | The first or last item.                                                                                   |
| <Kbd>Enter</Kbd> / <Kbd>Space</Kbd>, or a click          | Runs the item and closes every menu; on a submenu item, opens it. A disabled item does nothing.           |
| <Kbd>ArrowRight</Kbd>                                    | On a submenu item, opens it and focuses its first item.                                                   |
| <Kbd>ArrowLeft</Kbd>                                     | In a submenu, closes it and focuses the item that opened it.                                              |
| A printable character                                    | Moves to the next item whose label starts with what was typed.                                            |
| <Kbd>Escape</Kbd>                                        | Closes the menu — a submenu alone, back to its item — and goes no further: the grid's selection stays.    |
| <Kbd>Tab</Kbd> / <Kbd>Shift</Kbd>+<Kbd>Tab</Kbd>         | Closes every menu.                                                                                        |

Moving the pointer over an item focuses it, and resting it on a submenu item opens that submenu. A disabled item still takes focus, so a screen reader finds it. While an area opens a menu, the `aria-keyshortcuts` of its headers, cells or group rows lists `Shift+F10`. The [theme](/docs/theme-tailwind) keys off that to give the long-press to the menu alone: on those headers, cells and group rows iOS shows no callout of its own, and a touch screen does not start selecting their text.

## Props

| Prop                      | Type                                          | Default | Description                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `contextMenu`             | `boolean \| GridContextMenuOptions<Row>`      |         | The grid's own context menu. `true` shows the defaults; `{ header, cell, group, body }` gives an area's entries, or a function of its request — `[]` or `null` for the browser's menu there. |
| `commands`                | `readonly GridCommand<Row>[]`                 |         | Your own commands, for menus to list by id. One with a built-in's id replaces it.                                                                                                            |
| `onCommand`               | `(event: GridCommandEvent) => void`           |         | Called after a command or an inline menu item runs, with `{ commandId, target, source }`.                                                                                                    |
| `onContextMenuOpenChange` | `(event: ContextMenuOpenChangeEvent) => void` |         | Called as the menu opens or closes, with `{ open, target }`.                                                                                                                                 |

Each menu's accessible name is a message — `headerMenuLabel`, "Name column menu"; `cellMenuLabel`, "Row menu"; `groupMenuLabel`, "Group menu"; `bodyMenuLabel`, "Grid menu" — and every item's label a message too; see [localization](/docs/react/localization).

## See also

- [Toolbar](/docs/react/toolbar) for the same commands in a bar.
- [Localization](/docs/react/localization) for the item labels.
- [core: Commands and menus](/docs/core/commands) for the framework-free model.

docs.title: DataGrid
docs.description: The grid component: columns, data, borders, resizing, reordering, and selection.
docs.body:
`DataGrid` takes column definitions and a data source and renders an accessible grid. Every feature is opt-in: turn it on for the whole grid with a prop such as `resizableColumns`, `reorderableColumns` or `selectable`, or per column through the column's own field, such as `resizable` or `reorderable`.

## A minimal grid

```tsx title="App.tsx"
import { DataGrid, type ColumnDefinition } from "@gridkitjs/react";

interface Task {
  id: number;
  title: string;
  owner: string;
  estimate: number;
}

const tasks: Task[] = [
  { id: 1, title: "Write the release notes", owner: "Ana", estimate: 2 },
  { id: 2, title: "Review the pull request", owner: "Marko", estimate: 1 },
  { id: 3, title: "Fix the flaky test", owner: "Ivana", estimate: 3 },
];

const columns: readonly ColumnDefinition<Task>[] = [
  { field: "title", header: "Task" },
  { field: "owner", header: "Owner" },
  { field: "estimate", header: "Estimate (h)", type: "number" },
];

export default function App() {
  return (
    <DataGrid
      columns={columns}
      dataSource={tasks}
      getRowId={(row) => String(row.id)}
      label="Tasks"
    />
  );
}
```

See the [quick start](/docs/react) for installing the package and importing its stylesheet.

## Resizable, reorderable columns

<DataGridResizeReorderExample />

## Props

`DataGridProps<Row>` is @gridkitjs/core's [`GridOptions<Row>`](/docs/core#grid-options), plus `ReactRenderSlots<Row>` — the props that name a React type: `columns`, `pager`, `infiniteScroll` and `renderToolbarItem` — plus the selection callbacks and `ref`.

| Prop                                                                                                | Type                                                               | Default                          | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `columns`                                                                                           | `readonly ColumnDefinition<Row>[]`                                 |                                  | Columns to render. Falls back to `defineColumnsFromRows(dataSource)` when omitted. See [column definitions](/docs/react/column-definition) for every field.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `dataSource`                                                                                        | `readonly Row[]`                                                   |                                  | The rows to render.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `getRowId`                                                                                          | `(row: Row, index: number) => string`                              | `row position`                   | A row's stable identity, for state keyed by it. Give one for data that sorts, filters, or pages.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `getRowProps`                                                                                       | `(row: ResolvedRow<Row>) => RowProps`                              |                                  | A class and `data-*` attributes for each data row — `{ className?, attributes? }`. See [row props](#row-props).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `onRowClick / onRowDoubleClick`                                                                     | `(event: RowPointerEvent<Row>) => void`                            |                                  | Called when a data row is clicked or double-clicked. See [events](/docs/react/events#row-clicks).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `label`                                                                                             | `string`                                                           |                                  | The grid's accessible name, announced when it takes focus — without one a screen reader announces only "grid".                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `labelledBy`                                                                                        | `string`                                                           |                                  | The id of an element naming the grid, for a heading already on the page. Takes precedence over label.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `locale`                                                                                            | `string \| readonly string[]`                                      | the browser's                    | The locale cells and aggregates without a template are formatted for, e.g. `"de-DE"`. Setting it turns on `Intl` formatting of dates and numbers in every column; without it, only a column with its own `format` is formatted. The counts in the grid's own messages follow it too. See [formatting values](/docs/react/column-definition#formatting-values) and [counts](/docs/react/localization#counts). |
| `messages`                                                                                          | `Partial<GridMessages>`                                            | English                          | The grid's own strings — pager, group-by bar, loading row, boolean and blank values, menu items and menu names, toolbar and column chooser, live announcements — replaced key by key. See [localization](/docs/react/localization).                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `contextMenu`                                                                                       | `boolean \| GridContextMenuOptions<Row>`                           | `false`                          | The grid's own menu on headers, cells, group rows and empty body space, opened by a right-click, <Kbd>Shift</Kbd>+<Kbd>F10</Kbd> or the <Kbd>ContextMenu</Kbd> key. `true` shows the defaults; an object lists an area's items. See [context menu](/docs/react/context-menu).                                                                                                                                |
| `commands`                                                                                          | `readonly GridCommand<Row>[]`                                      |                                  | Your own commands, for menus to list by id; one with a built-in's id replaces it. See [commands of your own](/docs/react/context-menu#commands-of-your-own).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `onCommand`                                                                                         | `(event: GridCommandEvent) => void`                                |                                  | Called after a command or an inline menu item runs, with `{ commandId, target, source }`. See [events](/docs/react/events#commands-and-the-context-menu).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `onContextMenuOpenChange`                                                                           | `(event: ContextMenuOpenChangeEvent) => void`                      |                                  | Called as the context menu opens or closes, with `{ open, target }`. See [open state](/docs/react/context-menu#open-state).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

## Row props

`getRowProps` gives each data row a class and `data-*` attributes worked out from the row — a class for your stylesheet to target, an attribute for a test or a script to find the row by. It takes the `ResolvedRow<Row>` and returns `{ className?, attributes? }`; group headers and summary rows are not passed to it. There is no inline `style`: styling belongs to the stylesheet, which the class already reaches.

```tsx title="App.tsx"
import { DataGrid, type ColumnDefinition } from "@gridkitjs/react";

interface Invoice {
  id: number;
  customer: string;
  status: "paid" | "open";
  dueDate: string; // ISO date, e.g. "2026-03-01"
}

const invoices: Invoice[] = [
  { id: 1, customer: "Alder & Co", status: "paid", dueDate: "2026-01-15" },
  { id: 2, customer: "Birchwood Ltd", status: "open", dueDate: "2026-02-01" },
  { id: 3, customer: "Cedar Supplies", status: "open", dueDate: "2099-12-31" },
];

const columns: readonly ColumnDefinition<Invoice>[] = [
  { field: "customer", header: "Customer" },
  { field: "status", header: "Status" },
  { field: "dueDate", header: "Due" },
];

const today = new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10);

export default function App() {
  return (
    <DataGrid
      columns={columns}
      dataSource={invoices}
      getRowId={(row) => String(row.id)}
      getRowProps={({ row }) => ({
        className:
          row.status === "open" && row.dueDate < today
            ? "is-overdue"
            : undefined,
        attributes: { "data-status": row.status },
      })}
    />
  );
}
```

```css title="index.css"
.grid-row.is-overdue {
  color: oklch(0.55 0.2 25);
}
```

It runs for each data row as the row renders, so keep it cheap. A row whose class and attributes read the same as last time is not redrawn for them, so an inline arrow returning a fresh object every time is fine.

Every data row also carries `data-gridkit-row-id`, its id as `getRowId` resolves it, whether or not `getRowProps` is given — `tr[data-gridkit-row-id="42"]` finds a row however it has been sorted or paged. The grid's own `data-gridkit-*` attributes win over one of the same name from `getRowProps`.

## Scrollable layout

Set `height` to bound the row area to a fixed size, independently scrollable, while the group-by bar, header, footer, and pager stay outside it and always visible:

```tsx title="App.tsx"
import { DataGrid, type ColumnDefinition } from "@gridkitjs/react";

interface Reading {
  id: number;
  sensor: string;
  celsius: number;
}

const readings: Reading[] = Array.from({ length: 200 }, (_, index) => ({
  id: index + 1,
  sensor: `Sensor ${String((index % 8) + 1)}`,
  celsius: 18 + ((index * 7) % 90) / 10,
}));

const columns: readonly ColumnDefinition<Reading>[] = [
  { field: "id", header: "#", type: "number", width: 80 },
  { field: "sensor", header: "Sensor" },
  { field: "celsius", header: "°C", type: "decimal" },
];

export default function App() {
  return (
    <DataGrid
      columns={columns}
      dataSource={readings}
      getRowId={(row) => String(row.id)}
      label="Readings"
      height={400}
    />
  );
}
```

Under the hood, the header, the rows, and (when `aggregates` is active) the grand-total footer each render as their own `<table>` rather than sharing one. All three carry `.gridkit-data-grid`; the header adds `.gridkit-data-grid-header`, the footer `.gridkit-data-grid-footer`, and the rows' table sits inside `div.gridkit-data-grid-body`, the scroll container `height` applies to. That's what keeps the header and footer out of the region that scrolls: they're never inside it to begin with, so there's nothing to pin in place with `position: sticky`. A consumer who wants a divider or shadow at the seam adds their own CSS targeting one of those classes directly, for example:

```css
.gridkit-data-grid-header {
  box-shadow: 0 1px 0 var(--gridkit-line);
}
```

## Server rendering

`DataGrid` renders on the server (for example, prerendered by a Next.js App Router page) and hydrates on the client without a mismatch, so it needs no client-only wrapper. The server draws the grid's initial state from its props; anything that needs the browser (measuring the grid's width under `resizeMode="fit"`, the `virtualized` row window, a `use*State` hook reading the grid's `ref`) settles once the grid has hydrated. Until then, a hook such as `usePaginationState` reads its documented pre-mount value.

## Keyboard & pointer interactions

- Drag a header's trailing edge to resize; double-click it to size the column to its content.
- With a resizable header focused, <Kbd>Alt</Kbd>+<Kbd>ArrowLeft</Kbd> / <Kbd>Alt</Kbd>+<Kbd>ArrowRight</Kbd> nudge the width and <Kbd>Alt</Kbd>+<Kbd>Enter</Kbd> sizes the column to its content; <Kbd>Escape</Kbd> cancels an in-progress resize.
- Click a sortable header's sort toggle, or focus the header and press <Kbd>Alt</Kbd>+<Kbd>ArrowUp</Kbd>, to cycle its sort; <Kbd>Shift</Kbd>+click or <Kbd>Alt</Kbd>+<Kbd>Shift</Kbd>+<Kbd>ArrowUp</Kbd> stacks it into the sort instead.
- Drag a header to reorder columns.
- With a header focused, <Kbd>Ctrl</Kbd>+<Kbd>ArrowLeft</Kbd> / <Kbd>Ctrl</Kbd>+<Kbd>ArrowRight</Kbd> reorders it via keyboard; <Kbd>Escape</Kbd> cancels an in-progress drag.
- Click a row, column, or cell to select it; <Kbd>Ctrl</Kbd>+click toggles, <Kbd>Shift</Kbd>+click takes a range. Under `selectable.toggleOnClick` a plain click toggles a row too.
- Under `selectable.rows: "multiple"`, <Kbd>Ctrl</Kbd>+<Kbd>A</Kbd> selects every data row on the current page; <Kbd>Escape</Kbd> clears every
  selection.
- Click a groupable header's group icon, or focus the header and press <Kbd>Alt</Kbd>+<Kbd>ArrowDown</Kbd>, to add or remove it from the group-by stack — or drag the header into the group-by bar, for a column that sets `groupByDraggable`.
- Click a filterable header's filter button, or focus the header and press <Kbd>Alt</Kbd>+<Kbd>Shift</Kbd>+<Kbd>ArrowDown</Kbd>, to open its [filter menu](/docs/react/column-filter-menu).
- Drag a chip in the group-by bar to reorder the stack; with a chip focused, <Kbd>Ctrl</Kbd>+<Kbd>ArrowLeft</Kbd> / <Kbd>Ctrl</Kbd>+<Kbd>ArrowRight</Kbd> moves it via keyboard.
- Click a group header, or focus it and press <Kbd>Space</Kbd>/<Kbd>Enter</Kbd>, to expand or collapse it.
- Under `contextMenu`, right-click a header, cell or group row, or focus it and press <Kbd>Shift</Kbd>+<Kbd>F10</Kbd> or <Kbd>ContextMenu</Kbd>, to open its menu.
- Under `toolbar`, <Kbd>Tab</Kbd> to the toolbar and move between its controls with <Kbd>ArrowLeft</Kbd> / <Kbd>ArrowRight</Kbd>.

These keys act only when pressed inside the grid itself. A popover or menu that a template portals into `document.body` still sits inside the grid in React's tree, and React bubbles its events through the grid's handlers — but the grid ignores them, so <Kbd>Escape</Kbd> in it leaves the selection alone and <Kbd>Ctrl</Kbd>+<Kbd>A</Kbd> in its text box selects the text.

docs.title: Events
docs.description: The callbacks DataGrid fires as a user resizes, reorders, sorts, groups, filters, pages and selects.
docs.body:
Every interaction reports through a callback prop rather than a ref or an event you have to subscribe to — and so does every change made through the [imperative handle](/docs/react/imperative-handle)'s setters and `restoreState`, with the same payload, so one callback sees every change to its slice. A setter whose value equals the current one fires nothing. Resizing, reordering, and sorting fire one each; selection fires thirteen, one per row, column, and cell transition plus a whole-selection change to persist from.

## Every callback, firing live

<EventsShowcaseExample />

## Resizing, reordering & sorting

| Prop                       | Type                                      | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `onColumnResize`           | `(event: ColumnResizeEvent) => void`      | Fires continuously with phase "move" while dragging, once with "end" on release — the one to persist. Autofitting a column fires it once, with "end".                                                                                     |
| `onColumnOrderChange`      | `(event: ColumnOrderEvent) => void`       | Fires once when the user drops a column somewhere new. A drop that leaves the order unchanged does not call it.                                                                                                                           |
| `onColumnVisibilityChange` | `(event: ColumnVisibilityEvent) => void`  | Fires once per `showColumns`/`hideColumns` call that changes something, with every column it touched (`columnIds`) and the whole `visibility` state to persist. See [column visibility](/docs/react/column-definition#column-visibility). |
| `onColumnSortChange`       | `(event: ColumnSortEvent) => void`        | Fires once when the user changes the sort — a toggle, a stack, or a clear back to "none".                                                                                                                                                 |
| `onGroupByChange`          | `(event: GroupByEvent) => void`           | Fires once when the user adds, removes, or reorders a group-by level.                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `onGroupExpansionChange`   | `(event: GroupExpansionEvent) => void`    | Fires once when the user expands or collapses a group, or every group at once.                                                                                                                                                            |
| `onFilterChange`           | `(event: FilterChangeEvent<Row>) => void` | Fires once per filter change — the toolbar's search box, the `filter.clearAll` command ("Clear filters") or a `setFilter` call on the ref — with the whole `filter` to persist. See [column filtering](/docs/react/column-filtering).     |
| `onPaginationChange`       | `(event: PaginationChangeEvent) => void`  | Fires once when the user changes the page or the page size, with `{ pagination, pageCount }`. The reset to the first page a filter, sort or regroup causes fires nothing of its own. See [pagination](/docs/react/pagination).            |

## Row clicks

| Prop               | Type                                    | Description                                                                                                                                   |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `onRowClick`       | `(event: RowPointerEvent<Row>) => void` | Fires on every click on a data row, after the click has changed the selection, so a handler reading it sees the new one.                      |
| `onRowDoubleClick` | `(event: RowPointerEvent<Row>) => void` | Fires once per double-click on a data row — the usual "open this record" gesture. Its two clicks still fire `onRowClick` and select as usual. |

Neither fires for a group header or a group's summary row; a click there expands or collapses the group. `RowPointerEvent<Row>` carries no DOM event, so a handler reads the same payload whichever renderer drew the row:

| Field      | Type                                             | Description                                                                            |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `row`      | `ResolvedRow<Row>`                               | The row clicked — its `rowId`, the `row` itself, and its position.                     |
| `columnId` | `string \| null`                                 | The column of the cell clicked, or `null` when the pointer was on no cell.             |
| `native`   | `{ ctrlKey, metaKey, shiftKey, altKey, button }` | The modifiers held and the button pressed, numbered as `MouseEvent.button` numbers it. |

```ts
<DataGrid
  columns={columns}
  dataSource={rows}
  getRowId={(row) => String(row.Id)}
  onRowDoubleClick={({ row }) => openRecord(row.row)}
/>
```

## Commands and the context menu

| Prop                      | Type                                          | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `onCommand`               | `(event: GridCommandEvent) => void`           | Fires after a command or an inline menu item runs — from a menu, the toolbar, or the ref's `runCommand` — with `{ commandId, target, source }`. One that did not run is not reported. See [commands of your own](/docs/react/context-menu#commands-of-your-own). |
| `onContextMenuOpenChange` | `(event: ContextMenuOpenChangeEvent) => void` | Fires as the context menu opens or closes, with `{ open, target }` — however it was opened or closed. A menu opened in place of another reports that one closing first. See [open state](/docs/react/context-menu#open-state).                                   |

## Selection

| Prop                                                                                                | Type                                        | Description                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `onRowSelect / onRowsSelect`                                                                        | `(event) => void`                           | Once per row newly selected, and once per interaction with every row it selected — a range selects many rows but fires `onRowsSelect` once. Payloads are `RowSelectEvent` and `RowsSelectEvent`. |
| `onRowDeselect / onRowsDeselect`                                                                    | `(event) => void`                           | The deselecting counterpart of each, above.                                                                                                                                                      |
| `onRowSelectionChange`                                                                              | `(event: RowSelectionChangeEvent) => void`  | Once per change with what it added, removed, and everything selected after.                                                                                                                      |
| `onColumnSelect / onColumnsSelect / onColumnDeselect / onColumnsDeselect / onColumnSelectionChange` | `(event) => void`                           | The same five events, for column selection.                                                                                                                                                      |
| `onCellSelect / onCellDeselect`                                                                     | `(event: CellSelectEvent) => void`          | Once for the cell selected, once for the cell deselected.                                                                                                                                        |
| `onCellSelectionChange`                                                                             | `(event: CellSelectionChangeEvent) => void` | Once per change with what was selected and deselected — one interaction can fill both, since moving between cells does so at once.                                                               |

Every payload's fields are broken down where its feature lives, rather than repeated here: [row selection](/docs/react/row-selection#payload-shape) for `RowSelectionChangeEvent`, [column selection](/docs/react/column-selection#payload-shapes) for `ColumnSelectEvent`/`ColumnsSelectEvent`/`ColumnSelectionChangeEvent`, [cell selection](/docs/react/cell-selection#payload-shapes) for `CellSelectEvent`/`CellSelectionChangeEvent`, and [row grouping](/docs/react/row-grouping) for `GroupByEvent`/`GroupExpansionEvent`.

## See also

- [Controlled and uncontrolled state](/docs/react/state) for holding the state these events report.
- [Imperative handle](/docs/react/imperative-handle) for `subscribe` and the ref's reads.
- [DataGrid](/docs/react/data-grid) for the full props list.
