docs.description: Download what the grid shows as CSV or JSON from the toolbar, the context menu or the ref, and add formats of your own through export writers.

docs.title: FAQ
docs.description: Answers to the problems that come up first: an unstyled grid, virtualized without height, paginated with infiniteScroll, and Tailwind scanning.
docs.body:
Short answers to the questions and problems that come up first, each linking to the page that covers it in full.

## The grid renders, but unstyled

The stylesheet is missing. Without it the grid renders as bare tables: no padding, borders or hover colours, and sort icons drawn as large as the header. Import the theme in a CSS file your app loads, after Tailwind itself:

```css title="src/index.css"
@import "tailwindcss";
@import "@gridkitjs/theme-tailwind/styles.css";
```

The theme is a Tailwind CSS v4 stylesheet, compiled by your app's Tailwind build, so the app needs Tailwind v4 set up. See [import the stylesheet](/docs/react#import-the-stylesheet), and [without Tailwind](/docs/theme-tailwind#without-tailwind) if your app does not use it.

## `virtualized` does nothing

`virtualized` needs `height`. Without a bounded row area there is no viewport to window rows against, so every row still mounts and the grid logs a `console.error`: "`virtualized` has no effect without `height`". Set `height` to a number of pixels or a CSS length such as `"60vh"`. See [row virtualization](/docs/react/row-virtualization).

## `paginated` and `infiniteScroll` together

They are mutually exclusive: with both set, only `paginated` takes effect, and the grid logs a `console.error` saying so. Choose one. Pages suit rows a user moves through and comes back to; infinite scroll suits a feed that grows as the user reads. See [pagination](/docs/react/pagination) and [infinite scroll](/docs/react/infinite-scroll).

## Tailwind classes in a template do not apply

A class in a `cellTemplate` or `headerTemplate` is your own code, so your Tailwind build must scan the file it is in. Tailwind v4 scans your project's source automatically, but skips `node_modules` and gitignored folders; a template in one of those needs an `@source` line for its path. The theme also registers its palette as colours (`text-accent`, `text-fg-muted`, `bg-selected` and the rest) that follow the grid's light and dark mode. See [styling a template](/docs/react/column-templates#styling-a-template).

GridKit's own packages need no `@source`: the grid renders semantic class names such as `gridkit-data-grid` and `grid-row`, and the theme's stylesheet styles them.

## A selection moves to other rows after a sort

Pass `getRowId`. Without it a row's id is its position, so a selection stays on the positions while sorting, filtering or new data moves different rows through them. See [row selection](/docs/react/row-selection).

## A screen reader announces an unnamed grid

Give the grid a name with `label`, or with `labelledBy` pointing at a visible heading's `id`. Without either, the grid has no accessible name. See [accessibility](/docs/react/accessibility).

## Does the grid fetch data from a server?

No. `dataSource` is an array, and the grid never fetches. To sort, filter and page on a server, hold that state with the controlled props and fetch with it. See [server-side data](/docs/react/server-side-data).

## Can users edit cells?

Not yet: there is no built-in editing. See [not yet](/docs/react/migrating#not-yet) for the other features GridKit does not have today.

## Does it work in the Next.js App Router?

Yes. The published bundle is marked `"use client"`, so a server component can import `DataGrid`. Function props such as `getRowId`, `cellTemplate` and event callbacks cannot be passed from a server component, though, so render the grid inside a client component of your own and pass it the rows.

## See also

- [Overview](/docs/react) for installing and a first grid.
- [From Syncfusion or AG Grid](/docs/react/migrating) for mapping another grid's props.
- [Performance](/docs/react/performance) for a slow or busy grid.
- [Theming](/docs/theme-tailwind) for the stylesheet and its tokens.

docs.title: Imperative handle
docs.description: The DataGridApi reached through DataGrid's ref: reading and setting grid state, saving and restoring it, and triggering focus, scroll and selection actions.
docs.body:
`DataGrid` accepts a `ref` typed `Ref<DataGridApi<Row>>`, for driving the grid from outside: the grid's DOM nodes, getters and a setter for every slice of its state, saving and restoring that state as a whole, and the handful of actions every grid ref carries.

```ts
import { useRef } from "react";
import { DataGrid, type DataGridApi } from "@gridkitjs/react";

const gridRef = useRef<DataGridApi<Row>>(null);

<DataGrid ref={gridRef} columns={columns} dataSource={rows} />;

gridRef.current?.scrollToRow("42");
gridRef.current?.getColumnSizing();
```

Every getter reads the grid's state at the moment it is called, so a read straight after an action sees the action's result. Every setter changes the grid as the user's own interaction would: it fires the slice's `on*Change` callback once, fires nothing when the new value equals the current one, and — for a slice you hold with a [controlled prop](/docs/react/state) such as `columnSort` — only asks, through that callback, as a click would.

## Elements

| Member    | Type                       | Description                                                                                                                                                                        |
| --------- | -------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `element` | `HTMLDivElement \| null`   | The grid's scrollable viewport element.                                                                                                                                            |
| `table`   | `HTMLTableElement \| null` | The row-area `<table>`, the one holding `<tbody>`. The header and, when aggregates are active, the footer are sibling `<table>`s outside it; `element` reaches the whole viewport. |

## Reading state

| Member                  | Returns                                     | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `getRows()`             | `readonly ResolvedRow<Row>[]`               | Rows as currently filtered and sorted — what's rendered, ungrouped.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `getDisplayRows()`      | `readonly DisplayRow<Row>[]`                | `getRows()` regrouped into the active `groupBy` — group headers interleaved with data rows, in render order. Identical to `getRows()` when `groupBy` is empty. Each group header's `aggregates` field carries that group's own computed results; under `groupAggregateDisplay: "row"`, a group's own summary row (`kind: "group-summary"`) is interleaved right after it, carrying the same `aggregates`. |
| `getPageRows()`         | `readonly DisplayRow<Row>[]`                | The current page of `getDisplayRows()` — exactly the rows the body renders. All of `getDisplayRows()` when `paginated` is off. See [pagination](/docs/react/pagination).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `getDataColumns()`      | `readonly DataColumn<Row>[]`                | Every column in its current order as `{ id, column }`, hidden ones included — what sorting, filtering and grouping read. See [column visibility](/docs/react/column-definition#column-visibility).                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `getColumns()`          | `readonly ResolvedColumn<Row>[]`            | Columns as currently sized and ordered — what's rendered, so hidden columns are left out.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `getColumnSizing()`     | `ColumnSizingState`                         | Column widths, keyed by column id.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `getColumnOrder()`      | `ColumnOrderState`                          | Column ids in their current render order.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `getColumnVisibility()` | `ColumnVisibilityState`                     | Columns shown (`true`) or hidden (`false`) since the grid mounted, keyed by id. A column absent from it follows its definition's `hidden`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `getColumnSort()`       | `ColumnSortState`                           | The active sort, in priority order.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `getFilter()`           | `FilterState<Row>`                          | The active filter. See [column filtering](/docs/react/column-filtering).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `getGroupBy()`          | `GroupByState`                              | The active group-by stack, outer to inner. See [row grouping](/docs/react/row-grouping).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `getGroupExpansion()`   | `GroupExpansionState`                       | Group ids currently collapsed.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `getPagination()`       | `PaginationState`                           | The active page and page size. See [pagination](/docs/react/pagination).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `getPageCount()`        | `number`                                    | How many pages the current page size splits the rows into — `1` whenever `paginated` is off.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `getAggregates()`       | `AggregateResults`                          | The grand-total aggregate results. See [aggregate functions](/docs/react/aggregate-functions).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `getRowSelection()`     | `SelectionState`                            | Selected row ids.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `getSelectedRows()`     | `readonly ResolvedRow<Row>[]`               | The selected rows, in selection order, among every row the filter lets through. See [row selection](/docs/react/row-selection#selecting-from-code).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `getColumnSelection()`  | `SelectionState`                            | Selected column ids.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `getCellSelection()`    | `CellSelectionState`                        | The selected cell, if any.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `getFocusedCell()`      | `{ rowIndex: number; columnIndex: number }` | The cell currently holding the grid's single tab stop.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `getState()`            | `GridState<Row>`                            | Every slice of state in one object — what `restoreState` takes back. See [saving and restoring a layout](/docs/react/state#saving-and-restoring-a-layout).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |

## Resolved row and column

`getRows()` and `getColumns()` return `ResolvedRow<Row>` and `ResolvedColumn<Row>` — the same shapes the selection events carry, resolved once here so no other doc page repeats them.

`ResolvedRow<Row>`:

| Field          | Type     | Description                                                                                        |
| -------------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `rowId`        | `string` | This row's id, as `getRowId` (or the position fallback) resolved it.                               |
| `row`          | `Row`    | The row itself.                                                                                    |
| `rowIndex`     | `number` | Position among the rows as rendered — filtered and sorted, and paginated once `paginated` is on.   |
| `datasetIndex` | `number` | This row's absolute position in the whole filtered/sorted/grouped dataset, unaffected by the page. |

`ResolvedColumn<Row>`:

| Field              | Type                            | Description                                                                                                        |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `column`           | `ColumnDefinition<Row>`         | The column definition this was resolved from.                                                                      |
| `id`               | `string`                        | The column's id.                                                                                                   |
| `width`            | `number`                        | This column's current width, in px.                                                                                |
| `sized`            | `boolean`                       | Whether `width` came from a user resize rather than the column definition or an autofit.                           |
| `label`            | `Node \| string`                | What the header shows: the column's own `headerTemplate`, else its `header`, else a label read off the field path. |
| `resizable`        | `boolean`                       | Whether this column can be resized, after the grid-level default.                                                  |
| `reorderable`      | `boolean`                       | Whether this column can be dragged, after the grid-level default.                                                  |
| `groupByDraggable` | `boolean`                       | Whether this column's header may be dragged into the group-by bar, after the grid-level default.                   |
| `alignment`        | `"left" \| "center" \| "right"` | How this column's cells align, after falling back to its type.                                                     |

## Actions

| Member                               | Description                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `focusCell(rowIndex, columnIndex)`   | Moves the grid's tab stop, and the browser's focus, to a cell.                                                                                                    |
| `clearSelection()`                   | Clears row, column, and cell selection together — the same as pressing <Kbd>Escape</Kbd>.                                                                         |
| `selectAllRows()`                    | Selects every data row on the current page, under `selectable.rows: "multiple"` only — the same as <Kbd>Ctrl</Kbd>+<Kbd>A</Kbd>.                                  |
| `selectRows(rowIds, intent?)`        | Selects rows by id within `selectable.rows`: `"replace"` (the default) or `"toggle"`. Fires the row callbacks once, or not at all when nothing changed.           |
| `expandAllGroups()`                  | Expands every group at once, as the `group.expandAll` command ("Expand all groups") does.                                                                         |
| `collapseAllGroups()`                | Collapses every group currently shown at once.                                                                                                                    |
| `goToPage(pageIndex)`                | Moves to the given page, clamped into range. Fires `onPaginationChange`, or nothing when that is the page already shown.                                          |
| `nextPage()`                         | Moves to the next page. A no-op on the last page — `onPaginationChange` doesn't fire.                                                                             |
| `previousPage()`                     | Moves to the previous page. A no-op on the first page — `onPaginationChange` doesn't fire.                                                                        |
| `setPageSize(pageSize)`              | Changes the page size, resetting to the first page.                                                                                                               |
| `showColumns(columnIds)`             | Shows the given columns, each in the place it held. Fires `onColumnVisibilityChange` once, or not at all when every one was already showing.                      |
| `hideColumns(columnIds)`             | Hides the given columns. A hidden column still sorts, filters and groups, and keeps its place in the order.                                                       |
| `scrollToRow(rowId, options?)`       | Scrolls the row with the given id into view, if it is currently shown.                                                                                            |
| `scrollToColumn(columnId, options?)` | Scrolls the column with the given id into view.                                                                                                                   |
| `autoFitColumn(columnId)`            | Sizes a shown column to fit its content, as double-clicking its resize handle does, firing `onColumnResize`. A hidden column, or one with no rows, is left alone. |
| `autoFitColumns(columnIds?)`         | `autoFitColumn` for each column given, or for every column shown when given none. Fitting more than one announces them once, as `columnsAutoFitted`.              |
| `openContextMenu(target, anchor?)`   | Opens the [context menu](/docs/react/context-menu#from-the-ref) `target` has, as a right-click there would. Returns whether it opened.                            |
| `closeContextMenu()`                 | Closes the context menu, if one is open.                                                                                                                          |
| `openColumnChooser()`                | Opens the [column chooser](/docs/react/column-chooser) at the grid's top-end corner, in place of any panel open. Closing it gives focus back to what had it.      |
| `openFilterMenu(columnId)`           | Opens a shown column's [filter menu](/docs/react/column-filter-menu) below its header. Returns whether it opened: not for a column with no filter menu.           |
| `closeFilterMenu()`                  | Closes the filter menu, if one is open, leaving any other panel open.                                                                                             |
| `runCommand(commandId, target?)`     | Runs a command by id on `target` — `{ area: "grid" }` by default — when it can run there, firing `onCommand`. Returns whether it ran.                             |
| `exportData(format, options?)`       | Exports the grid's view as a file of `format` without downloading it, and resolves to a `Blob` of it. See [export](/docs/react/export#from-the-ref).              |
| `print(options?)`                    | Prints the grid's view through the browser's print dialog, and resolves once it closes. See [printing](/docs/react/printing#from-the-ref).                        |

`options` on `scrollToRow`/`scrollToColumn` is a standard
[`ScrollIntoViewOptions`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Element/scrollIntoView),
passed straight through.

## Setting and restoring state

| Member                            | Fires                         | Description                                                                                                                                   |
| --------------------------------- | ----------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `setColumnSort(sort)`             | `onColumnSortChange`          | Replaces the sort, naming the first column whose place or direction changed.                                                                  |
| `setFilter(filter)`               | `onFilterChange`              | Replaces the filter and goes back to the first page. See [column filtering](/docs/react/column-filtering#change-the-filter-from-your-own-ui). |
| `setGroupBy(groupBy)`             | `onGroupByChange`             | Replaces the group-by stack, naming the first level that changed.                                                                             |
| `setGroupExpansion(expansion)`    | `onGroupExpansionChange`      | Replaces the collapsed groups, reported with `groupId: null`.                                                                                 |
| `setPagination(pagination)`       | `onPaginationChange`          | Replaces the page and page size as given; a page past the last shows the last.                                                                |
| `setColumnSizing(sizing)`         | `onColumnResize`              | Replaces the widths, reported as the `"end"` of a resize of the first column that changed.                                                    |
| `setColumnOrder(order)`           | `onColumnOrderChange`         | Replaces the order, naming the first column whose position changed.                                                                           |
| `setColumnVisibility(visibility)` | `onColumnVisibilityChange`    | Replaces the visibility state, naming every column whose entry changed.                                                                       |
| `setRowSelection(selection)`      | row selection callbacks       | Replaces the selected row ids as given, whatever `selectable` allows.                                                                         |
| `setColumnSelection(selection)`   | column selection callbacks    | Replaces the selected column ids as given.                                                                                                    |
| `setCellSelection(selection)`     | cell selection callbacks      | Replaces the selected cell as given, `null` for none.                                                                                         |
| `restoreState(saved)`             | each changed slice's callback | Puts back state saved earlier, whole or in part; the grid re-renders once.                                                                    |

`getState()` holds the filter as given, so a `Date` value or a predicate entry won't survive `JSON.stringify`; pass it through `serializeGridState` (exported by both `@gridkitjs/react` and `@gridkitjs/core`) before saving it. See [saving and restoring a layout](/docs/react/state#saving-and-restoring-a-layout).

## Subscribing to state changes

```ts
subscribe(listener: () => void): () => void;
```

Registers `listener` to be called after any render in which the grid's internal state may have changed — any getter above may return a different value once it fires, not just one. Returns an unsubscribe function.

Most consumers should reach for one of the `use*State` hooks built on it instead of calling `subscribe` directly — each wraps it in [`useSyncExternalStore`](https://react.dev/reference/react/useSyncExternalStore) so a component elsewhere in the tree stays reactive with no `on*Change` prop to forward and no polling:

| Hook                       | Reads                                                                                                                                                      |
| -------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `usePaginationState`       | `getPagination`, `getPageCount` — see [pagination](/docs/react/pagination#building-a-pager-outside-the-grids-own-tree).                                    |
| `useGroupByState`          | `getGroupBy`, `getGroupExpansion` — see [row grouping](/docs/react/row-grouping#building-a-group-by-ui-outside-the-grids-own-tree).                        |
| `useColumnSortState`       | `getColumnSort` — see [column sorting](/docs/react/column-sorting#reading-sort-state-outside-the-grids-own-tree).                                          |
| `useSelectionState`        | `getRowSelection`, `getColumnSelection`, `getCellSelection` — see [row selection](/docs/react/row-selection#reading-selection-outside-the-grids-own-tree). |
| `useAggregateState`        | `getAggregates` — see [aggregate functions](/docs/react/aggregate-functions#reactively-outside-the-grids-own-tree).                                        |
| `useColumnSizingState`     | `getColumnSizing`.                                                                                                                                         |
| `useColumnOrderState`      | `getColumnOrder`.                                                                                                                                          |
| `useColumnVisibilityState` | `getColumnVisibility` — see [column visibility](/docs/react/column-definition#column-visibility).                                                          |
| `useFilterState`           | `getFilter`, plus `setFilter` — see [column filtering](/docs/react/column-filtering#change-the-filter-from-your-own-ui).                                   |

Each hook falls back to an empty/zero value before the grid mounts, the same way its matching getter would if called too early.

## See also

- [DataGrid](/docs/react/data-grid) for the rest of the component's props.
- [Events](/docs/react/events) for callbacks that report the same interactions as they happen, rather than being queried on demand.
- [Row grouping](/docs/react/row-grouping) for `getGroupBy`/`getGroupExpansion`/`getDisplayRows`/`expandAllGroups`/`collapseAllGroups`, in depth.
- [Pagination](/docs/react/pagination) for `getPagination`/`getPageCount`/`goToPage`/`nextPage`/`previousPage`/`setPageSize`, in depth.
- [Aggregate functions](/docs/react/aggregate-functions) for `getAggregates`, and reading a group's own results off `getDisplayRows`, in depth.

docs.description: Feeding DataGrid rows that change on their own, from a timer, a poll or a WebSocket, while selection, sort and filter keep up.

docs.title: Localization
docs.description: Translating the grid's own strings with messages, and formatting values with locale.
docs.body:
Two props put a grid into another language, and they divide the work:

- **`locale`** formats values — dates and numbers in cells and aggregates, through `Intl`, and the counts in the grid's own messages. See [formatting values](/docs/react/column-definition#formatting-values) and [counts](#counts).
- **`messages`** replaces the grid's own strings — the pager's buttons, the group-by bar, the loading row, boolean and blank values, the labels of the [built-in commands](/docs/core/commands#built-in-commands), the names of its menus, the toolbar's search box and "More" button, the filter menu, and every [live announcement](/docs/react/accessibility#live-announcements) a screen reader hears.

Text your data supplies — cell values, headers, `label` — is already yours to choose, so neither touches it.

## Translating the grid's strings

`messages` takes a partial `GridMessages`: give the keys you want to change and the rest keep their English. A message that names something is a function, so a translation can put the name, page or count where its own grammar wants it.

```ts
import { useState } from "react";
import { DataGrid, type GridMessages } from "@gridkitjs/react";

const german: Partial<GridMessages> = {
  previousPage: "Zurück",
  nextPage: "Weiter",
  pageSizeLabel: "Zeilen pro Seite",
  pageStatus: (page, pageCount) => `Seite ${page} von ${pageCount}`,
  booleanTrue: "ja",
  booleanFalse: "nein",
  selectedCount: (count, target) =>
    `${count} ${target === "rows" ? "Zeilen" : "Spalten"} ausgewählt`,
};

const french: Partial<GridMessages> = {
  previousPage: "Précédent",
  nextPage: "Suivant",
  pageSizeLabel: "Lignes par page",
  pageStatus: (page, pageCount) => `Page ${page} sur ${pageCount}`,
  booleanTrue: "oui",
  booleanFalse: "non",
  selectedCount: (count, target) =>
    `${count} ${target === "rows" ? "lignes" : "colonnes"} sélectionnées`,
};

const translations = { "de-DE": german, "fr-FR": french };

const [language, setLanguage] = useState<keyof typeof translations>("de-DE");

<DataGrid
  columns={columns}
  dataSource={rows}
  paginated
  locale={language}
  messages={translations[language]}
/>;
```

Define each set once, outside the component, as you would `columns`. A `messages` object rebuilt on every render still works — rows are not redrawn for it unless the boolean or blank-value text actually changes — but a stable one saves the grid re-reading it.

`defaultMessages`, `createDefaultMessages` and `resolveMessages` are exported from `@gridkitjs/core` for building on the English defaults, or for a renderer of your own.

## Counts

Every count the English defaults print goes through `Intl.NumberFormat` with the grid's `locale`, as a whole number — "1,204 of 10,000 rows" under `"en"`, "1.204 of 10.000 rows" under `"de-DE"`, "1 204 of 10 000 rows" under `"fr"`. Without a `locale` the runtime's own is used, so a count of a thousand or more is grouped even on a grid that formats no cell. Counts under a thousand read the same in most locales.

A key you override is called with the plain number, as before, and prints it however you write it. To keep the grouping in a translation, format the count yourself:

```ts
const count = new Intl.NumberFormat("de-DE");

const german: Partial<GridMessages> = {
  filterResults: (shown, total) =>
    `${count.format(shown)} von ${count.format(total)} Zeilen`,
};
```

A renderer of your own gets the same defaults from `resolveMessages(messages, locale)`, or the English alone for a locale from `createDefaultMessages(locale)`; `defaultMessages` is the one for the runtime's locale.

## Every key

Functions are called with numbers that count from one, and receive a column by its accessible name — its `header`, or its label.

| Key                        | Type                                               | Default                                                                                                                                                             |
| -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `pagerLabel`               | `string`                                           | "Pagination" — the pager's accessible name.                                                                                                                         |
| `firstPage`                | `string`                                           | "First" — the pager button to the first page. The four arrow buttons show icons, so these are their accessible names and tooltips.                                  |
| `previousPage`             | `string`                                           | "Previous" — the pager button to the previous page.                                                                                                                 |
| `nextPage`                 | `string`                                           | "Next" — the pager button to the next page.                                                                                                                         |
| `lastPage`                 | `string`                                           | "Last" — the pager button to the last page.                                                                                                                         |
| `pageSizeLabel`            | `string`                                           | "Rows per page"                                                                                                                                                     |
| `pageButtonLabel`          | `(page) => string`                                 | "Page 3" — a numbered pager button's accessible name.                                                                                                               |

| `exportSelectionCsv`       | `string`                                           | "Export selection to CSV" — `exportSelection.csv`.                                                                                                                  |
| `exportSelectionJson`      | `string`                                           | "Export selection to JSON" — `exportSelection.json`.                                                                                                                |

| `copied`                   | `(count, unit) => string`                          | "3 rows copied", "1 cell copied" — announced once a [copy](/docs/react/clipboard) is on the clipboard. `unit` is `"cells"`, `"rows"` or `"columns"`.                |
| `copyFailed`               | `string`                                           | "Copy failed" — announced when the browser refuses the clipboard, so nothing was copied.                                                                            |
| `print`                    | `string`                                           | "Print" — `print`, the toolbar's Print button and the [printing](/docs/react/printing) menu item.                                                                   |

## What messages don't cover

- **A `pager.template` or `infiniteScroll.loadingTemplate`** replaces the built-in UI outright, so its text is whatever you render.
- **Symbols** — the "×" on a group-by chip's remove button, the "…" between numbered pages, the "—" in an empty aggregate cell — read the same in any language and are not keys.
- **Development warnings** logged to the console stay in English: they are for whoever is building the page, not its users.

## See also

- [Accessibility](/docs/react/accessibility) for the announcements these messages carry.
- [Context menu](/docs/react/context-menu) and [toolbar](/docs/react/toolbar) for the labels shown in them.
- [Core overview](/docs/core/overview) for messages in the framework-free layer.

docs.title: From Syncfusion or AG Grid
docs.description: Syncfusion Grid and AG Grid concepts and props mapped to DataGrid, how the models differ, and the features GridKit does not have yet.
docs.body:
`DataGrid` covers most of what a Syncfusion `GridComponent` or an `AgGridReact` grid is used for: sorting, filtering, row grouping, aggregates, pagination, virtualization, selection, menus, a toolbar, export and print. Most features are a prop with a similar name. This page maps the common concepts, notes where the model differs, and lists what GridKit does not do yet, so you can check a screen before you move it.

## When to use it

Read it when moving a screen from either grid, or when comparing them. Check the [not yet](#not-yet) list first: a screen that depends on one of those features cannot move yet.

## How the model differs

- **State is props.** Each piece of state (sort, filter, row grouping, page, selection, column widths, order and visibility) is a prop pair: `defaultColumnSort` for the grid to keep it, or `columnSort` with `onColumnSortChange` for you to keep it. There is no `actionBegin`/`actionComplete` with a `requestType` to switch on, and nothing to set up through an API after the grid mounts. See [controlled and uncontrolled state](/docs/react/state).
- **Columns are data.** `columns` is an array of plain objects, as AG Grid's `columnDefs` is, rather than `ColumnsDirective` and `ColumnDirective` children.
- **The rows are an array.** `dataSource` takes rows, never a `DataManager`, an adaptor or a row model. The grid sorts, filters and pages the rows it holds; to do that on a server, hold the state and fetch. See [server-side data](/docs/react/server-side-data).
- **Styling is a stylesheet.** `@gridkitjs/theme-tailwind` styles the grid's semantic class names and needs Tailwind CSS v4. There are no theme modules to import per component. See [theming](/docs/theme-tailwind).
- **One edition.** Every package is MIT-licensed. Row grouping, an Excel-style filter, Excel export, the context menu and clipboard copy, which AG Grid keeps in its Enterprise edition, are part of it.
- **The handle is a ref.** `ref` gives a `DataGridApi`, the counterpart of AG Grid's `gridRef.current.api` and of the methods on a Syncfusion grid instance. See [imperative handle](/docs/react/imperative-handle).

## Grid props

| GridKit                                   | Syncfusion                                  | AG Grid                                       |
| ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `DataGrid`                                | `GridComponent`                             | `AgGridReact`                                 |
| `dataSource`                              | `dataSource`                                | `rowData`                                     |
| `columns`                                 | `ColumnsDirective`                          | `columnDefs`                                  |
| `getRowId`                                | `isPrimaryKey` on a column                  | `getRowId`                                    |
| `height`                                  | `height`                                    | The container's height, or `domLayout`        |
| `sortableColumns`                         | `allowSorting`                              | `sortable` on a column                        |
| `defaultColumnSort`                       | `sortSettings`                              | `sort` or `initialSort` on a column           |
| `columnSort` and `onColumnSortChange`     | `actionComplete` with `requestType` sorting | `onSortChanged`                               |
| `filterableColumns`                       | `allowFiltering` and `filterSettings`       | `filter` on a column                          |
| `{...excelFilter}`                        | `filterSettings` with `type: "Excel"`       | The Set Filter (Enterprise)                   |
| The toolbar's `"search"` box              | The toolbar's `"Search"` item               | `quickFilterText`                             |
| `groupableColumns`, `defaultGroupBy`      | `allowGrouping`, `groupSettings`            | `rowGroup`, `enableRowGroup` (Enterprise)     |
| The group-by bar, `groupByBarVisibility`  | `groupSettings.showDropArea`                | `rowGroupPanelShow` (Enterprise)              |
| `aggregates`                              | `AggregatesDirective`                       | `aggFunc` on a column (Enterprise)            |
| `paginated`, `defaultPagination`, `pager` | `allowPaging`, `pageSettings`               | `pagination`, `paginationPageSize`            |
| `infiniteScroll`                          | `enableInfiniteScrolling`                   | The infinite row model                        |
| `virtualized`                             | `enableVirtualization`                      | On by default                                 |
| `resizableColumns`                        | `allowResizing`                             | `resizable` on a column                       |
| `reorderableColumns`                      | `allowReordering`                           | On by default; `suppressMovable` turns it off |
| `selectable={{ rows: "multiple" }}`       | `selectionSettings`                         | `rowSelection`                                |
| `selectable={{ cells: "single" }}`        | `selectionSettings` with `mode: "Cell"`     | Cell selection (Enterprise)                   |
| `contextMenu`                             | `contextMenuItems`                          | `getContextMenuItems` (Enterprise)            |
| `toolbar`                                 | `toolbar`                                   | None built in                                 |
| `getRowProps`                             | The `rowDataBound` event                    | `getRowClass`, `rowClassRules`                |
| `onRowClick`, `onRowDoubleClick`          | `recordClick`, `recordDoubleClick`          | `onRowClicked`, `onRowDoubleClicked`          |
| `messages`, `locale`                      | `locale` with `L10n.load`                   | `localeText`                                  |

## Column definition fields

| GridKit                         | Syncfusion `ColumnDirective`    | AG Grid column definition       |
| ------------------------------- | ------------------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| `field`                         | `field`                         | `field`                         |
| `header`                        | `headerText`                    | `headerName`                    |
| `type`                          | `type`                          | `cellDataType`                  |
| `format`, `valueFormatter`      | `format`                        | `valueFormatter`                |
| `cellTemplate`                  | `template`                      | `cellRenderer`                  |
| `headerTemplate`                | `headerTemplate`                | `headerComponent`               |
| `alignment`                     | `textAlign`                     | `cellStyle` or `cellClass`      |
| `width`, `minWidth`, `maxWidth` | `width`, `minWidth`, `maxWidth` | `width`, `minWidth`, `maxWidth` |
| `hidden`                        | `visible: false`                | `hide`                          |
| `cellClassName`                 | `customAttributes`              | `cellClass`                     |

`field` reaches one level into a nested object as `"customer.name"`, as both grids do. `format` takes `Intl.NumberFormat` or `Intl.DateTimeFormat` options, `{ currency: "EUR" }`, rather than a format string such as Syncfusion's `"C2"`. See [column definitions](/docs/react/column-definition) for every field.

## Methods

| GridKit (`DataGridApi`)                    | Syncfusion                              | AG Grid (`api`)                        |
| ------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `autoFitColumns()`                         | `autoFitColumns()`                      | `autoSizeColumns()`                    |
| `openColumnChooser()`                      | `openColumnChooser()`                   | The Columns tool panel (Enterprise)    |
| `runCommand("export.csv")`                 | `csvExport()`                           | `exportDataAsCsv()`                    |
| `runCommand("export.xlsx")`, with a writer | `excelExport()`                         | `exportDataAsExcel()` (Enterprise)     |
| `print()`                                  | `print()`                               | `domLayout: "print"`, then the browser |
| `getSelectedRows()`                        | `getSelectedRecords()`                  | `getSelectedRows()`                    |
| `clearSelection()`                         | `clearSelection()`                      | `deselectAll()`                        |
| `getState()`, `restoreState()`             | `getPersistData()`, `enablePersistence` | `getState()`, `initialState`           |

Excel export needs `@gridkitjs/export-xlsx` registered through `exportWriters`; see [Excel export](/docs/export-xlsx).

## A grid side by side

A Syncfusion grid like this one:

```tsx
<GridComponent
  dataSource={orders}
  allowSorting
  allowPaging
  pageSettings={{ pageSize: 20 }}
>
  <ColumnsDirective>
    <ColumnDirective field="id" headerText="Order" isPrimaryKey width={90} />
    <ColumnDirective field="customer" headerText="Customer" />
    <ColumnDirective field="total" headerText="Total" format="C2" />
  </ColumnsDirective>
  <Inject services={[Sort, Page]} />
</GridComponent>
```

or an AG Grid like this one:

```tsx
<AgGridReact
  rowData={orders}
  columnDefs={[
    { field: "id", headerName: "Order", width: 90 },
    { field: "customer", headerName: "Customer" },
    { field: "total", headerName: "Total", valueFormatter: formatMoney },
  ]}
  getRowId={(params) => String(params.data.id)}
  pagination
  paginationPageSize={20}
/>
```

becomes:

```tsx title="App.tsx"
import { DataGrid, type ColumnDefinition } from "@gridkitjs/react";

interface Order {
  id: number;
  customer: string;
  total: number;
}

const orders: Order[] = Array.from({ length: 60 }, (_, index) => ({
  id: index + 1,
  customer: `Customer ${String((index % 12) + 1)}`,
  total: Math.round(((index * 37) % 500) * 100 + 99) / 100,
}));

const columns: readonly ColumnDefinition<Order>[] = [
  { field: "id", header: "Order", type: "number", width: 90 },
  { field: "customer", header: "Customer" },
  {
    field: "total",
    header: "Total",
    type: "currency",
    format: { currency: "USD" },
  },
];

const getOrderId = (order: Order) => String(order.id);

export default function App() {
  return (
    <DataGrid
      columns={columns}
      dataSource={orders}
      getRowId={getOrderId}
      label="Orders"
      sortableColumns
      paginated
      defaultPagination={{ pageIndex: 0, pageSize: 20 }}
    />
  );
}
```

## Not yet

These are not in GridKit today. Each is absent from the source, not hidden behind an option:

- **Editing.** No inline cell or row editing, edit forms or edit events. A `cellTemplate` can render inputs of your own that write back to your rows.
- **Master-detail.** No detail row or panel that expands under a row.
- **Frozen columns.** No pinned or frozen columns; the header and footer stay put, but every column scrolls sideways. (The xlsx writer freezes the header row in the exported sheet, which is not the same thing.)
- **Column groups and spanning.** No grouped headers over several columns, and no row or column spanning of cells.
- **Row drag.** No dragging rows to reorder them or to move them between grids. Columns and group-by chips can be dragged; rows cannot.
- **A server-side data adapter.** No `DataManager`, adaptor or server-side row model. Server-side sorting, filtering and paging work through controlled state instead; see [server-side data](/docs/react/server-side-data).
- **Tree data.** No hierarchical rows from a parent id or a path; [row grouping](/docs/react/row-grouping) groups flat rows by a column's values.
- **Cell ranges.** Cell selection is one cell at a time.
- **PDF export.** The "Export to PDF" command appears only once you register a `pdf` writer of your own; none ships. [Printing](/docs/react/printing) to the browser's "Save as PDF" is the built-in route.

## See also

- [Choosing packages](/docs/react/choosing-packages) for what to install.
- [Your first grid](/docs/react) for the setup, stylesheet included.
- [DataGrid](/docs/react/data-grid) for every prop.
- [Server-side data](/docs/react/server-side-data) for replacing a data adaptor.
- [FAQ](/docs/react/faq) for the questions that come up first.

docs.title: Overview
docs.description: Install @gridkitjs/react and its Tailwind theme, import the stylesheet and render a first data grid.
docs.body:
`@gridkitjs/react` is a data grid for React: sorting, filtering, row grouping, pagination, selection, virtualization and more, each turned on with a prop. It renders semantic class names and carries no styles of its own; `@gridkitjs/theme-tailwind` is the stylesheet that draws them.

## Prerequisites

- **React 19.** `react` and `react-dom` 19 are peer dependencies.
- **Tailwind CSS v4.** The theme is a Tailwind v4 stylesheet (`tailwindcss` 4.3.3 or later), compiled by your app's Tailwind build. Without Tailwind, see [without Tailwind](/docs/theme-tailwind#without-tailwind).
- **An ESM bundler**, such as Vite or Next.js. The packages ship as ES modules only.

## Install

<PackageInstall pkg="@gridkitjs/react @gridkitjs/theme-tailwind" />

`@gridkitjs/react` brings `@gridkitjs/core` and `@gridkitjs/dom` with it. See [choosing packages](/docs/react/choosing-packages) for what each package does and when to install one yourself.

If your app has no Tailwind yet, add it. In a Vite app that is the Tailwind plugin:

<PackageInstall pkg="tailwindcss @tailwindcss/vite" dev="true" />

```ts title="vite.config.ts"
import tailwindcss from "@tailwindcss/vite";
import react from "@vitejs/plugin-react";
import { defineConfig } from "vite";

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [react(), tailwindcss()],
});
```

Other frameworks have their own setup; follow [Tailwind's installation guide](https://tailwindcss.com/docs/installation) for yours.

## Import the stylesheet

Import the theme in the CSS file your app already loads, after Tailwind itself. In a new Vite app that is `src/index.css`; replace the template's demo styles in it, which centre all text on the page:

```css title="src/index.css"
@import "tailwindcss";
@import "@gridkitjs/theme-tailwind/styles.css";
```

<Callout type="warning" title="An unstyled grid means a missing import">
  Without this import the grid still renders, but as bare tables: no padding,
  borders, hover or selection colours, and every header's sort icons drawn as
  large as the header itself. If that is what you see, check that the `@import`
  is in a CSS file your app loads, and that it comes after Tailwind's own.
</Callout>

## Your first grid

Give `DataGrid` the rows as `dataSource` and describe the columns. This is a complete component; paste it over a new app's `App.tsx`:

```tsx title="src/App.tsx"
import { DataGrid, type ColumnDefinition } from "@gridkitjs/react";

interface Order {
  id: number;
  customer: string;
  region: string;
  total: number;
  shipped: boolean;
}

const orders: Order[] = [
  {
    id: 1,
    customer: "Alder & Co",
    region: "North",
    total: 1250.5,
    shipped: true,
  },
  {
    id: 2,
    customer: "Birchwood Ltd",
    region: "South",
    total: 87.25,
    shipped: false,
  },
  {
    id: 3,
    customer: "Cedar Supplies",
    region: "East",
    total: 420,
    shipped: true,
  },
  {
    id: 4,
    customer: "Dunmore Trading",
    region: "West",
    total: 3105.9,
    shipped: false,
  },
  {
    id: 5,
    customer: "Elmfield Retail",
    region: "North",
    total: 640.1,
    shipped: true,
  },
];

const columns: readonly ColumnDefinition<Order>[] = [
  { field: "id", header: "Order", type: "number", width: 90 },
  { field: "customer", header: "Customer" },
  { field: "region", header: "Region" },
  {
    field: "total",
    header: "Total",
    type: "currency",
    format: { currency: "USD" },
  },
  { field: "shipped", header: "Shipped", type: "boolean" },
];

export default function App() {
  return (
    <DataGrid
      columns={columns}
      dataSource={orders}
      getRowId={(row) => String(row.id)}
      label="Orders"
      borders="horizontal"
      sortableColumns
    />
  );
}
```

- `columns` lists the column definitions: `field` is the key a cell reads, `header` its title, and `type` decides alignment, formatting and how the column sorts. See [column definitions](/docs/react/column-definition) for every field.
- `getRowId` gives each row a stable id, so selection and other state follow the row when it is sorted, filtered or paged.
- `label` names the grid for screen readers.
- `borders` draws lines between rows; `"all"` adds them between columns too.
- `sortableColumns` turns on one feature: click a header's sort toggle to sort by it. Most features are a prop like this one.

`columns` is optional: without it, the grid infers one column per field found in the rows, and a nested object's fields as `Parent.Child`. The same inference is available as `defineColumnsFromRows` from `@gridkitjs/core`, to start from and then adjust:

<DataGridBasicExample />

## Terms

A few words recur throughout these docs:

- **Column definition**: one entry of `columns`, a `ColumnDefinition<Row>`: which field a column shows and how.
- **Renderer**: the package that draws the grid for a UI framework. `@gridkitjs/react` is the renderer for React; the logic it draws comes from `@gridkitjs/core`.
- **View pipeline**: the steps that turn `dataSource` into the rows on screen, in order: filter, sort, group, aggregate, paginate. See [the view pipeline](/docs/core/view).
- **Controlled and uncontrolled**: a piece of state the grid keeps itself (`defaultColumnSort`) or that you hold and pass back in (`columnSort`). See [controlled state](/docs/react/state).
- **Row id**: the string `getRowId` returns for a row, which selection and other per-row state are keyed by. Without `getRowId`, a row's id is its position.
- **Roving tab stop**: the grid is one stop in the page's <Kbd>Tab</Kbd> order; arrow keys then move between cells inside it. See [accessibility](/docs/react/accessibility).
- **Sentinel row**: an invisible last row that infinite scroll watches, loading more when it scrolls into view. See [infinite scroll](/docs/react/infinite-scroll).
- **Autofit**: sizing a column to its content, by double-clicking its edge or from the context menu.

docs.title: Printing
docs.description: Print every row the grid holds from the toolbar, the context menu or the ref, with a title, a repeating header row and page numbers, or save it as a PDF.
docs.body:
The grid prints what the user sees: every row the filter, search and sort leave, across every page and inside collapsed groups, not only the rows a virtualized or paginated grid has drawn. The toolbar's Print button, a Print item in the context menu, `ref.current.runCommand("print")` and `ref.current.print()` all open the browser's print dialog on the same document.

The grid builds that document from its state — the [export model](/docs/core/export), as an export does — and prints it through a hidden frame: a page of its own holding the title, the table and a footer, with the column headers repeated at the top of every page and the rows never split across two. Nothing of the page around the grid prints, and no popup opens.

## From the toolbar

`"print"` in the toolbar's items is a Print button:

```ts
<DataGrid
  columns={columns}
  dataSource={orders}
  label="Orders"
  toolbar={{ items: ["search", "spacer", "export", "print"] }}
/>
```

It is not among the default toolbar's items, so `toolbar` alone does not show it; list it where you want it. It is disabled only while no column is shown — a grid with no rows still prints its header.

## From the context menu

No default menu prints, so list `print` in the areas you want it — `cell` for a row's menu, `body` for the grid's empty space:

```ts
import { defaultContextMenu } from "@gridkitjs/core";

<DataGrid
  columns={columns}
  dataSource={orders}
  contextMenu={{ cell: [...defaultContextMenu.cell, "separator", "print"] }}
/>;
```

A print from a row's menu still prints the whole grid. The command reports to `onCommand` like any other; see [built-in commands](/docs/core/commands#built-in-commands).

## From the ref

`print(options?)` prints and resolves once the print dialog has closed. `options` go over the grid's `print` option field by field, so a call need only say what differs:

```ts
const gridRef = useRef<DataGridApi<Order>>(null);

await gridRef.current?.print({
  subtitle: "Selected orders",
  scope: "selection",
});
```

| Method                | Returns         | Description                                                                                   |
| --------------------- | --------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `print(options?)`     | `Promise<void>` | Prints the grid's view under `print` with `options` over it; resolves once the dialog closes. |
| `runCommand("print")` | `boolean`       | Prints under the `print` option, as the toolbar does. Says whether it ran.                    |

One print at a time: a print asked for while the dialog is open does nothing, and its promise resolves at once.

## Options

`print` sets how the grid prints unless a call says otherwise:

```ts
<DataGrid
  columns={columns}
  dataSource={orders}
  label="Orders"
  toolbar={{ items: ["print"] }}
  print={{
    subtitle: "Q1, all regions",
    footer: "Internal — do not distribute",
    timestamp: true,
    fitToWidth: true,
  }}
/>
```

| Option              | Type                                      | Default      | Description                                                                                                           |
| ------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `title`             | `string`                                  | `label`      | A heading above the table, and the document's title, which names a PDF saved from the dialog. `""` prints none.       |
| `subtitle`          | `string`                                  |              | A line under the title.                                                                                               |
| `footer`            | `string`                                  |              | A line after the table, once, at the end.                                                                             |
| `timestamp`         | `boolean \| Date`                         | `false`      | When the print was made, under the title: `true` for now, or a `Date`, in the grid's `locale`.                        |
| `locale`            | `string \| string[]`                      | the grid's   | The language the timestamp is written in.                                                                             |
| `orientation`       | `"portrait" \| "landscape"`               | by the width | Landscape for a table of more than six columns, else portrait.                                                        |
| `paperSize`         | `string`                                  | `"A4"`       | A page size CSS names: `"A4"`, `"Letter"`, `"A3"`, `"Legal"`. The print dialog can still change it.                   |
| `pageNumbers`       | `boolean`                                 | `true`       | "3 / 12" at the foot of each page, where the browser can — see [browser support](#browser-support).                   |
| `fitToWidth`        | `boolean`                                 | `false`      | Squeezes a wide table onto the page — a smaller font and fixed columns that wrap their text — rather than run off it. |
| `styles`            | `string`                                  |              | CSS added after the print stylesheet, to restyle the printed document — see [styling the print](#styling-the-print).  |
| `scope`             | `"all" \| "page" \| "selection"`          | `"all"`      | Every row the filter leaves, the current page's, or the selected rows.                                                |
| `columns`           | `"visible" \| "all" \| readonly string[]` | `"visible"`  | The shown columns, every column, or these ids in this order. A column with `exportable: false` never prints.          |
| `includeGroups`     | `boolean`                                 | `true`       | Group header rows, when the grid is grouped.                                                                          |
| `includeAggregates` | `boolean`                                 | `true`       | Aggregate values: group summaries and the grand total, printed once at the end.                                       |
| `includeHeader`     | `boolean`                                 | `true`       | The header row, repeated on every page.                                                                               |

Cells print as the grid formats them, and a column decides its own part with `exportable` and `exportValue` — see [column definitions](/docs/react/column-definition). Without a `title` or a `label` the print has no heading, and the browser names a saved PDF after the page.

## Styling the print

The printed document is a page of its own, so it sees none of your CSS, the theme's included. It carries a small stylesheet of its own — the page size and margins, the repeating header, neutral borders, group rows indented by level — and `styles` goes after it:

```ts
<DataGrid
  columns={columns}
  dataSource={orders}
  print={{
    styles: `
      .print-title { color: #1d4ed8; }
      .gridkit-export-table th { background: #dbeafe; }
    `,
  }}
/>
```

The heading is `header.gridkit-print-header` holding `h1.print-title`, `p.print-subtitle` and `p.print-timestamp`; the footer `footer.gridkit-print-footer`; the table `table.gridkit-export-table`, with group rows `tr.export-group` and summary rows `tr.export-group-summary`, each with a `data-level`. See @gridkitjs/core's [print document](/docs/core/export#printing) and @gridkitjs/dom's [print stylesheet](/docs/dom/downloads-clipboard-print#print).

## Save as PDF

GridKit's PDF is the browser's own: print, and choose to save instead of paying for paper. Nothing is downloaded or bundled for it, and because the browser draws the text with the fonts it already has, any script comes out right — Macedonian and Croatian, Greek, CJK — where a library that writes PDFs itself would need a font file embedded first.

1. Run Print from the toolbar, the context menu or `ref.current.print()`.
2. In the print dialog, choose "Save as PDF" as the destination: Chrome and Edge list it with the printers; Firefox lists "Save to PDF" (or "Microsoft Print to PDF" on Windows); Safari and macOS offer it in the PDF menu of the dialog.
3. Save. The file is named after the document's title — `title`, else the grid's `label`.

The wording of the destination varies by browser, operating system and version.

The PDF holds what the print holds: the title, subtitle and timestamp above the table, the footer line at the end, the column headers repeated at the top of every page, rows kept whole across page breaks, and page numbers, "3 / 12", where the browser can draw them — see [browser support](#browser-support). The page size and orientation come from the `print` option's `paperSize` and `orientation`, which the dialog can still change. These are the options worth setting for a PDF:

```ts
<DataGrid
  columns={columns}
  dataSource={orders}
  label="Orders"
  toolbar={{ items: ["print"] }}
  print={{
    title: "Orders, Q1",
    timestamp: true,
    paperSize: "A4",
    orientation: "landscape",
    fitToWidth: true,
    pageNumbers: true,
  }}
/>
```

The grid shows no "Export to PDF" item of its own, because it writes no PDF. An app that must produce the file in code — to upload it, or to save it without a dialog — registers a `pdf` writer, and the Export dropdown and `export.pdf` then pick it up: see [PDF in code](/docs/react/export#pdf).

<Callout type="note" title="Browser support">

In Chrome the header row repeats at the top of every page and each page is numbered, "1 / 4", at its foot. Firefox and Safari have not been checked yet.

Page numbers use CSS `@page` margin boxes. A browser without them prints no numbers and nothing else changes; the browser's own header and footer, when turned on in the dialog, number the pages instead.

</Callout>

## Printing the page

The browser's own print — <Kbd>Ctrl</Kbd>+<Kbd>P</Kbd>, or <Kbd>Cmd</Kbd>+<Kbd>P</Kbd> on a Mac — prints the page, the grid as it is drawn. The [theme](/docs/theme-tailwind) makes that read as a plain table: the toolbar, the pager, the group-by bar and the resize handles are hidden, a `height` stops bounding the rows, and no row is split across two pages. It prints only the rows the grid has drawn, though — not those on another page, or those a virtualized grid has not mounted — so use the grid's own Print for everything.

## Props

| Prop    | Type           | Default | Description                                                                 |
| ------- | -------------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `print` | `PrintOptions` |         | How the grid prints unless a call says otherwise — see [options](#options). |

The button's and the menu item's label is a message, `print` — see [localization](/docs/react/localization).

## See also

- [Export](/docs/react/export) for writing the grid to a file.
- [Toolbar](/docs/react/toolbar) and [context menu](/docs/react/context-menu) for where Print is offered.
- [core: Export](/docs/core/export) for the printing options.

docs.title: Row virtualization
docs.description: Rendering only the rows near the current scroll position with virtualized, for a dataset too large to mount in full.
docs.body:
`virtualized` renders only the rows near the current scroll position rather than every row `dataSource` holds at once. It's the safe default for a dataset with thousands of rows or more: without it, every row mounts as a real `<tr>` regardless of how many are actually visible.

## Enable virtualization

`virtualized` requires `height` to be set — the row area needs a real, bounded viewport to compute a visible-row window against. A body left at its default content-driven height has nothing to window relative to, so combining `virtualized` with no `height` fires a `console.error` in development and otherwise does nothing useful.

```tsx
<DataGrid columns={columns} dataSource={rows} height={400} virtualized />
```

<RowVirtualizationExample />

## Row height is measured, not assumed

Rows in this grid are not uniform: a column with `wrap: { cells: true }` allows multi-line content, and group header/summary rows (see [row grouping](/docs/react/row-grouping)) differ in height from data rows. `virtualized` measures each rendered row's real height rather than assuming a fixed one, so none of that is out of scope — a `.is-wrapped` column keeps wrapping exactly as it does without `virtualized`.

This does mean a row's height isn't known until it has actually rendered once. Two props tune how that unmeasured state behaves:

```tsx
<DataGrid
  columns={columns}
  dataSource={rows}
  height={400}
  virtualized
  estimatedRowHeight={48}
  overscan={8}
/>
```

- `estimatedRowHeight` (default `40`) is the assumed height for a row never yet measured. It only matters for the very first paint and for `scrollToRow`'s initial jump — real measurements replace it row by row as rows render, and the on-screen result self-corrects.
- `overscan` (default `4`) is how many rows render outside the visible range on each side. A larger value trades a few more mounted rows for fewer blank-frame flashes on fast scrolling.

## `scrollToRow` and keyboard navigation reach unmounted rows

Without virtualization, every row is already in the DOM, so `scrollToRow` and arrow-key navigation only ever need to move focus or scroll to an existing element. With it, a target row — `scrollToRow`'s argument, or wherever <Kbd>ArrowDown</Kbd>, <Kbd>End</Kbd> or <Kbd>Ctrl</Kbd>+<Kbd>End</Kbd> would land — may not be mounted at all.

Both handle this the same way, in two passes: jump to an estimated scroll offset (using measured heights where known, `estimatedRowHeight` for the rest), let the target row mount, then correct the scroll position once its real height is measured. This happens automatically; there is nothing extra to call.

```tsx
const gridRef = useRef<DataGridApi<Row>>(null);

// Works the same whether row-2000 is currently mounted or not.
gridRef.current?.scrollToRow("row-2000");
```

## Interaction with pagination and grouping

`virtualized` windows whatever the grid is about to render — the current page's rows when `paginated` is on, the full set otherwise — so the two compose freely. Virtualizing an already-small paginated page still works, it's just low-value: there's rarely enough rows on one page for windowing to matter.

`groupBy` is unaffected: a flattened row list mixing data, group-header, and group-summary rows is exactly what measuring each row's real height is for, and virtualization doesn't distinguish between the three.

## Props

| Prop                 | Type      | Default | Description                                                                         |
| -------------------- | --------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `virtualized`        | `boolean` | `false` | Renders only the rows near the current scroll position. Requires `height`.          |
| `overscan`           | `number`  | `4`     | Rows rendered outside the visible range on each side.                               |
| `estimatedRowHeight` | `number`  | `40`    | Assumed height for a row never yet measured — only matters before it first renders. |

## See also

- [Scrollable layout](/docs/react/data-grid#scrollable-layout) for `height`, the bounded viewport `virtualized` windows against.
- [Row grouping](/docs/react/row-grouping) and [pagination](/docs/react/pagination) for the two transforms `virtualized` composes with.
- [Imperative handle](/docs/react/imperative-handle) for `scrollToRow`.
- [Infinite scroll](/docs/react/infinite-scroll) for `infiniteScroll` — the recommended pairing for a dataset that grows without bound, not a requirement.
- [core: Focus and virtualization](/docs/core/navigation) for the framework-free logic.
- [Performance](/docs/react/performance) for when to virtualize and keeping a large grid fast.
