docs.title: Toolbar
docs.description: A toolbar above the grid: clear the filters or sort, search every column, add dropdowns and content of your own, in the same vocabulary as the context menu.
docs.body: `toolbar` puts a toolbar above the grid: buttons for the grid's own commands — clear the filters, clear the sort, expand or collapse every group, choose the columns shown — a search box over every column, an Export dropdown, a Print button, dropdown menus of actions, and content of your own. It is written in the same vocabulary as the [context menu](/docs/react/context-menu), so a command you register once shows in both. It is off by default, like every other GridKit feature. ## Turning it on ```ts ``` `toolbar` alone shows the defaults, `defaultToolbar` from @gridkitjs/core: the search box on the left, and "Clear filters" and "Choose columns" at the far end, with a spacer between them. "Clear filters" is disabled until something filters; "Choose columns" opens the [column chooser](/docs/react/column-chooser) below it. The toolbar is the first thing inside the grid, above the group-by bar. It sticks to the grid's start edge, so it stays in view while a grid wider than its container scrolls sideways under it. ## Choosing the items An object lists the items yourself, in order, and may name the toolbar for a screen reader — it is "Grid toolbar" otherwise: ```ts ``` | Item | Drawn as | | ------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | A command id, `"filter.clearAll"` | A button. A checkable command is a toggle button, pressed while it is checked. | | `{ type: "item", id, label, onSelect, … }` | A button of your own; a toggle when it has `checked`. | | `{ type: "submenu", id, label, items }` | A dropdown button, opening a menu of `items`. | | `"separator"` | A separator. | | `"search"` | The search box — see [search](#search). | | `"export"` | The Export dropdown — see [export](#export). | | `"print"` | The Print button — see [print](#print). | | `"spacer"` | The free space, pushing what follows it to the far end. | | `{ type: "custom", id }` | Content of your own, drawn by `renderToolbarItem` — see [below](#content-of-your-own). | A button shows only where its command has something to act on, and is disabled while it cannot run, exactly as the command says: "Clear all sorting" is disabled until something is sorted, and "Expand all groups" is not there at all until the grid is grouped. Separators collapse when the items around them are hidden. The toolbar follows the grid's state as it changes, from the toolbar or anywhere else. The built-in commands meant for a toolbar: | Item | Command | Shown when | | ------------------- | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | | Clear all sorting | `sort.clearAll` | Always; disabled until something is sorted. | | Clear filters | `filter.clearAll` | Always; disabled until something filters. | | Ungroup all | `group.clearAll` | The grid is grouped. | | Expand all groups | `group.expandAll` | The grid is grouped. | | Collapse all groups | `group.collapseAll` | The grid is grouped. | | Autofit all columns | `column.autoFitAll` | Any column is resizable. | | Choose columns | `column.choose` | Always; opens the column chooser below it. | The rest act on a column, a row or a group, which a toolbar has none of, so they never show in one. See [built-in commands](/docs/core/commands#built-in-commands) for every command, and @gridkitjs/core's [toolbar model](/docs/core/toolbar) for the vocabulary in depth. ### Items of your own An inline item is a button of your own; with `checked` it is a toggle button, drawn with `aria-pressed`. A submenu is a dropdown, whose items are a menu's — command ids, inline items, separators and submenus of their own. `onSelect` receives the [command context](/docs/core/commands#the-context): the grid's state, its rows and its actions. ```ts const [compact, setCompact] = useState(false); setCompact((current) => !current), }, { type: "submenu", id: "selected", label: "Selected", items: [ { type: "item", id: "selected.archive", label: "Archive", disabled: ({ state }) => state.rowSelection.length === 0, onSelect: ({ selectedRows }) => archiveOrders(selectedRows()), }, { type: "item", id: "selected.delete", label: "Delete", disabled: ({ state }) => state.rowSelection.length === 0, onSelect: ({ selectedRows }) => deleteOrders(selectedRows()), }, ], }, ], }} />; ``` An action offered in the toolbar and a menu both is better registered once as a [command of your own](/docs/react/context-menu#commands-of-your-own), through `commands`, and listed by its id in each. ### Content of your own A custom entry, `{ type: "custom", id }`, holds whatever `renderToolbarItem` draws for its id — a status, a select, a button of your own. It sits in the toolbar's keyboard order: the arrow keys reach the first control in it. ```ts id === "rowCount" ? {orders.length} orders : null } /> ``` ## Export `"export"` is a dropdown, "Export", of the formats the grid can export now: "Export to CSV" and "Export to JSON", Excel and PDF once a writer for them is registered, and — while rows are selected — exports of the selected rows alone. Choosing one downloads the file. It is not among the defaults, so list it where you want it: ```ts ``` For a different list, write the export commands' ids yourself — `"export.csv"` alone is a button. See [export](/docs/react/export) for what an export holds, its options and formats of your own. ## Print `"print"` is a button, "Print", that prints every row the grid holds through the browser's print dialog — under a title, with the header row on every page. Like the Export dropdown, it is not among the defaults: ```ts ``` See [printing](/docs/react/printing) for what is printed and its options. ## Search `"search"` is a search box over every column. What is typed applies once typing rests for a moment, or at once on Enter; Escape empties the box. Once the rows are filtered, a screen reader hears how many were found: "3 rows found". The box writes the filter's global text entry — `{ query: "%text%" }`, naming no column, a case-insensitive "contains" — through the grid's filter, so it fires `onFilterChange` and sends the grid back to its first page like any filter change, and leaves every column's own entry alone. It reads its text back from the filter, so anything else that changes the search changes the box: "Clear filters" empties it, and a restored layout or a controlled `filter` fills it. It matches what the global entry matches: every data column, hidden ones included, by its raw value — a date cell is not found by its formatted text. See [column filtering](/docs/react/column-filtering) and @gridkitjs/core's [search helpers](/docs/core/filtering#a-search-box). ## When it is narrow The toolbar keeps its items on one row. When they do not all fit, the ones from the first that does not fit onwards move into a "More" menu button at the end — a button becomes a menu item, a toggle a checkable one, and a dropdown a submenu — and widening the toolbar brings them back out. They run from "More" exactly as they would have from their buttons, and report the same target to `onCommand`. The search box and custom entries never move: they stay however narrow the toolbar gets. The search box narrows with the toolbar, to half its width at most, and should they still not fit, "More" stays at the toolbar's end over what is cut off there, so it can always be reached. ## Commands and `onCommand` A toolbar button runs its command against the target `{ area: "toolbar", itemId }` — the button, or the dropdown an item was chosen from. `onCommand` is called after it runs with `source: "toolbar"`: ```ts { // "filter.clearAll", { area: "toolbar", itemId: "filter.clearAll" }, "toolbar" analytics.track(commandId, source); }} /> ``` A disabled button runs nothing and reports nothing. The change a command made reports through its own callback too, as it always does: `onFilterChange` for "Clear filters". ## Keyboard & pointer interactions The toolbar follows the [WAI-ARIA toolbar pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/toolbar/): it is one tab stop, and the arrow keys move within it. | Key or action | Does | | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Tab / Shift+Tab | Into the toolbar, on the control used last, or out of it. | | ArrowRight / ArrowLeft | The next or previous control, wrapping round the ends. Separators and spacers are passed over. | | Home / End | The first or last control. | | Enter / Space, or a click | Runs a button. A disabled one does nothing. | | Enter, Space or ArrowDown on a dropdown or "More" | Opens its menu, on its first item. A second click closes it. | | ArrowUp on a dropdown or "More" | Opens its menu, on its last item. | | In the search box: ArrowLeft / ArrowRight | Move the caret; at the start or end of the text, move on to the previous or next control. | | In the search box: Home / End | Move the caret. | | In the search box: Enter / Escape | Searches at once / empties the box. | A dropdown's menu works as the context menu's does — see its [keys](/docs/react/context-menu#keyboard--pointer-interactions) — and closing it puts focus back on the dropdown. A disabled button still takes focus, so a screen reader finds it. ## Props | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | ------------------- | ------------------------------------ | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `toolbar` | `boolean \| GridToolbarOptions` | | The toolbar. `true` shows the defaults; `{ items, label }` lists the items and names the toolbar. | | `renderToolbarItem` | `(id: string) => ReactNode` | | Draws a custom entry, `{ type: "custom", id }`, by its id. | | `commands` | `readonly GridCommand[]` | | Your own commands, for the toolbar and menus to list by id. One with a built-in's id replaces it. | | `onCommand` | `(event: GridCommandEvent) => void` | | Called after a command or an inline item runs, with `{ commandId, target, source }`. | The toolbar's name, the search box's name and placeholder, the "N rows found" announcement, the "More" button and every built-in button's label are messages — `toolbarLabel`, `searchLabel`, `searchPlaceholder`, `searchResults`, `moreToolbarItems` — see [localization](/docs/react/localization). The theme's classes for it are listed under [toolbar](/docs/theme-tailwind#toolbar). ## See also - [Context menu](/docs/react/context-menu) for the same commands in a menu. - [Export](/docs/react/export) and [printing](/docs/react/printing) for the commands the toolbar offers. - [core: Toolbar](/docs/core/toolbar) for the framework-free model.

docs.title: Overview
docs.description: Palette tokens, dark mode, and the grid's styles.
docs.body:
@gridkitjs/react renders semantic class names (`gridkit-data-grid`, `header-cell`, `grid-row`) and this stylesheet targets them directly. Nothing needs to scan component source, and every colour is a CSS custom property, so overriding one is plain CSS.

## Requirements

The stylesheet is written for Tailwind CSS v4 and needs `tailwindcss` 4.3.3 or later, a peer dependency. It is not plain CSS: it uses Tailwind's `@variant dark` to follow your app's dark mode and `@theme inline` to register the palette as colour utilities (`text-accent`, `bg-surface`), so your app's Tailwind build has to compile it. Tailwind v3 cannot.

## Install

<PackageInstall pkg="@gridkitjs/theme-tailwind" />

Import it in your app's CSS entry, after Tailwind itself:

```css title="src/index.css"
@import "tailwindcss";
@import "@gridkitjs/theme-tailwind/styles.css";
```

The [quick start](/docs/react) walks through the whole setup, Tailwind included, in a new Vite app.

## Without Tailwind

There is no plain-CSS build of the theme yet. Without Tailwind, `@gridkitjs/react` still works: it renders the same semantic class names with no styles of its own, so a stylesheet of yours can target them. The tables below list every class and state, and the [theme tokens](#theme-tokens) are a starting palette to copy. Expect to write the layout rules too, such as `table-layout: fixed` on `.gridkit-data-grid`, which column widths depend on.

## Layout

The grid is a set of siblings rather than one table, so the header and footer never scroll with the rows:

| Class                         | Element   | Description                                                                                                                                                       |
| ----------------------------- | --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.gridkit-data-grid-viewport` | `<div>`   | The grid's root: the toolbar, the group-by bar, the tables and the pager, in that order. Scrolls sideways when the columns are wider than it.                     |
| `.gridkit-data-grid-tables`   | `<div>`   | Holds the three tables and carries `role="grid"` (or `"treegrid"` while grouped), since the pattern needs one element around every row.                           |
| `.gridkit-data-grid-header`   | `<table>` | The header's table. Also a `.gridkit-data-grid`.                                                                                                                  |
| `.gridkit-data-grid-body`     | `<div>`   | The scroll container around the rows' table — the one `height` bounds, through `--gridkit-body-height`.                                                           |
| `.gridkit-data-grid-footer`   | `<table>` | The grand-total footer's table, while `aggregates` is non-empty. Also a `.gridkit-data-grid`.                                                                     |
| `.gridkit-sr-only`            | `<div>`   | The live region announcements are read from, clipped to nothing but left in the accessibility tree. Usable on anything of your own that should be read, not seen. |

## Semantic classes

| Class                                                        | Element                | Description                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.gridkit-data-grid`                                         | `<table>`              | Each of the grid's tables — header, rows and footer — not the grid's root, which is `div.gridkit-data-grid-viewport`. Carries the border, hover and selectable modifiers below. |
| `.grid-header`                                               | `<tr>`                 | The header row.                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `.header-cell`                                               | `<th>`                 | A header cell. States: is-resizing, is-dragging, is-drop-before, is-drop-after, is-wrapped, and is-reorderable on one that can be dragged.                                      |
| `.grid-row`                                                  | `<tr>`                 | A body row.                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `.grid-cell`                                                 | `<td>`                 | A body cell. States: is-resizing, is-wrapped.                                                                                                                                   |
| `.selectable-rows / .selectable-columns / .selectable-cells` | `<table>`              | Present on the grid while the matching selectable member is enabled — what turns on the pointer cursor and text-selection guard.                                                |
| `.is-selected`                                               | `<tr> \| <th> \| <td>` | A selected row, header cell, or cell. A selected cell wins over its row and column.                                                                                             |

### Header

| Class                                       | Element  | Description                                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------------------------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `.header-resize-handle`                     | `<span>` | The strip on a resizable header's trailing edge that a drag resizes from and a double-click autofits.                                                              |
| `.header-sort-toggle`                       | `<span>` | A sortable header's sort icon. Hidden until the header is hovered or focused, or the column sorts. `.is-sorted-asc` / `.is-sorted-desc` while it does, in accent.  |
| `.header-sort-priority`                     | `<span>` | The column's place in a sort of more than one column, beside its sort icon.                                                                                        |
| `.header-group-toggle`                      | `<span>` | A groupable header's group icon, before its label. Faint until hovered or focused; `.is-grouped` while the column is grouped, in accent.                           |
| `.header-filter-toggle`                     | `<span>` | A filterable header's filter button, at its end, the sort icon beside it. Hidden until hovered or focused; `.is-filtered` while the column is filtered, in accent. |
| `.gridkit-data-grid.header-cell.drag-ghost` | `<div>`  | The header following the pointer while a column is dragged, rendered into `document.body`.                                                                         |

### Group rows

| Class                      | Element  | Description                                                                                                   |
| -------------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.grid-group-row`          | `<tr>`   | A group header row, also `.is-group-level-N` for its depth.                                                   |
| `.grid-group-cell`         | `<td>`   | Its one cell, spanning every column.                                                                          |
| `.grid-group-cell-content` | `<div>`  | The cell's content — toggle, label, count and aggregates in a row — which carries the padding and the indent. |
| `.group-toggle`            | `<span>` | The triangle; `.is-expanded` turns it open, `.is-collapsed` marks it closed.                                  |
| `.group-label`             | `<span>` | The grouped column's name and the group's value.                                                              |
| `.group-count`             | `<span>` | The group's row count.                                                                                        |
| `.group-aggregates`        | `<span>` | A group's own subtotals, inline after the count, under `groupAggregateDisplay: "inline"`.                     |
| `.group-aggregate`         | `<span>` | One of those subtotals.                                                                                       |

### Footer, summary and loading rows

| Class                                      | Element         | Description                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------------------------------ | --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.grid-footer`                             | `<tr>`          | The grand-total row, in the footer's table.                                                                                              |
| `.grid-footer-cell`                        | `<td>`          | One column's grand total.                                                                                                                |
| `.grid-group-summary-row`                  | `<tr>`          | A group's own summary row, under `groupAggregateDisplay: "row"`, also `.is-group-level-N`.                                               |
| `.grid-group-summary-cell`                 | `<td>`          | One column's subtotal in it.                                                                                                             |
| `.grid-group-summary-indent`               | `<span>`        | The empty spacer in its first cell that indents the row to its group's depth.                                                            |
| `.grid-loading-row` / `.grid-loading-cell` | `<tr>` / `<td>` | The loading row and its one cell, while `infiniteScroll.isLoadingMore` is on — holding "Loading more…", or what `loadingTemplate` draws. |

### Borders and hover

The `borders` and `hoverable` props put modifiers on each `.gridkit-data-grid` table:

| Class                                                        | Description                                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.borders-horizontal` / `.borders-vertical` / `.borders-all` | Draw lines between rows, between columns, or both. `borders="none"`, or none given, draws none. |
| `.no-hover-rows` / `.no-hover-columns` / `.no-hover-cells`   | Turn off one kind of hover highlight, for a `hoverable` member set to `false`.                  |

## Group-by bar

The [group-by bar](/docs/react/row-grouping) sits above the tables, outside `.gridkit-data-grid`, so its selectors are unscoped.

| Class                       | Element    | Description                                                                                                                                                                            |
| --------------------------- | ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.gridkit-group-by-bar`     | `<div>`    | The bar. `.is-drag-target` while a chip or a header that can be grouped is dragged — a dashed accent outline — and `.is-drag-blocked` while a header already grouped is dragged at it. |
| `.group-by-bar-placeholder` | `<span>`   | The hint shown while nothing is grouped and a column can be dragged in.                                                                                                                |
| `.group-by-chip`            | `<span>`   | One level of the grouping. States: is-dragging, is-drop-before, is-drop-after; as `.group-by-chip.drag-ghost`, the chip following the pointer.                                         |
| `.group-by-chip-remove`     | `<button>` | The chip's remove button.                                                                                                                                                              |

## Pager

The [pager](/docs/react/pagination#the-built-in-pager) sits below the tables, unscoped like the group-by bar.

| Class                      | Element    | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| -------------------------- | ---------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.gridkit-grid-pager`      | `<div>`    | The pager.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `.grid-pager-bar`          | `<div>`    | First, Previous, the pages or the status, Next and Last, drawn as one connected bar with the radius on its outer corners. Its `--gridkit-pager-digits` (the page count's digits) sizes every page-number slot alike.                                                                                      |
| `.grid-pager-button`       | `<button>` | Every button in the bar. The current page's carries `[aria-current="page"]`, drawn in the accent with a ring.                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `.grid-pager-nav`          | `<button>` | The four arrow buttons, each with `.grid-pager-first`, `.grid-pager-previous`, `.grid-pager-next` or `.grid-pager-last`. Their chevrons mirror right-to-left. One that leads nowhere is `[aria-disabled="true"]`, not `:disabled`, and stays focusable, so its chevron fades and its focus ring does not. |
| `.grid-pager-page`         | `<button>` | A page number, under `"numbered"`, in tabular numerals.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `.grid-pager-ellipsis`     | `<span>`   | The `…` standing for pages left out, under `"numbered"`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `.grid-pager-status-slot`  | `<span>`   | The status segment under the default `"compact"` variant, as wide as its widest text.                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `.grid-pager-status`       | `<span>`   | "Page 2 of 5", inside the status segment.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `.grid-pager-status-sizer` | `<span>`   | The status's widest text, hidden, which holds the segment's width.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `.grid-pager-page-size`    | `<label>`  | The page-size `<select>` beside the bar, followed by its label text in `.grid-pager-page-size-label`, while `pager.sizeOptions` is given.                                                                                                                                                                 |

## Toolbar

The grid's [toolbar](/docs/react/toolbar) is the first thing inside it, above the group-by bar. It sticks to the grid's start edge, so it stays in view while the tables scroll sideways, and keeps its entries on one row — what does not fit moves into "More". States are ARIA attributes, not classes.

| Class                       | Element    | Description                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| --------------------------- | ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.gridkit-toolbar`          | `<div>`    | The toolbar (`role="toolbar"`): its row, padding, surface and bottom border.                                                                                                                 |
| `.toolbar-button`           | `<button>` | A command's button, a dropdown, or "More". `[aria-disabled="true"]` mutes it, `[aria-pressed="true"]` marks a toggle that is on, and `[aria-expanded="true"]` a dropdown whose menu is open. |
| `.toolbar-button-icon`      | `<span>`   | The icon before a button's label; hidden when empty.                                                                                                                                         |
| `.toolbar-button-indicator` | `<span>`   | The chevron after a dropdown's label.                                                                                                                                                        |
| `.toolbar-more`             | `<button>` | The "More" button, holding the entries that do not fit. Also a `.toolbar-button`. Sticks to the toolbar's end edge when the search box and custom entries alone overflow it.                 |
| `.toolbar-search`           | `<input>`  | The search box: `12rem`, or half the toolbar's width when that is less.                                                                                                                      |
| `.toolbar-separator`        | `<div>`    | A separator (`role="separator"`).                                                                                                                                                            |
| `.toolbar-spacer`           | `<div>`    | The free space, pushing what follows it to the far end.                                                                                                                                      |
| `.toolbar-custom`           | `<div>`    | Holds what `renderToolbarItem` draws.                                                                                                                                                        |

A dropdown's menu, and "More"'s, are [menus](#overlays-and-menus) like the context menu's.

## Overlays and menus

The grid's [context menu](/docs/react/context-menu) renders into `document.body`, not inside the grid, so no scrolling ancestor clips it — its selectors are top-level rather than under `.gridkit-data-grid`. States are ARIA attributes, not classes.

| Class                     | Element  | Description                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ------------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.gridkit-overlay`        | `<div>`  | The positioned box around every menu, submenu and panel, `position: fixed` and above the grid. Carries the grid's `.gridkit-light`/`.gridkit-dark`.                                         |
| `.gridkit-menu`           | `<div>`  | A menu (`role="menu"`): its surface, border, shadow and padding.                                                                                                                            |
| `.menu-item`              | `<div>`  | An item. Focused (`:focus`) when the keyboard or the pointer is on it; `[aria-disabled="true"]`, `[aria-checked="true"]` and `[aria-expanded="true"]` (its submenu is open) style the rest. |
| `.menu-item-icon`         | `<span>` | The icon before the label — empty when the item has none, so labels line up; a checked item's check.                                                                                        |
| `.menu-item-label`        | `<span>` | The label.                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `.menu-item-shortcut`     | `<span>` | A key-combination hint after the label.                                                                                                                                                     |
| `.menu-submenu-indicator` | `<span>` | The chevron on an item that opens a submenu.                                                                                                                                                |
| `.menu-separator`         | `<div>`  | A separator (`role="separator"`).                                                                                                                                                           |

Because an overlay sits outside the grid, it takes its colours from the tokens on `:root` — or from `.gridkit-light`/`.gridkit-dark`, which the grid copies onto it from the nearest ancestor that has one (below). A token you override on some other wrapper around the grid does not reach its menus or its column chooser; override it on `:root`, or on `.gridkit-overlay` as well.

### Column chooser

The [column chooser](/docs/react/column-chooser) is an overlay too, in a `.gridkit-overlay` like a menu. Its checkboxes are native, so a disabled one is `:disabled` rather than an ARIA attribute.

| Class                     | Element   | Description                                                                                           |
| ------------------------- | --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.gridkit-column-chooser` | `<div>`   | The chooser (`role="dialog"`): a fixed width, its surface, border, shadow and padding.                |
| `.column-chooser-search`  | `<input>` | The search box.                                                                                       |
| `.column-chooser-option`  | `<label>` | A checkbox and its label — "Show all", or a column. Muted while its checkbox is disabled.             |
| `.column-chooser-all`     | `<label>` | "Show all", set apart from the list below it. Also a `.column-chooser-option`.                        |
| `.column-chooser-list`    | `<ul>`    | The columns, one `<li>` each. Scrolls inside itself past about ten, which does not close the chooser. |
| `.column-chooser-empty`   | `<p>`     | "No matching columns", in place of the list when the search matches none.                             |

### Filter menu

A column's [filter menu](/docs/react/column-filter-menu) is an overlay too. Its buttons and fields are native, so a disabled button is `:disabled`; a sort entry for the direction the column sorts in is `[aria-pressed="true"]`, a value box marked invalid `[aria-invalid="true"]`, and a checklist value `[aria-checked="true"]` while checked. No token names an error colour, so a marked box and its message take `--gridkit-accent` turned red, as light or dark as the accent.

| Class                            | Element               | Description                                                                                                                 |
| -------------------------------- | --------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.gridkit-filter-menu`           | `<div>`               | The menu (`role="dialog"`): a fixed width, its surface, border, shadow and padding.                                         |
| `.filter-menu-form`              | `<form>`              | Everything inside it, in a column. Submitting it applies the editor.                                                        |
| `.filter-menu-sort`              | `<div>`               | The column's sort entries, set apart from what follows. Left out for a column that does not sort.                           |
| `.filter-menu-sort-item`         | `<button>`            | A sort entry, drawn as a menu item.                                                                                         |
| `.filter-menu-sort-icon`         | `<span>`              | The icon before its label — empty for "Clear sort", so labels line up; in accent while pressed.                             |
| `.filter-menu-conditions`        | `<div>`               | The simple editor: its conditions in a column, And/Or between them.                                                         |
| `.filter-menu-custom`            | `<p>`                 | "Custom filter" above either editor, or "Filtered by condition" above the checklist: a filter the editor can't show. Muted. |
| `.filter-menu-condition`         | `<div>`               | One condition (`role="group"`): its operator picker on a line of its own, its value boxes sharing the next.                 |
| `.filter-menu-operator`          | `<select>`            | A condition's operator picker.                                                                                              |
| `.filter-menu-value`             | `<input>`, `<select>` | A value box — a true/false `<select>` on a boolean column; a "Between" has two. Red-bordered while `[aria-invalid="true"]`. |
| `.filter-menu-combinator`        | `<div>`               | And/Or (`role="radiogroup"`), between the two conditions.                                                                   |
| `.filter-menu-combinator-option` | `<label>`             | One of its native radio buttons, with its text.                                                                             |
| `.filter-menu-invalid`           | `<p>`                 | The message under the conditions while one is marked invalid, in red.                                                       |
| `.filter-menu-values`            | `<div>`               | The excel editor: its search box, "Select all" and checklist in a column, with a note above or below when one applies.      |
| `.filter-menu-submenu`           | `<button>`            | "Number filters", opening the column's conditions beside the menu: drawn as a menu item, shaded while its menu is open.     |
| `.filter-menu-submenu-icon`      | `<span>`              | The icon before its label: a tick, in accent, while the column is filtered by conditions; empty otherwise.                  |
| `.filter-menu-submenu-indicator` | `<span>`              | The chevron at the end of its line.                                                                                         |
| `.filter-menu-back`              | `<button>`            | "Back to values", above a condition its menu chose, in place of the checklist: drawn as a menu item.                        |
| `.filter-menu-back-icon`         | `<span>`              | The chevron before its label.                                                                                               |
| `.filter-menu-search`            | `<input>`             | The excel editor's search box.                                                                                              |
| `.filter-menu-select-all`        | `<label>`             | "Select all", a native checkbox and its label, lined up with the checklist's drawn checkboxes.                              |
| `.filter-menu-checklist`         | `<div>`               | The values (`role="listbox"`): a fixed-height box that scrolls inside itself, only its visible values drawn.                |
| `.filter-menu-option`            | `<div>`               | A value (`role="option"`), checked while `[aria-checked="true"]`; a ring while focused by the keyboard.                     |
| `.filter-menu-option-check`      | `<span>`              | Its drawn checkbox: an outline, filled with the accent and ticked while the value is checked.                               |
| `.filter-menu-option-label`      | `<span>`              | Its label, ending in an ellipsis when too long for the menu.                                                                |
| `.filter-menu-option-count`      | `<span>`              | How many rows hold it, under `showCounts`. Muted, at the end of the line.                                                   |
| `.filter-menu-search-first`      | `<p>`                 | "Type to search 12,000 values", in the checklist's box while it waits for a search. Muted.                                  |
| `.filter-menu-more`              | `<p>`                 | "250 more, refine the search" (`role="status"`), under a checklist the value limit cut short. Muted.                        |
| `.filter-menu-actions`           | `<div>`               | The buttons: "Clear filter" at the start, Cancel and OK at the end.                                                         |
| `.filter-menu-clear`             | `<button>`            | "Clear filter".                                                                                                             |
| `.filter-menu-cancel`            | `<button>`            | Cancel.                                                                                                                     |
| `.filter-menu-apply`             | `<button>`            | OK, the form's submit button, tinted.                                                                                       |

## Printing

An `@media print` block makes the browser's own print of the page — <Kbd>Ctrl</Kbd>+<Kbd>P</Kbd>, or <Kbd>Cmd</Kbd>+<Kbd>P</Kbd> on a Mac — read as a plain table. Inside `.gridkit-data-grid-viewport`, it:

- hides the toolbar, the group-by bar, the built-in pager and the resize handles;
- drops a `height` bound and the inner scrolling, so every row the grid has drawn flows onto as many pages as it takes;
- drops the focus ring;
- prints the header's and selected rows' shading as it is (`print-color-adjust: exact`) rather than dropping it to save ink;
- keeps each row whole rather than splitting it across two pages.

It prints only what the grid has drawn: not the rows on another page, nor those a virtualized grid has not mounted. The grid's own [Print](/docs/react/printing) is the supported way to print every row. It prints a separate document in a hidden frame, which sees none of the page's CSS — this stylesheet included — and carries a print stylesheet of its own; restyle it through the `print` option's `styles`, not here.

## Theme tokens

| Token                       | Type    | Description                                                               |
| --------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--gridkit-surface`         | `color` | Header background.                                                        |
| `--gridkit-surface-muted`   | `color` | Hover background.                                                         |
| `--gridkit-line`            | `color` | Borders.                                                                  |
| `--gridkit-hover-line`      | `color` | Cell hover outline, resize edge.                                          |
| `--gridkit-fg`              | `color` | Text.                                                                     |
| `--gridkit-fg-muted`        | `color` | Secondary text and icons.                                                 |
| `--gridkit-accent`          | `color` | Focus rings, drop indicators, and the active sort, group and check marks. |
| `--gridkit-selected`        | `color` | A selected row, column, or cell.                                          |
| `--gridkit-selected-strong` | `color` | A selected row or cell also hovered.                                      |

```css
:root {
  --gridkit-accent: oklch(0.6 0.17 145);
  --gridkit-line: oklch(0.9 0.01 145);
}
```

### Corner radius

`--gridkit-radius` (default `0.25rem`) rounds the grid's outer frame, `.gridkit-data-grid-viewport`, which clips the header and rows to it, and the outer corners of the pager bar. It is not a colour, so it has no light and dark pair: set it on `:root` or on any ancestor of the grid, for example `--gridkit-radius: 0.375rem`, or `0` for square corners.

### Scrollbars

The viewport, the row area, the menus, the column chooser list and the filter checklist show thin scrollbars (`scrollbar-width: thin`) whose thumb is `--gridkit-fg-muted` at 45%, on a transparent track, so they follow light and dark with the other tokens. Engines without `scrollbar-color` get an 8px rounded `::-webkit-scrollbar` equivalent. Only the grid's own elements are styled, never `html` or `body`. To change them, set `scrollbar-width` or `scrollbar-color` on any of those classes.

### Light and dark values

Each token is backed by a raw pair, `--gridkit-<name>-light` and `--gridkit-<name>-dark` — `--gridkit-accent-light`, `--gridkit-accent-dark` and so on — defined once on `:root`. The stylesheet only ever reads `--gridkit-<name>`, and points it at one of the pair: the light one on `:root`, the dark one under `@variant dark`, and whichever `.gridkit-light` or `.gridkit-dark` names on an element that has one.

That reassignment is why an override of `--gridkit-<name>` on `:root` does not reach a grid, or its menus, pinned with `.gridkit-light`/`.gridkit-dark`: the class sets `--gridkit-<name>` again, closer to the grid. To change a colour everywhere, override the raw pair instead:

```css
:root {
  --gridkit-accent-light: oklch(0.6 0.17 145);
  --gridkit-accent-dark: oklch(0.7 0.15 145);
}
```

## Dark mode

GridKit doesn't register its own `dark:` variant — it follows whatever your app's Tailwind build already resolves `dark:` to. Out of the box that's the OS preference. For the common class-toggle pattern, declare it yourself, same as any Tailwind v4 app would:

```css
@import "tailwindcss";
@custom-variant dark (&:where(.dark, .dark *));
@import "@gridkitjs/theme-tailwind/styles.css";
```

```ts
document.documentElement.classList.toggle("dark", isDark);
```

Redefine a token inside `@variant dark { }` to change its dark value too:

```css
:root {
  --gridkit-accent: oklch(0.6 0.17 145);

  @variant dark {
    --gridkit-accent: oklch(0.7 0.15 145);
  }
}
```

## Forcing a theme on one grid

`.gridkit-light` / `.gridkit-dark` pin a grid to one palette regardless of the ambient `dark:` state. Put either on any ancestor of the grid, including the grid's own root; its menus follow, since the grid copies the class onto each overlay it opens. Toggle the app theme below and only the first grid follows it:

<DarkModeExample />

```tsx
<div className="gridkit-dark">
  <DataGrid ... />
</div>
```
